title: fix(import): refuse a STEP closed shell that meshes open, by name
body:
**Stacked on #1574** (#1548, head fd1a1c94): this branch starts from that head, so until #1574 merges the diff below also shows its commits. The commits that belong to this PR are 820529a3 and bda36c6e.

## What changed
- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_closed.rs`. It finds the shells the file declares closed (`CLOSED_SHELL`, and the outer shell a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` names). It also counts unmatched edges: an edge not shared by exactly two facets running opposite ways, with vertices welded by neighbourhood within 1e-6 of the file's length unit, which is truck's `TOLERANCE`.
- `step.rs::shell_facets` now records, for each tessellation pass, the first face truck returned no polygon for. `to_polygon` drops such a face without any error. On the pass that refinement kept:
  - **Closed shell that meshes open: refused.** The message reads `closed shell #id (N faces) meshes open: K unmatched edges, the first from (..) to (..) mm; face #F (i of N) got no mesh from the kernel - ...`.
  - **Face with no mesh: refused in any shell, open or closed.** The message reads `face #F (i of N) in shell #id could not be tessellated: the kernel ... returned no mesh for it - ...`.
- An `OPEN_SHELL` or surface model may still mesh open. Only a dropped face is refused there.
- Downstream checked: the default stock backend accepts an open mesh as a model. Only the SDF backend (`validate_shell`) refuses one. So the importer is the place to catch this.
- Volume shortfall: not reported. The true volume of the B-rep is unknown, and the signed volume of an open mesh means nothing. The message carries the edge count and the first edge's position instead. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/1573-closed-shell-watertight.md`.

## How tested
New suite `crates/app/tests/import_step_closed_shell.rs`:
- `a_closed_shell_that_meshes_open_is_refused_by_name`: `fillet_corner.step` with its blend weights bent to `1E300, 1E-300`. Truck drops the blend. Before this PR the file imported open with no refusal.
- `a_face_the_kernel_cannot_mesh_is_refused_in_an_open_shell_too`: the same bent file, declared `OPEN_SHELL` inside a `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`.
- `every_solid_step_fixture_still_imports`: box, bspline_dome, fillet_corner, Milling-test, Milling-test-inch, sample_ap214, lathe_holder_offset and tool_csys_box_iso13399 all still import.
- Unit tests in `step_closed`: a cube is closed, a cube missing one facet has 3 unmatched edges, and copies within the weld still meet.

**Mutation check** (each refusal disabled in turn, then the suite rerun):
- Closed-shell refusal disabled (`if edges > 0` changed to `if false && edges > 0`): `a_closed_shell_that_meshes_open_is_refused_by_name` FAILS. The import falls through to the dropped-face message.
- Dropped-face refusal deleted: `a_face_the_kernel_cannot_mesh_is_refused_in_an_open_shell_too` FAILS. The file imports.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on bda36c6e: app lib plus the 11 import suites (bore_facet_sagitta, import_step_*, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- A closed shell that meshes open because a face was trimmed wrongly while every face still got a polygon. No fixture for that case is committed. The open-edge count covers it, and the first test shows the count fires on its own: with the dropped-face refusal as a fallback, deleting the closed-shell line changes the message.
- Files with `BREP_WITH_VOIDS` or `ORIENTED_CLOSED_SHELL` voids: only `CLOSED_SHELL` and the `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` outer shell are read as closed.
- The release-lane heavy models.

Changelog: STEP import refuses, by name, a closed shell whose mesh comes out open, and any face the kernel cannot mesh, instead of importing a model with walls missing.
Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(bore): refuse a bore too wide for its ring, and keep it out of Detect holes
body:
## What changed

The Bore op's ride is a centre dive, one radial sweep and one ring on the wall. The dive clears radius `r`; the ring clears the band `[rc - r, rc + r]` (`rc = R - r - leave`). They meet only while `rc <= 2r`, so for holes up to **3 x tool diameter + 2 x stock to leave**. Past that, the ride left a core no pass touches. On a through bore it came loose at the last level (the issue's Ø74.3 bore with a 4 mm tool left a Ø66 disc). Generate still said ok, and so did verify.

- **motion** (`machining2d/bore.rs`): a new door refuses such a hole by name at generate. The message gives the hole's diameter and position, the cutter, the ring radius, the core left and the limit, and points the user at a pocket/adaptive op or a larger tool. `max_bore_diameter()` states the limit once.
- **app** (`operation/bore_reach.rs`, `material.rs`): `detect_holes` on a Bore op keeps only the holes its own tool clears and names each one left out (`DetectedHoles { params, skipped }`). If every hole is too wide, the detection is refused and nothing is stored. Drill and Thread ops are not filtered.
- **MCP**: `detect_holes` now answers `skipped` (one sentence per hole left out), and the tool description says so.
- **GUI**: the Detect holes click stores the same `EditOperationParams` through a `DetectedHoles` queue arm, and the status line names the skipped holes. Undo is unchanged.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/1556-bore-core-door.md`. Refusing was chosen over clearing the floor with more rings (filed as #1566). The limit is 3d from the geometry, not the issue's "about 2d".
- The issue is raised P3 -> P1: a freed core after a clean verify is unsafe output that passes.

## How tested

Pins, each mutation-checked:

- `motion` lib `machining2d::bore_core_tests`:
  - `bore_refuses_a_bore_that_would_leave_a_free_core`: Ø74.3 with a 4 mm tool is refused with "74.300 mm hole", "R35.150", "core from 4.000 to 66.300 mm" and "up to 12.000 mm".
  - `bore_refuses_just_past_the_limit_and_takes_the_limit`: a Ø13 hole (4 mm tool, 0.5 leave) bores and its floor is fully covered; Ø13.02 is refused.
  - `every_bore_the_ride_takes_clears_its_whole_floor`: a point-to-chord coverage law at the floor level over five hole/tool ratios.
  - Mutations: removing the door fails both refusal pins. A stricter limit (`rc - r`) fails the limit pin, the coverage law and `bore_rides_the_wall_circle`. A looser one (`rc - 3r`) fails the limit pin.
- `app` `tests/bore_core.rs` (MCP, on a synthetic 200 x 100 x 10 plate with a Ø74.3 through bore beside a Ø6 hole, 4 mm end mill):
  - `detect_holes_leaves_the_wide_bore_out_of_a_bore_op_and_names_it`: 1 hole stored, `skipped` names the Ø74.3, and the Ø6 bore generates and verifies `ok`.
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_with_only_too_wide_holes_is_refused_by_name`: the refusal stores nothing, and a Drill op on the same plate is not filtered.
  - `a_bore_op_handed_the_wide_bore_by_hand_refuses_at_generate`: a hand-edited list is refused at generate with the numbers, and verify is not ok.
  - Mutations: with no detect filter, all three fail. With no kernel door, the by-hand pin fails and generate answers `ok` (the original bug).
- `ui` lib `detect_holes_note_tests` (GUI parity):
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_stores_the_small_hole_and_names_the_wide_one`: the status line names the skipped hole.
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_with_only_a_wide_hole_is_refused`.
  - Mutation: forcing the plain status fails the first.
- Fixture changes: three motion fixtures bored Ø20 with a 6 mm tool (3.33 d), a ride that left a ring of floor from Ø6 to Ø8 uncut. They now bore Ø16: the unit test `bore_rides_the_wall_circle`, `tests/center_cut_law.rs::a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting_never_plunges_into_a_bore_or_circular` and `tests/level_links.rs::bore_params`. What those tests check is unchanged. No golden and no app fixture held a hole past the limit.
- `tests/thread_boss.rs` reads `.params` from the new return type.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on fce68299: motion 163 s, app 747 s, ui 36 s, 15.8 min wall. An earlier run on e56a4dba failed `center_cut_law` and `level_links`, whose Ø20/6 mm fixtures this law now refuses; they were moved inside the limit.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The user's own STEP (`End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step`) is not in the repo. The synthetic plate reproduces the same shape and the same path.
- No pixel snapshots changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill doc (`.claude/skills/`) is a process file and was not touched, so there is no PROCESS_VERSION bump. The tool description in `mcp/tools.rs` carries the `skipped` field.
- A general "freed piece" law in verify / the stock sim: neither one detects a disconnected piece today. That needs design (some slugs are freed on purpose) and is filed as #1565.

## Follow-ups

- #1565: verify / the stock sim do not detect a freed piece (P8, effort:max).
- #1566: the Bore op could clear wide holes with rings or a spiral instead of refusing them (P7, effort:high).

Changelog: A Bore op refuses, by name, a hole wider than 3 x its tool diameter (+ 2 x stock to leave). Its one ring would leave a free core, which it used to post as ok. Detect holes leaves such holes out of a Bore op and names each one (MCP `skipped`).
Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(import): tessellate three-fillet corner blends instead of refusing them
body:
## What changed

A STEP solid whose rounded edges meet in corner blends now imports closed, instead of being refused by #1546's guard (or, before that, hanging: #1536).

The issue assumed truck cannot subdivide the blends because they are not continuous. They are continuous. I rebuilt the #1536 model from the issue's description with solidcore (two L-shaped halves united, all 30 edges rounded R3.125, written by its step-export): 1 shell, 62 faces, 126 edges, 66 vertices, as the issue lists, and the same refusal on d569372f. Two separate faults were measured on it.

**1. The pole (root cause of the hang and of the refusal).** The corner blend is a rational Bezier patch of degree (4, 2) with one side collapsed to the corner vertex. Every parameter along that side is a pre-image of the vertex. truck finds a boundary point's parameters by Newton iteration; at the pole the free parameter came back as **-1,195,342,517** (knot domain 0..1), which truck accepts because the extrapolated rational surface still passes through the vertex. It then subdivides the bounding box of the boundary's parameters: a billion knot spans of extrapolation, which never meets the tolerance. On the knot domain itself the same subdivision ends in 3 to 5 rounds at every tolerance of the schedule.

- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_pole.rs`. The metered surface (`step_guard`) post-processes truck's parameter searches for B-spline and NURBS faces. An answer inside the knot domain is returned untouched. One outside it is replaced by a parameter inside the domain (the previous boundary point's value for each coordinate that left it, else the nearest bound), but only when the surface there is the searched point (truck's own 1e-6). Anything else is left as truck found it, still bounded by #1546's meter.

**2. The edges (a silent wrong mesh behind the refusal).** With the pole fixed alone, the model imported in 2.4 s with no refusal and was wrong: **13,981 mm3 of 19,549.7**, every planar face missing a corner. The rounded edges are `SURFACE_CURVE`s whose master is `.PCURVE_S1.`; truck rebuilds such an edge as a 2D curve on the neighbouring surface, in its own parametrisation of that surface and between parameters it searches for without a hint.

- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_edge3d.rs`. Before the shells are converted, every `EDGE_CURVE` on a surface curve is pointed at that curve's `curve_3d`. Switching only the master to `.CURVE_3D.` is not enough: for an edge with `same_sense = .F.` truck 0.3.0 inverts the curve twice on that path (pinned below).

No new tessellator: truck's subdivision is kept, so no other B-spline face changes its mesh. The issue's three options and why they were dropped are in `docs/decisions/1548-bspline-corner-blends.md`.

## Readings

Debug build. "Closed" means 0 unmatched edges.

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| #1536 part rebuilt, 62 faces, on d569372f | refused: "face #14010 (NURBS surface, face 19 of 62 ...) did not converge" |
| same, with this PR | 33,073 facets, closed, **19,545.21 mm3** (stated 19,549.71; the 4.5 mm3 is the inscribed mesh's chord error), 1.3 s |
| same, every edge reversed (`same_sense = .F.`), with this PR | identical: 33,073 facets, closed, 19,545.21 mm3 |
| same, face senses turned, with this PR | 33,236 facets, 19,545.21 mm3. Counted with an earlier rounding-based edge count only: it showed 20 edges, in pairs one rounding step apart (the same point either side of a step). Not re-counted with the welding count the test uses. |
| 30 mm cube, all 12 edges R3.125, on d569372f | imported with no refusal at **14,993 mm3** (57% of the closed form 26,286.4) |
| the same cube written with solidcore's opt-in fixes on, with this PR | 15,820 facets, closed, 26,281.69 mm3. (The cube file of the row above was not re-run after the fix.) |
| `fillet_corner.step` (the fixture), with this PR | imports closed, volume inside the test's bound around the closed form 26,816.49 mm3 |
| the fixture, with this PR but without the pole rule | refused: "face #1228 (NURBS surface, face 2 of 10 ...) did not converge" (mutation 1 below) |

The gate's suites over the existing STEP fixtures are green (below).

## How tested

New fixture `testdata/models/fillet_corner.step` (76 KB): the #1536 part's size, a 30 mm cube centred on the origin, with the three edges at (-15, -15, -15) rounded R3.125. Three cylinders and one corner blend; 12 of its 21 edges are surface curves with a pcurve master. Generated with solidcore (recipe below), face senses turned outward.

Mutation checks: each mutation applied, the test seen RED, then restored and seen GREEN.

| Test | Pins | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import_step_corner_blend::a_three_fillet_corner_imports_closed_at_its_volume_within_the_chord_tolerance` | default cap, 120 s hard limit; bounds; 0 unmatched edges; volume short of the closed form by 0 ..= 0.005 mm x curved area; `coarse_mm` is `None` | `settle` not applied in the two metered searches | RED: refused, "face #1228 (NURBS surface, face 2 of 10 in shell #1288) ... did not converge within 25000000 evaluations" |
| same | same | `prefer_3d` not called | RED: 24 unmatched edges |
| `import_step_corner_blend::edges_declared_against_their_curves_import_the_same_closed_solid` | every edge rewritten with its vertices swapped and `same_sense = .F.` imports the same solid | edges left on their surface curve (master switched only) | RED: 74 unmatched edges |
| `step_pole::tests::an_outside_answer_that_is_not_a_pole_is_left_as_truck_found_it` | the only guard in the rule: no replacement unless it is the same point | same-point check removed | RED: `(1.0, 0.9)` instead of `(1.0, 2.0)` (also fails `a_non_finite_answer_ends_cleanly`) |
| `step_pole::tests::a_pole_answer_far_outside_takes_the_previous_boundary_points_parameter` | the -1.2e9 reading goes to the previous point's parameter | hint not carried | RED: `(0.0, 0.0)` instead of `(0.0, 1.0)` |
| `step_pole::tests::{an_answer_inside_the_knot_domain_is_returned_untouched, a_pole_answer_with_no_usable_hint_goes_to_the_nearer_domain_bound, a_surface_without_knots_is_never_touched, a_non_finite_answer_ends_cleanly}` | the rest of the rule | - | - |
| `import_step_corner_blend::bent_corner_blends_end_cleanly_and_bounded` | 10 variants of the blend (zero, negative and 1E300 weights; reversed, zero-length, 1E300 and -1E9 knots; the pole pulled apart): each imports finite facets or is refused, inside 90 s | - (degenerate-input pin) | - |

This PR adds no new refusal. Faces that still cannot be subdivided keep #1546's refusal by name (`import_step_guard`, unchanged and green).

Gate on the final head fd1a1c94 (merged with upstream/main f1de41a5):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 56 s. App lib plus bore_facet_sagitta, import_step_corner_blend, import_step_guard, large_models, model_fidelity, step_budget, step_chord_units, step_fidelity, step_nesting, stock_export: 252 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. (The planner mapped the change to these suites; it did not fall back to batch.)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import`: 26 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- **The user's own `sc_logo.step` was not available.** The readings are on a rebuild of that part with solidcore at the pinned rev 55d0e76 with all opt-in fixes on. The topology counts match the issue, but the writer is not the same: the issue's file has 14 spheres and 20 B-spline surfaces, the rebuild 14 rational patches and 6 surfaces of revolution. Please re-run the #1536 repro on a build of this branch; expected is a closed mesh near 19,545 mm3.
- The rebuilt 62-face model and the full rounded cube are not committed (1 MB and 365 KB); only the one-corner fixture is.
- **A closed shell that meshes open is still not refused.** Three bent variants in the fuzz test import with the blend face dropped (138 facets, open). Filed as #1573 (P1).
- Edge-curve and swept-surface divisions and the parameter searches are still unmetered (#1545; one slow reading added there).
- The GUI import path was not run by hand; it calls the same `parse_with_chord_budget`.
- Release-mode timings were not measured.

<details><summary>Fixture recipe (scratch crate, not committed)</summary>

Dependencies: `solidcore` and `step-export` from `https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore` at rev `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda` (the rev `crates/kernel` pins).

```rust
let mut k = solidcore::Kernel::default();
k.fixes = solidcore::kernel::UpstreamFixes::all();
let mut b = prim::create_box(&mut k, Point3::new(-15.0, -15.0, -15.0), 30.0, 30.0, 30.0)?;
// the three edges with an end at (-15, -15, -15)
let edges: Vec<EdgeId> = /* b.edges() filtered by curve end points */;
fillet_edges(&mut k, &mut b, &edges, 3.125, 1, 1, 1.0)?;
let text = step_export::write(&step_export::brep_to_model(&b)?)?;
```

Then every `ADVANCED_FACE` sense and every `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` orientation is flipped (the writer's senses came out inward), and `FILE_DESCRIPTION` is replaced. The 62-face model is the same with four boxes united into the two L halves and all 30 edges rounded.
</details>

Changelog: STEP import: a solid whose rounded edges meet in corner blends (three-fillet corners) now imports closed at its volume instead of being refused; edges written as surface curves with a pcurve master are read from their 3D curve (#1548)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Builds on #1546, which merged while this was in work; the branch carries a merge of upstream/main f1de41a5.

title: fix(ui): "Pick for WCS" takes viewport picks in the default Model mode
body:
## What changed

Root cause: `wcs_pick::arm` leaves the toolbar's pick mode alone on purpose, because the row takes faces, edges and corners together. But `interact::pick_at` sent a viewport click to `feature_click::click` only when `geo_pick` was Face, Edge or Vertex, and `update_hover` had the same gate. The default mode is Model, and the only control that changes it is on an operation's Geometry page. So from a fresh project every click selected the whole model and the armed draft never received a pick. `feature_click::ask` and `click` already handled the armed row; they were just never reached.

Fix: a new predicate, `interact::feature_routed`, is true in a feature mode or while `wcs_pick::collecting`. Both the click and the hover route on it. Disarmed or paused, the mode's own click behaviour is back. Apply is unchanged: it still queues the undoable `SetWcs`, whose MCP tool is untouched. A tilted frame is still placed, and generation still refuses it by name (#1518). The other setup drafts (plane, points, axis, locate, boundary) switch the mode when armed, so they did not have this gap.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1562-wcs-pick-route.md` (route on the draft's state rather than switching the mode and restoring it on every exit path).

## How tested

- Pinning test: `egui_app::wcs_pick_click_tests::an_armed_row_takes_viewport_picks_from_the_default_model_mode` (ui lib). From a fresh project (mode Model, no operation open) it arms the row through its button, checks the hover names the top face, and drives a face (Z), an edge (X) and a corner (Origin) through `interact::pick_at`, never through `wcs_pick::take`. It checks that no whole-model Select is queued and that the "Picked:" line shows. It then clicks Apply, checks the WCS lands on the corner, and checks that a click after the draft ends is a whole-model select again.
- Mutation check: I removed `|| crate::wcs_pick::collecting(state)` from `feature_routed`, and the test failed at the hover assert (line 83). I then reverted only the click routing in `pick_at` (keeping the hover), and it failed at the Z-pick assert (line 87). Both were restored.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (ui lib + boundary, boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, operations, sinker_setup, theme_files; 59 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The existing `wcs_pick_tests` and `wcs_pick::tests` pass unchanged.

## Not exercised

- **A GUI hand check by the maintainer is owed**: real mouse clicks and the drawn hover highlight in the live viewport (the test covers the hover state, not the pixels).
- No structural assertions changed: the row's labels and widgets are the same. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- `interact.rs` was already over 400 lines before this change (1794); this PR adds 12.

Changelog: "Pick for WCS" on the Setups page now takes face, edge and corner picks from the viewport in the default pick mode, and the hover highlights them (#1562)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(circular): judge a whole-model Circular against the finished part
body:
## What changed

A Circular whose source is the finished part (a whole model, `SrcRef::Entity` with `part_solid` true) is now judged against that part. `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`) gave every Circular `DepthLaw::None`, so a circle typed through the part's wall generated with no warning on the operation. It now takes `DepthLaw::Section` (the section and solid laws Contour, Face and the picked pockets answer to) through one shared function:

```rust
pub(super) fn authored_law(src: &SrcRef) -> DepthLaw  // Entity -> Section; Stock, Selection -> None
```

It is written for every kind that cuts geometry typed by hand (Circular's centre and radius here; the Slot's endpoints and width in #1537, where SKULL can call it; coordination comment on #1537). It runs after `depth_law_of`'s `part_solid` early return, so a Stock source (or an entity that is the setup's stock) still cuts unjudged. A picked Circular keeps its law (`None`).

**Root cause / readings.** The old contract said "the source is the material to remove, not a part to keep", which holds only for a Stock source. On main, in the readings taken (radius-12 circle in a radius-10 through hole, 6 mm end mill, 0.5 left), the operation carried **0 warnings** (status ok, no MCP `verify` finding on the op). The post was held only by the program-level stock sim (`post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 719 cell(s), worst 8.00 mm`). Now the operation itself carries blocking `Warning::Gouge`s on the moves that enter the wall (1028 over MCP), `held_by: ["C1"]`.

## How tested (each pin mutation-checked)

New `crates/app/tests/circular_entity_law.rs`:
- `a_whole_model_circle_typed_through_the_hole_wall_is_a_gouge_and_never_posts`: Entity source, gouge on the op, `posting::post_setup` refuses with "post blocked", no file written.
- `a_whole_model_circle_inside_the_modeled_hole_stays_clean`: radius 10, no gouge, and the path equals the Stock source's move for move (judging never moves the tool).
- `a_stock_source_still_cuts_the_typed_circle_unjudged`: the radius-12 circle on Stock carries no gouge.
- `over_mcp_the_whole_model_circle_is_judged_the_same`: import_model / set_stock from_model / add_operation Circular on "part" / generate / verify: the op's own blocking gouge findings, `ok` false, `held_by` C1; the legal circle verifies `ok` true.

New in-crate `operation::authored_law_tests` (the law table): Entity -> Section, picked Circular -> None, Stock / stock entity (`part_solid` false) -> None, `authored_law` alone.

Mutations (each reverted after):
- M1 Circular arm back to `DepthLaw::None`: the wall test, the MCP test and `a_whole_model_circular_is_judged_against_the_part` fail.
- M2 `authored_law` judges picks (`Selection -> Section`): `a_picked_circular_keeps_its_law` and `the_shared_authored_law_reads_the_source_alone` fail.
- M3 `part_solid` early return dropped and Stock judged: `a_stock_source_still_cuts_the_typed_circle_unjudged` and both table tests fail.
- M4 `Entity -> Contain`: the table tests fail (the integration wall test also passes under Contain, which convicts the wall too; the decision file says why Section).

title: feat(ops): one machining-frame seam - OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame
body:
Replaces PR 768 (jenhaert's commits kept as they are, plus one merge of main; the fork refused a maintainer push)

## What changed

Phase 1 of #763: **`OpFrame`** — the one machining-frame seam in
`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` — composes the two existing frame
mechanisms (the setup's `part_alignment` from #326 and the op's 3+2
`Tilt` from M5.1 B) behind one door, and `collect_job` reads through it:

- `OpFrame::of(op)` built once per generation; material and heights
  resolve through it; the tilt frame comes from
  `OpFrame::checked_frame` — one construction site, the refusal keeping
  its exact words and its exact precedence (after the heights resolve,
  the job's error-order law).
- The contract is stated once in the module header: D / S / L frames,
  right-to-left composition `p_L = T(A(p_D))`, the CL wrapping back via
  `TiltedFrame::world_path` (identity clone without a tilt), and the
  furniture law (stock / WCS / fixtures live in S: never aligned, but
  read local by the tilt).
- Heights and bounds in L ship correct from day one
  (`aabb_local_of`, `height_z_local`): they resolve against FULLY
  TRANSFORMED geometry, never a `z − origin.z` shift of the S box —
  the shift is only correct while the tool axis is the world Z.

**No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.** The four
verified kinds, picks, area controls and tilt-in-aligned-setups keep
their refusals; the later phases lift them one by one, each with its
numeric pin.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` (8 tests) + the seam's inline
  unit tests (6): identity passthrough; zero-tilt index reproduces the
  prismatic path EXACTLY move-for-move (the identity-bits law); a
  tilted face runs in its own plane (every endpoint maps back into the
  L1-folded height band over the local silhouette, tool axis =
  hand-computed Rx(45)); 90-degree alignment turns the solid and its
  TopOfModel height (15, not 10); 180-degree alignment mirrors the
  facets by hand math; alignment × tilt composition pinned against
  hand-composed transforms; local heights/boxes read fully transformed
  geometry (and provably NOT the z-shift); picks stay refused by name
  while the door Phase 2 will read through is already aligned.
- Capability gates: unchanged by design; the tilted-move refusal keeps
  its existing verbatim pin in `tests/inverted_post.rs`.
- The four kinds' aligned generation keeps its pins in the #326 suites
  (`plane_align`, `axis_align`, `rest_across_setups`, …), run by the
  same gate.

## What was not exercised

- The L-frame height/AABB resolve methods are pinned by tests only —
  no production call site switches onto them until Phase 2+ lifts the
  matching refusals (deliberate: the seam lands behavior-identical).
- The boundary/region builders (`boundary_ctx`, `material_region`,
  `boundary_picks`) still build their own frames from `op.params.tilt()`
  — they move onto the seam in the later phases.



Changelog: feat: one machining-frame seam (OpFrame) composing part_alignment and TiltedFrame behind a single door; generation reads through it byte-identically (#763, PR)

## The merge of main (one commit, 302d81ac0)

Only `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` conflicted. Main's #904 `judged_material` (material excess also covers the setup stock) and #1510 tilt refusal met the branch's `OpFrame::material_of`:
- `frame.rs`: `OpFrame::material_of` now delegates to `material::judged_material`, so the seam is the one door and the verdict reads the same material, excess and stock as main. Doc comment updated.
- `job.rs` `collect_job`: kept main's `setup_wcs_tilt::generation_problem` refusal, then `OpFrame::of(op)` and `opframe.material_of`; the branch's `resolve_heights` / `checked_frame` calls kept.
- No test removed from either side; no golden or snapshot touched.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: app suites ok (988 s), ui suites ok (153 s), 0 failed. The run covered `opframe_seam`, `coarse_laws`, `tool_body_judged`, `wcs_tilt`.

title: fix(slot): judge a whole-part Slot by the part's depth law
body:
**Stacked on #1522** (branched from its head f35bd14e, because #1522 changes `depth_law_of`'s Slot arm). Until #1522 merges, this PR's diff includes #1522's commits; this PR's own change is the last two commits (526fff3c, b8653f25).

## What changed

Root cause: `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`) gave a Slot `DepthLaw::Section` only when its source was a Selection (#1522). A Slot whose source is the whole finished part (`SrcRef::Entity("part")`, `part_solid` true) fell to `_ => DepthLaw::None`, so a typed slot through the part's wall generated and posted with no gouge warning.

Fix: every Slot takes `DepthLaw::Section` when `part_solid` holds (picked or whole model). A Stock source, or an entity that is the stock, is not part-solid (`part_solid_of`), so it is still cut unjudged. No existing law weakened; the pocket-family Selection arm is unchanged. Decision record: `docs/decisions/1537-slot-entity-law.md`.

Circular has the same gap; left out to keep this P1 minimal, filed as #1543.

## Changed pin

`with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` (`crates/app/tests/slot_picks.rs`) asserted that an Entity("part") slot through the pocket wall gets **no** Gouge. That was the unsafe behaviour #1537 reports (#1504's maintainer expectation: "the model gouge check still decides"). It now covers only the Stock source (still cut as typed, unjudged); the Entity case moved to the new test below.

## How tested

- New pinning test `a_whole_part_slot_through_the_wall_is_convicted_and_holds_the_post`: Entity("part") slot (-20,0)-(20,0) w12 through the 30x16 pocket's walls -> blocking `Warning::Gouge`; plus an Entity("part") slot inside the pocket verifies clean (over-conviction guard).
- Mutation check: deleting the line `OpParams::Slot { .. } => DepthLaw::Section,` -> the new test RED (and #1522's `a_slot_through_the_pocket_wall_is_refused_and_one_below_the_floor_holds_the_post` RED, since the arm now carries the picked case too); restored -> 8/8 GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion 337 s, app 1189 s, ui 208 s; 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

Real-world whole-model slot projects beyond the test fixture; Circular (#1543).

title: fix(sim): cut the stock along the travelled part of the move in flight during playback
body:
## What changed

During playback, the simulator's stock is now cut along the move under the playhead, up to where the tool is drawn. Before this change it was cut only once each G1/G2 move had finished. This is display only: the kept stock, its checkpoints, every verdict (gouge, collision, rapid-in-stock) and what blocks the post are still cut by whole moves, exactly as before.

- `camcraft-sim`: a new module, `stock_sim/partial.rs`.
  - `partial_move` gives the travelled part of a move (lines and arcs). It uses the same `sim::point_along` that places the drawn tool, which this PR factors out of `at_seg`.
  - `Stock::with_partial` cuts that part on a copy and returns the bricks it changed.
  - `Script::travelled(t)` gives the playhead's fraction along the segment under it.
- `camcraft-app`:
  - `FieldPlay::seek_to(k, frac)` shows move `k` cut as far as `frac` on a copy of the completed-move stock. `seek_to(k + 1, 0.0)` is bit-identical to `seek(k + 1)`.
  - `PlayIndex::position_at` gives no fraction on a connector rapid, past an op's last move or at the end.
  - The playback worker has `request_at(k, frac)`, and `PlayFrame.frac`.
  - The bricks of a partial cut ride the frame's patch and are re-sent once after it moves on.
  - `Progress` and `progress` moved unchanged into `stock_play_head.rs` (400-line law).
- `camcraft-ui`: `follow_playhead` passes the fraction.
- Rotary and turning ops still show whole moves; the reason is in the decision file.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1516-sim-partial-move-cut.md`.

**Frame cost:** this cost only applies when the playhead's fraction changes. It is one `Stock` clone (the cut layers; the mesh layer is shared) plus one sub-move sweep on the playback worker, then the existing view clone and pack. A paused playhead costs nothing new.

## How tested

- `camcraft-sim` lib, `stock_sim::partial`:
  - `mid_line_stock_is_the_sweep_of_the_travelled_part`
  - `mid_arc_stock_is_the_sweep_of_the_travelled_part`
  - `degenerate_moves_and_fractions_cut_nothing`
  - `the_playhead_fraction_follows_the_drawn_tool`
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play_partial`:
  - `the_move_in_flight_cuts_as_far_as_the_tool_travelled`: the end of the move is bit-equal to the plain seek; scrubbing back restores the start; a NaN fraction cuts nothing.
  - `the_playhead_fraction_applies_only_to_a_move_in_flight`
  - `the_worker_publishes_the_move_in_flight`
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play` still passes: 7 tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green on 9bd9fcbd8 (sim, motion, app, ui suites; 9.5 min wall).

## Not exercised

- Nothing was looked at in the GUI. The worker agent cannot launch the app, so the live playback picture needs a hand test.
- No partial cut for rotary or turning ops; they still cut whole moves.

Changelog: Simulation playback removes material along a move as the tool travels, not only when each G1/G2 move ends

title: fix(fixtures): a flipped setup's fixtures are judged against the carried stock's shape, not its box
body:
Branched from upstream main.

## What changed

The check for fixtures in a carried setup (`app::fixture_carried`) used to judge each fixture by its world bounding box. A vise's box spans the opening between its jaws. A soft-jaw nest pocket sits inside the jaws' box. So a part clamped between the jaws, or seated in the nest, was reported as "standing inside the stock carried from Setup 1", and the post was refused (#1530: 4.48 mm and 11.43 mm deep).

- **Box first, then mesh.** The box is still the first check. When it flags a fixture, the fixture's closed world mesh is then read column by column against the carried stock. For each column it takes the Z spans the mesh puts on the column's vertical line and compares them with the column's material.
  - The line reading is the new `FixtureMesh::steel_on_line` in `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/column.rs`.
  - It uses signed crossings with the same nonzero/odd-parity rule as the existing point-in-solid test.
  - Touching or overlapping shells merge into one span.
  - An ambiguous line (one through a facet edge, or one lying in a wall face) is nudged by one millionth of the mesh's scale, capped at 0.1 micron a step, and read again.
  - A line whose winding goes negative or does not close at zero (an inside-out shell over another) is not read: the box stands.
- **Between the columns, read whole (review rework).** Every rectangle spanned by four neighbouring material columns, trimmed by the contact tolerance, is judged against the material the four share by the new `FixtureMesh::steel_in_prism` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/prism.rs`). Facets clipped to the rectangle that reach into the material slab convict. With no facet over the rectangle, there is no steel there. Otherwise the slab holds no surface, and one line decides whether it is all steel or all air. Nothing inside the material is sampled, so a post or a lip narrower than the pitch is refused. Where the four columns disagree (a side face or a step runs through), only what they share is judged: a boundary is known to one pitch, as with the box law.
- **Contact tolerance.** A column is refused only when the overlap is more than `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL` (0.01 mm). That must hold on the centre line and on four lines 0.01 mm beside it, so a face that lies exactly on a column centre counts as contact.
- **The mesh can only clear a fixture, never add a hit.** In these cases the box depth stands, as before:
  - an open or refused mesh;
  - a coarse-fidelity fixture (#864);
  - a line that no nudge can read, or that winds inconsistently;
  - a rectangle between the columns that cannot be read;
  - a spent facet-visit budget (`MESH_VISIT_BUDGET`, 50 M visits per fixture, logged when it runs out);
  - a footprint narrower than one grid cell.
- **Bounded time.** A column or rectangle whose box depth cannot exceed the worst depth already found is skipped. A fixture that really penetrates therefore stops after its first refused column.
- **Refusal text.** A fixture that really enters the carried material is still refused by name with its depth, in the same message as before.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1530-carried-fixture-shape.md`.

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_shape.rs`:
- **Setup.** A 50 x 50 x 10 part in 56 x 56 stock. Setup 1 contours its sides down to Z 4, leaving a 3 mm brim (the hat). Setup 2 flips it over X (AlignPartToSetup FlipX) and faces the brim side. In Setup 2 the section stands at Z 0..6 and the brim at Z 6..10.
- **Pins.** Each also checks that the post gate reports the same lines:
  - `the_flipped_hat_enters_setup2_section_down_brim_up`: the fixture geometry is real, and the grid pitch is under 0.5 mm.
  - `a_builtin_vise_gripping_the_flipped_parts_sides_is_held`: built-in 5 in vise, jaws 5 mm high, faces at Y ±25, floor at Z 0. Accepted.
  - `a_vise_jaw_moved_into_the_part_is_refused_by_name_with_its_depth`: opening 48. Refused, `5.00 mm deep`.
  - `soft_jaws_whose_nest_clears_the_part_are_held`: one-piece soft jaws (5 shells) whose pocket clears the part by 0.05 mm. Accepted.
  - `soft_jaws_with_a_nest_too_small_are_refused_by_name_with_the_depth`: pocket 0.5 mm too small on each side. Refused, `fixture 'Soft jaws' ... setup 'Setup1' ... 5.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_a_hair_past_the_contact_tolerance_is_refused`: nest floor 0.03 mm into the part, 0.02 mm past the tolerance. Refused, `0.03 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_touching_within_the_contact_tolerance_is_held`: floor 0.005 mm into the part. Accepted.
  - `a_post_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 0.19 post, 3 mm in, on no column line. Refused, `3.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_lip_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 48 lip, 4 mm in. Refused, `4.00 mm deep`.
  - `an_open_mesh_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest with one facet removed. Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).
  - `a_coarse_fidelity_fixture_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest flagged coarse (#864). Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_guards.rs` calls `mesh_penetration` on hand-built carried bodies, so each guard is reached on its own:
- `an_unread_column_line_keeps_the_box_depth` (budget 0 gives the box depth)
- `an_inside_out_shell_between_the_columns_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_post_between_the_column_lines_is_steel`
- `a_fixture_narrower_than_a_cell_off_the_lines_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_face_on_a_column_centre_where_the_material_ends_is_contact`

New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_column.rs` tests `steel_on_line` directly:
- block span / miss
- a line on a facet diagonal is nudged and read
- nest pocket vs wall, with touching shells merged
- a line in a wall face is still read
- a spent budget reads nothing
- non-finite input is not read
- an inside-out shell over another is not read as air (the review's A 0..10 / B 5..15 reversed)
- a 6 micron block at X 5000 is read where it stands (capped nudge)
- a budget cut mid-line never reads part of a line
- `steel_in_prism`: a post no line meets is steel; a box wholly inside steel is steel; contact band; budget, NaN and inverted input are unread

The existing `carried_fixtures_cache.rs` passes unchanged, including the sub-cell dowel-pin pin.

### Mutation checks
The full table (the review's M1-M10 plus the rework's guards) is in the PR comment for head 87f657fa. Every guard is red under its mutation except two: M5 (centre line only) is stricter, not looser, and G2 (the winding must close at zero) is a defensive guard that only a partial reading reaches, and the budget guard pinned by M4 already catches that.

### Performance (release, M-series Mac, re-measured after the rework)
- Pins: `carried_fixture_shape` 0.52 s debug for all 11. `carried_fixture_guards` under 0.01 s.
- A 400 k-facet fixture: a 100 k-segment cylinder whose cap fans every line and rectangle near the centre meets.
  - With no limit: 16.6 s if the mesh clears it, 19.4 s if it penetrates. Reading the rectangles costs more than the lines alone (3.6 s before the rework).
  - With the 50 M-visit budget: both stop at 0.34 s and keep the box verdict, logged.

## Gates
On head 87f657fa (merges cleanly with upstream main):
- App, all green: lib 194; carried_fixture_shape 11; carried_fixture_guards 5; carried_fixtures_cache 7; accessory_collisions 2; builtin_vise 9; fixture_* (keys_lenient, law_gaps, library, locate, locate_stock, mesh, mesh_posed, plate, plate_detect, plate_followups, plate_riders, route, ux); fixtures 14; posting 17; setup_carry 9; verify 21; verify_arc_reading 7.
- Sim, all green: lib 146; fixture_mesh_column 12; fixture_mesh_convict 5; fixture_mesh_posed 9 (1 ignored); posed_band_cylinder 3.
- Clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-app --all-targets` clean. `-p camcraft-sim` lib and fixture_mesh_column clean. The sim `--all-targets` run stops on a lint already on main in `fixture_mesh_convict.rs`, a file this PR does not touch.

## Not exercised
- The MCP `add_builtin_vise` replay of the user's h5 project; the pins rebuild the same geometry headlessly.
- A real STEP soft-jaw import.
- Inside the material nothing is sampled. At a side face or a step, contact is resolved to the carried grid's pitch, as with the box law: steel within one cell of the face, short of the next column centre, can pass. This is pinned and stated in the decision record.
- A rotated (not flipped) setup is not pinned. The frame code is shared with the box.
- Seen while building the pins and not followed up: in 60 x 60 stock, a 15.24 mm contour around a 50 x 50 part left the stock's outer corners (about 1.5 mm triangles) at full height in the carried body. The pins use 56 x 56 stock. This may need its own issue.

Changelog: A flipped (carried) setup's fixtures are judged by their real shape against the stock carried from the earlier setup, so a vise gripping the part's sides or soft jaws with a nest are no longer refused; steel truly inside the carried part is still refused with its depth.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1530

title: fix(import): refuse a STEP face whose tessellation never converges
body:
## What changed

truck's surface subdivision (`sub_parameter_division`) recurses forever on a B-spline or NURBS face that is not continuous: one seam stays "far" at every depth. The recursion runs inside a rayon task that nothing can interrupt, and it produces no facet, so the facet budget never fires. That is the #1536 hang.

- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_guard.rs`. Each face's surface is wrapped in `Metered`, which counts the points truck evaluates on the face in one tessellation pass.
  - B-spline and NURBS faces are divided by truck's own generic `algo::surface::parameter_division`, called on the wrapper. Their own impls run exactly this algorithm, so the division and the mesh are identical. Other surface kinds keep their specialised division.
  - Past `FACE_EVAL_CAP` (25 M) evaluations, the wrapper returns one fixed point, so the subdivision stops within one sweep. It also returns the bare range as the division, so truck does not triangulate the runaway grid.
- `step.rs`: `shell_facets` builds the guarded shell, resets the meters on each pass, and reads them before a held panic is re-raised. A tripped face refuses the import by name, for example: `corrupt STEP: face #53 (B-spline surface, face 6 of 6 in shell #17) could not be tessellated: its surface subdivision did not converge within 25000000 evaluations (a discontinuous or degenerate surface) - re-export the model, or import an STL`.
- No thread is spawned, and nothing outlives the call. A worker thread with a deadline was rejected: a stranded thread keeps a core busy and its memory grows. Truck itself is not patched. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/1536-step-tess-guard.md`.

## How tested

New fixtures, built by hand from `box.step`:
- `testdata/models/bspline_discontinuous.step`: the top face is a degree-1 B-spline whose interior knot is repeated, so it jumps 0.25 at u = 0.5. Unguarded, `parameter_division` on it was confirmed still running after 30 s, in both debug and release.
- `testdata/models/bspline_dome.step`: the top face is a smooth biquadratic dome.

Pins, each mutation-checked (each mutation applied, the test seen failing, then reverted):

| Test | Pins | Mutation that fails it |
|---|---|---|
| `import_step_guard::a_face_that_never_converges_is_refused_by_name_within_the_budget` | default cap; refused by name in 4.5 s (debug) under a 120 s hard limit | no fixed-point short-circuit (times out); no entity names (`face_entities` mismatch) |
| `import_step_guard::a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` | the refusal names the face and the cap | same two |
| `import_step_guard::a_smooth_bspline_face_still_imports_closed_at_its_volume` | a B-spline face still imports: volume 1 + 0.2/9, crown at 1.05 | - (regression pin) |
| `import_step_guard::degenerate_bspline_variants_end_cleanly_and_bounded` | 7 bent knot/multiplicity variants each import or refuse, bounded | no short-circuit (times out) |
| `step_guard::tests::a_smooth_bspline_divides_exactly_as_truck_does_and_does_not_trip` | the division is identical to truck's own at 3 tolerances | tolerance scaled in the wrapper's division |
| `step_guard::tests::a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` | bounded division, empty grid on a trip | the empty-division return removed |
| `step_guard::tests::nothing_keeps_running_after_a_refused_pass` | no work left running after the call | the tessellation moved to a detached thread (option (c) shape) |
| `step_guard::tests::the_refusal_names_the_face_its_kind_and_the_cap` | the refusal text | - |

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green in 24 s (app lib plus bore_facet_sagitta, import_step_guard, large_models, model_fidelity, step_budget, step_chord_units, step_fidelity, step_nesting, stock_export). `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import`: 26 passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

Cap measured in release: a 400 mm doubly curved bicubic patch at the 0.0025 mm chord cap needs 1.5 M evaluations (a 475 x 475 grid). The discontinuous face reaches 25 M in about 1.7 s.

## Not exercised

title: fix(ui): show the one radial-step field each pocket strategy reads
body:
## What changed

The report: Stepover from 3 mm to 25 mm left the path unchanged. The path was correct. Adaptive and Offset rings step by **Optimal load** (`load_step(D, optimal_load)`) and never read Stepover. Zigzag, Waterline and Auto space their rows by Stepover. The Passes tab showed both fields for every strategy, so one of them was always dead.

- `PocketStrategy::steps_by_load()` (motion) names the load strategies. `tiling_step` in the 2D and 3D pocket params now uses it, and so does every page guard. One predicate covers both the generator and the page.
- **Passes tab** (Pocket, 3D Pocket, Rotary offset, Multi-axis rough): Stepover shows only for Zigzag, Waterline and Auto. Optimal load shows only for Adaptive and Offset rings. The 2D Adaptive kind no longer shows Stepover; 2D Offset keeps it.
- Every Optimal load field has a hint: "this load sets the step between passes - Stepover is not used here (it spaces Zigzag, Waterline and Auto)".
- **Leads tab, Engagement**: a hint says it changes the entry feeds only, and that the side load of the passes is Stepover or Optimal load on Passes. This answers the "which is actually winning" question.
- **Trochoid**: a hint says Forward step is the most a loop advances, and that the loops shorten where Max engagement would be exceeded.
- **3D validate**: a stepover wider than the tool is refused only for strategies that read it. Before, a stale value refused a legal Adaptive job. A stepover of zero or less is still refused for every strategy.
- **2D past-reach refusal** now names the field ("stepover" / "optimal-load step") and both values.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1512-stepover-load.md` (hide the inert field rather than make Adaptive read Stepover; Engagement group name kept).

No change to posted G-code, goldens, the project file or commands. MCP: no new command; the parameters were already settable.

## How tested

- New `crates/motion/tests/radial_step.rs`:
  - `zigzag_rows_follow_the_stepover`

  - `load_strategies_step_by_the_load_not_the_stepover`: Offset rings with stepover 3 vs 25 gives identical moves; load 0.10 vs 0.30 differs
  - `adaptive_clearing_never_reads_the_stepover`

title: fix(heights): model-referenced heights read the setup's parts, never its fixtures
body:
## What changed

`Top of Model` / `Bottom of Model` resolved through `setup_align::solid_aabb_in`, which walks every `model::model_entities` entry - built-in vises, accessories (soft jaws, plates, chucks) and tagged STEP/mesh fixtures of any setup included. With a vise under the part, a default 2D Contour ran down to the vise base (about 100 mm below the part) and generate reported ok; only verify/post caught it.

- New `setup_align::part_aabb_in(world, setup)`: the bounds of every model that is not a fixture (`FixtureDef`), in the asking setup's frame (the #326 alignment still applies). `solid_aabb_in` now shares its body through a private `models_aabb_in` filter and is unchanged in behaviour.
- `operation/heights.rs`: `TopOfModel` / `BottomOfModel` and their `missing_source` diagnostic read `part_aabb_in`. These are the only references read from model bounds (stock, work offset and selection read their own sources). The op stamp reads the resolved Z via `resolve_height`, so it follows automatically.
- Not changed: `model::is_model`, `solid_aabb_in`, the fixture/collision laws. Verify still strikes a pass into the vise.
- Setup scoping: parts are document-wide (a setup holds the same parts in its own frame) and only fixtures bind to a setup, so leaving every fixture out means a vise in Setup 2 cannot move Setup 1's heights. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1529-heights-exclude-fixtures.md`, along with why the semantics stay "all parts" rather than "the op's source", and why the #1094 stock-only skip was left out.

## Pins (`crates/app/tests/heights_fixtures.rs`)

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `a_vise_under_the_part_leaves_bottom_of_model_at_the_part_and_the_path_unchanged` | 50 x 50 x 6 block (Z 4..10) plus a 5 in vise with jaw tops at Z 2: refs = (10, 4); the path signature and lowest Z are the same as without the vise |
| `a_vise_fitted_to_the_stock_leaves_top_of_model_at_the_part_not_the_jaw_tops` | vise `FitStock`, jaws above the part: Top of Model = 10, not the jaw tops |
| `a_vise_declared_in_setup_two_does_not_move_setup_ones_heights` | vise in Setup2: refs equal the part's in None/Setup1/Setup2; the contour path is the bare one |
| `a_soft_jaw_a_plate_and_a_tagged_mesh_fixture_are_not_the_model` | soft jaw accessory, 300 x 300 dowel plate, and two imported meshes tagged as fixtures (one under, one over the part): refs = (10, 4) |
| `the_collision_check_still_sees_the_vise` | a contour taken 3 mm under the part (Z 1, below the jaw tops) still gets `Op: ... strikes a fixture` from `posting::verification_gate` |

**Mutation checks**
- Revert the filter (`part_aabb_in` keeps every model): all 5 red. Restored: all 5 green.
- Blind the collision side (`fixture::tagged` returns nothing): only `the_collision_check_still_sees_the_vise` is red, the 4 height pins stay green. Restored: green. So the heights filter and the collision set are pinned independently.

title: fix(setup): a post option changed on one setup never changes another's program
body:
**stacked on #1527 - review only the commits after 8d5cbe8b; merge #1527 first.**

## What changed

Root cause: `State::route_post_options` (`crates/ui/src/state_setup_post_options.rs`) routed by `post_options_owner()` only - own-or-document, the pre-#1515 machine law. With two setups following the document's post options, an edit on Setup2's Post page wrote the DOCUMENT's options (`SetPostOptions`), which Setup1 also posts with: e.g. "Skip pauses and homes" on Setup2 silently dropped Setup1's optional stops and trips home (wrong posted G-code).

- `crates/ui/src/state_setup_post_options.rs`: new `State::post_options_target` = the owner, else #1515's `shared_mount_target` (the active setup when the document has two or more setups). Every option arm (Skip pauses and homes, Output, Threading, End units) routes through it: with 2+ setups the edit becomes that setup's own options via the existing undoable `SetSetupPostOptions`; with no setups or one, the document's, unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/state_setup_mount.rs`: `shared_mount_target` made `pub(super)` (one rule for machine, post and post options).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_post_page.rs`: under the options' own/document radios the page says where an edit lands - "A post option changed on this page is Setup2's own - no other setup changes." or "... sets the document's post options - every setup without its own uses them." (`options_target_line`, matching #1527's `target_line`).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1526-setup-own-post-options-edit.md`. Accepted consequence: Output and Threading are program-level, so changing Output on Setup2 alone now makes the whole-program post refuse by name (`program_problems`, "post the setups one at a time") instead of silently switching Setup1 too.

MCP: the server has no post-options tool at all (nothing in `crates/app/src/mcp/` names `PostOptions`), so no MCP bleed; missing parity filed as #1534 (P5, `MCP:`).

## How tested

New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_post_options_bleed.rs`:
- `an_option_changed_on_setup2_leaves_setup1s_posted_options` - document skips pauses, Setup2 turns it off: Setup1's resolved options (`setup_post_options::of`) and the document's still skip, Setup2 reads its own change, status names Setup2; undo/redo walk both.
- `output_and_options_on_setup2_never_reach_setup1` - Output and the generic `SetPostOptions` (End units) on Setup2; Setup1 and the document untouched; two undos restore.
- `with_one_setup_an_option_still_sets_the_documents` - single setup unchanged.
- `the_setup2_post_page_says_and_does_its_own_options` - real page: AccessKit label names Setup2's own; clicking "Skip pauses and homes" leaves Setup1 alone.
- `the_only_setups_post_page_names_the_documents_options` - AccessKit label names the document's options.
- Updated `setup_post_options::the_option_switches_land_on_the_active_setups_own_options`: its "Setup1 active edits the document's" step asserted the bleed; it now asserts Setup1's own.

Mutations (each reverted): routing back to `post_options_owner` -> 4 fail; target always the active setup (single setup binds own) -> 3 fail; page line always "own" -> 1 fails; page line removed -> 2 fail; `SetSetupPostOptions::invert` a no-op -> 3 undo pins fail.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (includes #1527's commits): green - ui lib + 10 ui suites, 0.4 min. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a GUI hand check; actual posted G-code with two setups' ops (pinned on the resolved options each setup posts with); release-lane pixel snapshots (no PNG changed; the setup Post page gains one text line, which may move a release-lane golden at the cut).

Follow-ups: #1534 (MCP post options tool).

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (stack base #1527 branches from upstream/main fd2f4f30).

Changelog: With two or more setups, a post option (skip pauses and homes, output, threading, end units) changed on one setup's Post page becomes that setup's own and no longer changes another setup's posted program; the page says where an edit lands (#1526)

title: fix(ui): operation picking is a mode - other tabs lock the selection
body:
Operation picking is now a mode (#1514). A viewport click changes the open operation's geometry only while its Geometry tab shows or a pick row (a boundary entry) is armed. Setup-page picks (locate, points, plane, axis, WCS) are their own modes and are not locked.

Root cause: Setup2 followed the document's machine (the default), so a pick on its Machine page routed to `LoadMachine` - the document's machine - which Setup1 also follows. Setup1 then read Setup2's pick: wrong travel and spindle refusals for Setup1 (Prime Directive).

MCP: `load_machine` already takes `setup` (that setup's own machine) and names the document explicitly without it, so an agent always states its target - no change. title: fix(ui): edge picks are one edge per click; selected and hovered picks read strongly
body:
What changed

title: fix(slot): a picked Slot stays inside its edges or face
body:
## What changed

A plain Slot picked on the part now stays inside its picks (#1504, P1 gouge).

- **Shared law, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`** (new): `SlotBound` is the room a selection allows. `SlotBound::from_edges(e1, e2)` is the strip between two straight, parallel, facing edges over their shared length. `SlotBound::from_face(region)` is a picked face's (or closed ring's) region, framed by its minimum-area rectangle (rotating calipers). `fit()` gives the slot that fills the room. `confine(a, b, width)` refuses by name, with numbers, a slot that is too wide, too long or placed past the picks. It is world-free, so the Trochoidal slot (#1503, M5) can call the same `confine`. Coordination comment posted on #1503.
- **App, `crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`** (new): `slot_bound_of(world, items)` resolves the picks (two open edges, or one face or closed ring; anything else is refused by name). `slot_from_picks` seeds the fitted a/b/width. `slot_fit_of` is the page echo.
- **Seeding, undoable:** `SetOperationGeometry` (and `CreateOperation` on picks) writes the fitted endpoints and width in the same command, the Probe's pick-seeding pattern, so one undo takes back the pick and the seed. MCP `set_operation_geometry` and `add_operation` call the same commands, so MCP has parity with no new tool.
- **Confine at generation and preview:** the job collects the picked Slot's room. The Slot arm calls `confine` before generating, and the preview's `region_for` draws nothing for a slot that does not fit. A slot is never previewed across a wall.
- **Gouge law:** a Slot with a Selection source now takes `DepthLaw::Section`, the picked pocket family's law. A picked slot cut below the floor is convicted as a `Gouge`, which blocks the post. A Stock or whole-model source is unchanged: no part law, typed endpoints rule.
- **Page:** the Geometry tab echoes `From selection: room L x W mm - the slot stays inside it`, or the refusal generation would make. The Boundary text for Slot (`area_unsupported`) now says the endpoints and width are seeded from the picks and kept inside them. TrochoidalSlot's text is untouched, split into its own arm for #1503.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/1504-slot-selection.md`. It covers the seed plus confine law, why it is not Circular's "picks author it outright" law, and the tolerances.

## Relation to #1513 (M5, Trochoidal slot)

Not stacked. #1513 adds `crates/app/src/operation/slot_fit.rs::refuse_unfit_slot(kind, a, b, width, region)`, a region-capsule law wired into the TrochoidalSlot arm. This PR keeps its own `SlotBound` for three reasons:
- The reported case is two open edges. `selection_drives_region` / `selection_region` refuse open runs for every kind but the contour, so flipping Slot there would refuse the edges before a region exists.
- A region law cannot read the strip two edges bound.
- The motion module was renamed `slot_room` so it does not share a name with #1513's `operation::slot_fit`.

The two PRs touch no common file hunk. `git merge-tree` of this head with #1513's head and with upstream/main is clean both ways. Unifying the two laws (TrochoidalSlot on `SlotBound`, or `refuse_unfit_slot` as a wrapper) is a P7 follow-up.

## How tested (pinning tests, each mutation-checked)

`crates/app/tests/slot_picks.rs`. The fixture is a 50 x 50 x 20 block with a 30 x 16 pocket to z 10, and a 10 mm end mill.
- `two_pocket_edges_give_a_slot_inside_the_pocket_and_undo_takes_it_back`: the seed is (-7,0)-(7,0), width 16. It generates with no blocking warning, every feed stays inside the pocket, and undo restores the typed slot and source.
- `the_floor_face_gives_the_slot_that_fits_it`
- `a_slot_longer_than_the_picked_edges_is_refused_by_name_and_not_previewed`: "56.000 mm long end to end ... share only 30.000 mm", and `region_of` is None.
- `a_slot_wider_than_the_picked_edges_is_refused_by_name`: "20.000 mm wide ... only 16.000 mm apart".
- `a_slot_through_the_pocket_wall_is_refused_and_one_below_the_floor_holds_the_post`: "runs 4.000 mm outside". The fitted slot with Bottom 5 gives a blocking `Gouge`.
- `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before`: Entity and Stock sources cut the typed slot through the wall, with no gouge, as before.
- `mcp_picks_seed_and_confine_the_slot_through_the_same_command`: MCP picks the two long floor chains, generates ok and verifies ok. A width of 20 is then refused by name.

`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_tests.rs` has 7 unit pins: edges fit, too wide, too long, misplaced, skew, collinear, no overlap, bowed, short, face fit, square, L-shaped face, and island.

`crates/ui/src/egui_app/slot_pick_page_tests.rs::picked_edges_seed_the_slot_echo_its_room_and_undo_together` is a structural (AccessKit) check: the echo is shown, the refusal is shown for a too-wide draft, and undo clears both. No PNGs.

Mutation results. Each mutation was applied alone and reverted after.

| Mutation | Pins that fail |
|---|---|
| M1: no `confine` in the Slot arm | 4 (too long, too wide, through the wall, MCP) |
| M2: no `DepthLaw::Section` for picked Slot | 1 (below the floor) |
| M3: no seed in `SetOperationGeometry` | 3 (edges, face, MCP) |
| M4: part law on every Slot, picked or not | 1 (no selection keeps old behaviour) |
| M5: no preview confine | 2 (not previewed) |
| M6: `FIT_TOL` loosened to 5 mm | 3 |
| UI: echo not drawn | the UI pin |

**Review fix (pullrequestreview-5897917927).** Each mutation was applied alone and reverted after. Pins run: motion `--lib slot_room` and app `slot_picks` + `slot_pick_refusals`.

| Mutation | Pins that fail |
|---|---|
| M7: `FIT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 | 4 (edge near-miss, face near-miss, stadium unit, stadium app) |
| M8: `FIT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.5 | 4 (same) |
| M9: `STRAIGHT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 | 1 (edge bowing 0.02) |
| M10: `STRAIGHT_TOL` 0.01 -> 1.0 | 2 (edge bowing, degenerate picks) |
| M11: face law, drop the wall law (region edges vs the slot's centre segment) | 6 |
| M12: face law, drop the end law (end centre outside the region) | 1 (slot wholly past the face / in a hole) |
| M13: `slot_bound_of` `([e1, e2], 0)` -> `([e1, e2, ..], 0)` | 1 (selection shapes) |
| M14: `slot_bound_of` `([], 1)` -> `(_, 1)` | 1 (selection shapes) |
| M15: `slot_bound_of` Vertex/Patch arm -> `continue` | 1 (selection shapes) |
| M16: `slot_bound_of` gone model -> `continue` | 1 (selection shapes) |
| M17: `from_face` drop "bounds no area" | 1 (degenerate picks) |
| M18: `fit` drop "no width" | 1 (degenerate picks) |
| M19: `from_edges` drop "first edge has no length" | 1 (degenerate picks) |
| M20: `confine` drop the finite / width > 0 guard | 1 (degenerate picks) |
| M21: `fit` drop the inscribe | 2 (stadium unit, stadium app) |
| M22: `judge` drop the picks' reason (plain confine) | 1 (coarse face says why) |
| M23: `CreateOperation` drop the seed | 1 (created on picks) |
| M24: `CreateOperation` undo keeps the op | 1 (created on picks) |

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 7eb71146: motion suites ok (163 s), app suites ok (741 s, `slot_picks` included), ui suites ok (38 s); wall 15.8 min, 0 failed. f35bd14e only rewrites four `!(x > t)` guards as NaN-explicit comparisons for clippy; the three pinning sets were re-run on it, green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

New pins (review fix): `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_pins.rs` (8: edge-room and face-room near misses, edge bowing, face wall law, face end law, stadium inscribed, coarse face says why, degenerate picks and numbers) and `crates/app/tests/slot_pick_refusals.rs` (3: `picks_that_bound_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_created_on_picks_takes_the_slot_between_them_and_undo_removes_it`, `a_tessellated_stadium_floor_face_seeds_the_inscribed_slot` - the reviewer's `rounded_rect(15, 8, 8, 8)` fixture).

Review-fix behaviour changes:
- `fit()` inscribes a face's slot: the radius is drawn in by the measured face overshoot (chord sag), capped at 5% of the room width (`INSCRIBE_MAX`); beyond that the face is refused. `FIT_TOL` is unchanged.
- `SlotBound::judge` (used by generation, the preview and the page echo) appends "the picks seed no slot: <reason>" when the picks bound no slot, so the user is not left with a bare length refusal.
- `face_overshoot` is exact (moved to `slot_room_face.rs`): region boundary segments against the slot's centre segment, plus end-centre containment, in place of 0.5 mm sampling.

## Not exercised

- A real STEP pocket with tessellated round ends was not run. A synthetic 8-chords-per-quarter stadium (0.039 mm sag) is now pinned and inscribed; coarser STEP tessellation inscribes up to 5% of the width.
- A face with point-ended (one chord per quarter) round ends: its minimum-area rectangle can turn diagonal (a hexagon's), so the frame is not the slot's axis; it is refused by name either way, never seeded wrong.
- Follow-up filed: #1537 (P1) - a Slot with a whole-model (entity) source takes no part law, so a typed slot through the finished part raises no gouge. Pre-existing; not changed here.
- Re-picking re-seeds over a user-shortened slot: kept by design (one undo restores it), recorded in the decision file.
- A Slot under a 3+2 tilt with picks is still refused upstream ("a tilted plane cannot yet index a picked selection"), unchanged.
- Refusal numbers print in mm regardless of the document's display unit, like the slot generator's other refusals.
- The TrochoidalSlot is not wired. That is #1503 (M5), which can call `SlotBound::confine`.

Changelog: A Slot with two opposite edges or a face picked now takes the slot between them (centre line, length, width - undoable with the pick), refuses by name a slot too wide, too long or placed past its picks (never previewed across a wall), and is judged against the part so a slot cut below the picked floor holds the post (#1504)

Review-fix quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on b1e25d27 (merged with upstream/main): motion 147 s, app 765 s (incl. `slot_picks`, `slot_pick_refusals`), ui 57 s; wall 16.2 min, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1504

title: fix(ui): hovering a Geometry-tab selection highlights it in the viewport
body:
## What changed
Hovering a selection row in an operation's Geometry tab (its label, its remove button, or anywhere on the row) now lights that face, chain/edge or vertex in the viewport with a strong hover highlight: a 7 px dark halo under a 3.5 px hot-magenta stroke (`Overlay::RowHover`, a dark and a light value), apart from the violet pick, the 1 px yellow viewport hover and the other overlay inks. It clears when the pointer leaves.

Root cause worth knowing: the old label hover set `State.geo_hover`, but the shell cleared it at frame start and the viewport pane draws before the properties pane sets it, so it never reached the draw (the highlight did not work at all). Fix: `State.geo_hover_drawn` carries last frame's value to the viewport (one-frame lag; a repaint is requested whenever the two differ). The thin `hover_features` pass no longer repeats the row hover; `interact::row_hover_segments` is the strong layer. Ephemeral view state in `State` (the existing hover precedent), no command, no undo, no direct world pokes. Decision: `docs/decisions/1507-geometry-row-hover.md`.

Reverse direction (hover in viewport marks the row) is not done: filed as #1519 (P4, effort:medium, area:ui).

Overlap: #1330 and #1314 touch ui files but not the geometry tab or the hover draw; #1505 (edge selected style) is untouched here, the hover ink was chosen distinct from the current pick inks.

## Pins
- `egui_app::tests::geo_row_hover::hovering_a_selection_row_or_its_remove_button_sets_the_hovered_selection`: face, chain and vertex rows; label and remove-button hover set `geo_hover` to that row's entity, row 2/3 give theirs, leaving clears it and the viewport draw segments, no command filed.
- `geo_row_hover::row_hover_style_is_strong_and_distinct_in_both_themes`: named constants, ink distinct from the other overlay inks in both themes.
- `law_tests::preview_tests::hover_features_lights_the_face_boundary` (updated): row hover goes through `row_hover_segments`; stale/gone/hidden draw nothing.

Mutation checks (each reverted): drop remove-button/row-rect hover -> row-0 remove-button assertion fails; shell never clears -> "leaving clears row 0" fails; `row_hover_segments` empty -> "reaches the draw list" fails; 1 px stroke -> style test fails; drop the one-frame carry -> "reaches the draw list" fails. Not pinned: reading `geo_hover` instead of `geo_hover_drawn` in the draw is indistinguishable post-frame (the ordering is exercised only by a real two-pane frame; the screenshot shows it works).

Gates: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green; `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=1` 710 passed; clippy ui + app `-D warnings` clean. No snapshot PNGs touched.

Screenshots: attached below (headless `harness.render()` of the throwaway test, which was deleted; the render has no GPU mesh, only the egui overlay, hovering the chain row). Local: `~/Desktop/camcraft/builds/pr-1507-hover/before.png` and `after.png` (before = no highlight, which is also what upstream main drew, per the root cause above).

title: fix(setup): refuse generation under a WCS tilted off the machine Z
body:
## What changed

A milling setup's WCS can be turned onto another face from the WCS pane, but every milling generator cuts along the machine's Z. The turned WCS was drawn and then ignored: the reporter's Setup2 facing machined the face that is level in the model (the wrong face) and the op said "OK". The post already refused any rotated work offset (#315), so no wrong G-code could post. The toolpath was still wrong, though, and nothing on screen said so.

- New `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_tilt.rs`: `generation_problem` / `setup_problem` return a named refusal when a milling setup's WCS Z is tilted off the machine's +Z (more than 1e-9 rad, the post's identity tolerance).
- `collect_job` (the generation door) refuses with it: *"setup 'Setup2': its WCS (G54) has its Z axis tilted 90.000 deg off the machine's Z - the tool always cuts along the machine's Z, so this would machine the part as it lies, not as the WCS shows; turn the part with the setup's Part alignment instead and keep the WCS Z pointing up"*.
- A facing pick on a face that is level only in the tilted WCS (the reporter's first error) now names the WCS as the reason instead of suggesting a 2D Contour. It keeps the "is not horizontal - a facing pass needs a floor" door phrase, so `door_refusal` still treats it as a door refusal.
- A WCS turned only about Z (a squared-up offset) still generates. Its post refusal is #315's, unchanged.
- Milling only (`Kind::Mill`). Lathe, wire and the other machine kinds are not affected.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1510-tilted-wcs.md`. Actually generating in the WCS frame was considered and dropped: that is effort:max work, and Part alignment (#326) already turns the part for a setup.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_tilt.rs::a_tilted_setup_wcs_refuses_generation_by_name`: the reporter's case (Setup1 square, Setup2 WCS turned 90 deg about X). Setup2's face is refused by name and Setup1's still generates.
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_tilt.rs::a_wcs_turned_only_about_z_still_generates`: the scope guard (yaw only still generates).
- `crates/app/tests/pick_doors.rs::a_wall_level_only_in_a_tilted_wcs_names_the_wcs`: the pick refusal names the tilted WCS and Part alignment.

Mutation check (standing rule):
- Deleted the `setup_wcs_tilt::generation_problem` check in `collect_job`: `a_tilted_setup_wcs_refuses_generation_by_name` went RED. Restored: GREEN.
- Deleted the tilted-WCS branch in `selection.rs`: `a_wall_level_only_in_a_tilted_wcs_names_the_wcs` went RED. Restored: GREEN.

Also run by hand, all green: rotated_wcs, commands_undo, mcp_model, mcp_setup, mcp_wcs_features, one_wcs, project_roundtrip, rotary_verify, wcs_align, wcs_roles, posting, setup_sheet, setups, heights, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, wcs_view_pose, circle_centre, face_origin, operations, setup_align.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`. green: 1 step (19 app suites + app lib), 0 failed, 4.3 min wall; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI by hand. The refusal reaches the op status and status line the way every `GenError::Invalid` does, and no UI code changed, so there are no structural assertions or snapshots to update.
- Ops in a non-mill setup under a tilted WCS. They are out of scope on purpose.

Changelog: A milling setup whose WCS Z is tilted off the machine's Z is now refused at generation by name (pointing at Part alignment), instead of quietly facing the wrong face; a facing pick that is level only in the tilted WCS says why (#1510)

Effort: high (no escalation)
