title: fix(trochoid): a Trochoidal slot stays inside its selection or is refused; the post judges it for gouges
body:
## What changed

A Trochoidal slot with a selection picked (a face or edge chains) generated a path across the selected pocket's wall into the model and reported **OK** (#1503, maintainer screenshot). Generation now refuses such a slot by name, with the numbers:

> Trochoidal slot: the 16.000 mm wide slot from A (-20.000, 0.000) to B (20.000, 0.000) does not fit its selection - it needs 8.000 mm clear each side of its centre line, but the selection's edge comes within 5.000 mm at (...), so the cut would run 3.000 mm past the selection into the model; shorten or narrow the slot, or select the region it should cut

- New `crates/app/src/operation/slot_fit.rs`: `refuse_unfit_slot(kind, a, b, width, region)`. This is pure plane geometry. The slot's capsule (centre line A-B, half-width width/2) must lie inside the picked region: both endpoints inside, and every boundary edge of every loop (holes included) at least width/2 from the centre line, with 1e-4 mm of slack so a slot exactly as wide as its pocket still fits. The generator already keeps every loop inside that band (`contained` in motion `trochoid_slot`), so the check covers what is cut. It refuses rather than clips, which is simpler and safe.
- `operation/generate.rs`: the TrochoidalSlot arm resolves its region first. When the source is a selection, it calls the helper before generating.
- No selection: nothing changes. The typed endpoints rule, and the post judges the path against the model.

**Step 0 (posted on #1503):** on upstream main df90b031 the post **already refused** this slot through the stock-sim gouge clause: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 5926 cell(s), worst 20.00 mm at (-25.31, -5.94, z 0.00)`. The gap was at generation, where the status was `ok` with cached blocking `Gouge` findings. Nothing opts this op out of the gouge check. The page text "Boundary settings do not apply" only means the area controls (offset, extension) are not used.

**Shared with #1504:** the helper takes the kind's label, so the plain Slot can call it unchanged. Slot is excluded in `selection_drives_region`, so its arm sees the authored stadium today, not the picks; #1504 (M3) owns that. Noted on #1503 and #1504. The Slot arm is not touched here.

**Split:** Expected item 2 (trochoidal motion as a 2D Adaptive method) is out of this PR. It is filed as #1509 (Part of #1503, effort:max). That is why this PR says `Refs #1503`, not Fixes: #1503's Done means includes the Adaptive method. The maintainer can close #1503 when this merges if #1509 carries item 2.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/trochoid_confine.rs`. The fixture is an 80 x 60 x 20 block with a 50 x 25 pocket to z 10 (floor face 1250 mm2, as in the screenshot) and a 6 mm `EM-0600-4FL`.

| Pin | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `a_slot_longer_than_its_selected_pocket_face_is_refused_by_name` | The screenshot setup (A (-20,0), B (20,0), width 16, floor face picked) is refused by name with 8.000 / 5.000 / 3.000. No path is cached and nothing posts. |
| `mcp_refuses_the_same_slot_by_name` | The same refusal over MCP: `add_operation` (seeded A/B/width), `set_operation_geometry` (floor face), `generate`. The post is refused too. |
| `a_slot_that_fits_its_selection_generates_and_posts_clean` | A (-12,0) to B (12,0), width 16 generates with no blocking warning. The program gate (stock sim against the model) is empty and it posts. No false refusal. |
| `the_post_refuses_an_unconfined_trochoid_that_enters_the_model` | With no selection, the same slot through the end walls generates, and the post's stock-sim gouge clause refuses it (`gouge: program cuts below the model ...`). |
| `slot_fit::tests` (unit, 2) | Fits, exactly-as-wide fits, past the end wall refused with numbers, endpoint outside, centre line across a hole. |

Mutation checks (revert the guard, confirm red, restore, confirm green):
- Confinement call disabled (`if false && ...` in generate.rs): `a_slot_longer...` and `mcp_refuses...` are **red**, the other two green. Restored: 4/4 green.
- Sim gouge clause blinded (`Ok(sim) if false && sim.dev.gouge_cells > 0` in posting_sim.rs): `the_post_refuses...` is **red**, the others green. Restored: 4/4 green.
- Guard made 5 mm too strict (`d + FIT_TOL < half + 5.0`): `a_slot_that_fits...` is **red** (a false refusal is caught). Restored: 4/4 green.

Gates (local, macOS, fork synced at upstream main df90b031): the quick gate's app step (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, 167 app suites incl. trochoid_op, trochoid_confine, operations, posting, mcp, mcp_order, stock_sim_document, slot_caps, pocket_overhead, plus mcp_verify, mcp_pick, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition) all green, and `camcraft-app --lib` 186/186 after a fix to my own unit fixture. motion `trochoid_slot` green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The quick gate's ui step (boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, feedback, machine, operations, sinker_setup) was **not run**: no ui code changed, and those suites open windows.

## Not exercised

- The UI page text ("Boundary settings do not apply to it") is unchanged. The structural UI test is not touched, and the ui suites were not run (no ui code changed; they open windows).
- Depth: a slot whose bottom is below the picked floor face is not refused at generation. The verify pass caches blocking `Gouge` findings and the post's sim refuses it, as for every other op.
- Edge-chain selections go through the same picked region. Only the face pick is pinned.

Changelog: A Trochoidal slot with a selection is refused by name, with the numbers, when its endpoints and width do not fit inside the selected region, instead of generating across a wall into the model (#1503)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(ui): setup eye in the browser; only the active setup is drawn by default
body:
## What changed
- Each setup row in the browser tree has the existing eye. By default only the active setup is drawn in the viewport; another setup's operation paths, work-offset triad and fixtures come up when its eye is turned on, without making it active. The active setup's eye is a no-op.
- State is `State::shown_setups` (view state, like `hidden_models` and friends: not undoable, not saved, reset on New/Open). Why no command or MCP tool: `docs/decisions/1494-setup-eye.md`.
- Display only: posting, simulation and collision checks read the world, not these lists.
- Eye icon: the existing Eye/EyeOff glyphs, no new asset.
- Two existing gizmo tests assumed another setup's triad was always drawn; they now turn its eye on (law_tests, wcs_gizmo_tests).

## Pinned by
`egui_app::tests::setup_eye::*` (5 tests): row eye and default hidden state, eye shows another setup's path without activating it, activating draws it, work offset follows the eye, `hiding_a_setup_never_changes_what_posts`.

## How tested
`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green (ui lib and suites); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised
- Not run in the GUI; no pixel snapshots touched.
- Before/after screenshots are owed (the worker cannot take them); needed before /merge-ready offers it.
- Other setups' stock is already undrawn (only the active stock draws); not changed.

Changelog: The browser shows an eye on each setup; only the active setup is drawn in the viewport unless another setup's eye is on.

title: feat(post): Sodick wire EDM post, 2-axis contour from the 1998 operation manual
body:
## What changed

A second wire EDM post, `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, offered as "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)" for machines declared `wire_edm`. It is never the default; the generic ISO wire post stays first.

**The output was not run on a real Sodick control. It must be checked by someone with the machine before cutting.** Every posted program says so in its header (`NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING`).

This is one slice: a vertical 2-axis Wire Contour. The program is:

- header comments (machine name, not verified, wire-centre path, no `G92` written, tank and flushing not programmed)
- `G21` or `G20`, `G90`
- a header line: each C condition named below must exist in the control's condition table before start
- per operation: a line naming its condition (`CONDITION C110 MUST EXIST IN THE CONTROL CONDITION TABLE - CHECK ITS VALUES`), the setup's `G54`-`G59`, `G40 G00 X Y` to the start hole (the wire offset is cancelled before any motion), `T91` (thread), the condition id as a `C` word, then `G01` / `G02` / `G03 X Y I J`, `T90` (cut the wire)
- `M02`

On a machine with `edm.awt: false` the operator threads and cuts the wire at a stated `M00`. Every coordinate carries a decimal point.

Refused by name, never posted: taper, 4-axis, a leaning or posed move, a rotary, a Z change, a rapid while threaded, a tool change, an rpm, a canned cycle, a non-XY arc, an arc without a centre, an arc as the first cut, a trip home, a non-wire machine or operation, a work offset outside `G54`-`G59`, a condition id that is not `C` and three digits, and a program that ends threaded.

Files: the script; `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (registry entry, `WIRE_POSTS`); `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `wire_post.rs` (the tables learn the second wire post); `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`; new tests and goldens; `docs/decisions/617-sodick-wire-post.md`. No new dependency.

## Sources

- Sodick Inc., "Wire EDM Machine Operation" (copyright November 1998; A320D, A530, A530D, AP350, AP500, A600, A750, A1000; Mark 21 / EX21 control), read at manualslib.com/manual/2816797/Sodick-A320d.html: G, M and T code tables, the word list, the AWT sequence and the program examples.
- RS-274 / ISO 6983 for the motion words.
- This project's `wire-iso.cps` for the script's structure.

No other CAM product's post, post library or output was read. The sample program attached to the issue is another CAM's output and was not used.

## Unconfirmed

Check each at the machine:

- Whether the LN1W / LN2W controls of the AQ / AD / ALN series (the issue's machine is an AQ600L) read these Mark 21 words unchanged. No free official reference for the LN controls was found.
- `G40` beside `G00` on the move to the threading point, with no offset active, in a program that never states `G41` / `G42`.
- A program with no `G92` / `G29`, relying on the work offset set at the control.
- Cutting with no flushing or tank word in the program.
- No `%`, no program number, no `M30`.
- The condition as a bare `C` word with no condition table rows in the file (the header and each section tell the operator to check it exists).
- `M02` after `T90` leaving the machine safe.
- The manual was read through a third-party-hosted copy by a summarising fetch, not page by page.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/sodick_wire_post.rs` (8 tests): `the_punch_contour_posts_its_sodick_golden_through_the_gate`, `the_registry_offers_the_sodick_post_for_wire_edms_only_and_never_by_default`, `taper_and_four_axis_are_refused_by_name`, `a_condition_id_that_is_not_a_sodick_c_word_is_refused_by_name`, `a_mill_machine_and_a_milling_section_are_refused_by_name`, `without_awt_the_operator_threads_and_cuts_at_a_stated_stop`, `an_inch_document_posts_g20_with_pointed_four_place_words`, `an_arc_posts_g03_with_incremental_i_j_and_never_as_the_first_cut`. New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch.nc`.
- `crates/post/tests/script_sodick_wire.rs`: the post on the 11 recorded edge-case streams, each a named refusal (new goldens in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/sodick-wire/`).
- Green on the head: every `camcraft-post` suite; `camcraft-app` lib plus the 38 suites that touch the post registry or wire work (`conformance`, `wire_post`, `posting`, `post_serves_kind`, `explain_option`, `smoothing`, `program_units`, `recorded_post_streams`, the `wire_*`, `plasma_*`, `coolant*` and lathe post suites among them); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- No existing golden or snapshot was changed.

## Not exercised

- No Sodick control or simulator ran the output.
- `cargo xtask gate quick` as one command: its plan for this diff is every app suite (about 350 binaries). The suites above were run instead; the rest of app and all of `camcraft-ui` were not.
- Taper and 4-axis only as refusals.
- No UI test: the post appears through the existing post list. No real Sodick machine file exists yet (#1501); the tests use the wire EDM fixture machine.

## Follow-ups

- #1496 taper
- #1497 4-axis
- #1498 control-side wire offset and skim passes
- #1499 tank and flushing words as parameters
- #1500 confirm the LN-control program format
- #1501 a Sodick machine file with sourced travels

No new command, so no MCP tool is owed.

Changelog: Sodick wire EDM post ("Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)"): 2-axis wire contours in the words of Sodick's 1998 operation manual; taper and 4-axis are refused by name; not verified on a control.

## Review fixes (second commit, 4276e97e8)

- `G40` placement: moved from the first cut to the `G00` to the threading point, so a wire offset left by an earlier program cannot shift the positioning or threading. Source: the manual shows `G40` riding a move (`G40 Y-.02`); RS-274 / ISO 6983 put `G40` in its own modal group, so it may share a block with `G00`, and cancelling with no offset active is legal. No header line was needed for this.
- Condition table: a header line says each C condition named below must exist in the control's condition table; each section names its own condition before its first motion. (A list of all conditions at the very top was dropped: the post writes as it reads, and splicing lines in afterwards would shift the section line ranges the engine records.)
- Closing keyword: this PR now only refers to the issue (the post is unverified; the issue's machine is an LN-control AQ600L, #1500 open). **The first commit's message (8460431c7) still carries a closing keyword for the issue** (history is not rewritten): the merger must check that issue 617 stays open after the merge, and reopen it if GitHub closes it.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Refs #617

title: feat(pocket): pre-drilled entry - plunge down proved drilled holes (#1449, slice 1)
body:
First slice of #1449: a 2D Pocket can enter each level by a straight plunge down a hole that a Drill operation ahead of it in the same setup made. It does this only where that hole is proved open. Everything else keeps the asked helix, ramp or arc, and the path says why by name.

Branched from upstream/main at ba3776b1 (the mkinney fork's main is on v0.18.0; this branch carries upstream's current process files).

## What changed

- **`camcraft-motion`**
  - New `Approach::predrilled` flag (default off).
  - New `machining2d::predrilled` module and `pocket_entered(region, params, holes)`; `pocket()` is unchanged and calls it with no holes.
  - The ladder's `descent::plan` takes a proved hole ahead of every arm. A hole is used only when it is open to the level's Z, its centre is a legal cutter centre, and the dive link from it to the pass start is proved. When no hole serves a level, the asked entry stands and a note says why.
  - The pass plan is re-seated on the deepest proved hole: a ring is rotated, an open zigzag pass is split into a forward tail and a reversed head. The link from the hole is then the shortest one to any pass, so it crosses none (verify's Crossing law stays silent).
- **`camcraft-app`**
  - New `operation::predrilled_entry::proved_holes`. Hole centres come from the moves of the Drill ops ahead (`rest::drills_ahead`, now also collected for a Pocket with the flag on). A hole is kept only if:
    - the drill's stated diameter is at least the tool's + 2 x 0.1 mm clearance;
    - the prior grid (the stock the program ahead leaves, as the drilling and thread laws read it) holds no material over the tool disc + clearance above the counted depth;
    - the counted depth is the deeper of the grid reading and the drill point's cone at the disc radius.
  - Unprovable cases are named and the hole is left out: no drill, a drill too narrow (with the numbers), an unreadable prior, a posed 3+2 pocket.
  - File: `links.approach.predrilled` (written only when on). Stamp: byte `0xC7` only when on. The pocket already goes Stale when the program ahead changes.
  - Door: the flag on any kind other than 2D Pocket is refused by name (`PREDRILLED_POCKET_ONLY`), never silently dropped.
- **Command / MCP:** the flag is an ordinary params field, so `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and MCP `edit_operation` / `add_operation` set it with `{"links": {"approach": {"predrilled": true}}}`. No new command or tool was needed.
- **Decision:** `docs/decisions/1449-predrilled-entry.md`.

## How tested (pins, each mutation-checked)

| Pin | Test(s) | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hole proved: plunge at every level, no helix; posted G-code has `G00 X0 Y0 Z..` then `G01 X0 Y0 Z12 F200`; verify silent; posts through the gate | app `a_drilled_hole_ahead_is_plunged_to_full_depth_and_posted`, motion `a_proved_hole_is_plunged_at_every_level_with_no_helix` | entry never plunges | caught |
| Delete the drill: the pocket goes Stale at once; regenerated, it has no plunge and uses the helix | app `deleting_the_drill_takes_the_plunge_away`, `without_the_drill_the_helix_stands_and_says_why` | pocket stamp ignores the program ahead | caught |
| Hole the grid does not show is never air | unit `a_hole_the_grid_does_not_show_is_never_air`, `an_unreadable_prior_proves_nothing` | floor from drill moves only, grid dropped | caught |
| Drill narrower than tool + clearance (Ø4 into Ø4, 4.2 needed): left out by name | app `a_drill_no_wider_than_the_tool_plus_clearance_is_refused_by_name`, unit twin | width check dropped | caught |
| Shallow hole: only the levels it reaches plunge; the floor level helixes, named with the Z numbers | app + motion `a_shallow_hole_serves_only_the_levels_it_reaches` | depth check dropped | caught |
| Hole outside the cutter-centre area is never plunged | motion `a_hole_outside_the_cutter_area_is_never_plunged` | area AND link proof dropped together | caught |
| Area check alone (`predrilled.rs` entry filter) | unit `predrilled::tests::a_hole_outside_the_cutter_area_is_refused_even_at_the_pass_start` | area check dropped | caught (only this pin) |
| Link proof alone | unit `predrilled::tests::a_hole_whose_link_crosses_a_planned_pass_is_refused` | link proof dropped | caught (only this pin) |
| Non-centre-cutting tool keeps its entry, named | motion `a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting_keeps_the_asked_entry` | guard dropped | caught |
| Undo/redo, file round trip, refused on another kind; MCP set + undo + refusal on adaptive | app `the_flag_is_an_undoable_edit_and_refused_off_the_pocket`, `mcp_sets_and_undoes_the_flag` | - | - |

Also: `with_the_flag_off_the_drill_is_never_read`, `without_a_hole_or_the_flag_the_helix_stands`, `a_non_finite_hole_is_ignored`, `a_posed_pocket_and_no_drill_are_named`, `an_open_wide_hole_is_handed_over_to_its_cone_depth`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 9d098fe8): green - motion suites 140 s, app suites 691 s, ui suites 18 s, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean (without `--no-deps` the newer clippy flags three pre-existing `needless_range_loop` sites in the untouched `camcraft-geometry` feature.rs).

## Not exercised / remaining on #1449

- UI: no "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group yet, so no structural UI test for it. The flag is reachable by MCP, script params and the file.
- 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing kinds (refused by name at the door for now).
- Holes in the model, typed points with an explicit "the hole exists" choice, carried stock from a previous setup, and a "pre-drilled only" refusal mode.
- Non-centre-cutting tools down a hole: the plunge law would need the proved holes.
- A user-set clearance (fixed at 0.1 mm a side).
- Golden CL file: the pins assert the moves and the posted lines directly.
- No hand check in the GUI or on a machine.

Changelog: 2D Pocket: pre-drilled entry - with `links.approach.predrilled` on, each level is entered by a straight plunge down a hole a Drill operation ahead of it in the setup made, only where the stock simulation proves the hole open wide and deep enough; elsewhere the asked entry stands, named (#1449, first slice)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Refs #1449

title: feat(contour): user-set exit point on closed 2D contours
body:
## What changed

Slice 1 of #1473 (follow-up of #1448 / PR 1478): a user-set **exit point** on a closed 2D Contour, plus the "no lead fits at the pick" refusal pin the review of PR 1478 asked for.

- `links.approach.exit_point` (`[x, y]` mm, optional) beside `start_point`: motion `Approach` (validated finite / within 1 km), project DTO (written only when set), op digest (bytes only when set), MCP `edit_operation` patch. No new command: `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` and undo carry it.
- Motion (`contour_start::pick_exit`, `exit_at`): the ring nearest the pick is cut all the way round from its start, then on along its own cutter-centre polyline to the pick's projection, and the lead-out is planned there by the existing lead law. Nothing is moved: refused by name when a lead-out asked for does not fit there, when the longer walk loses the start's lead-in, when the lead-out crosses the lead-in, or the pick is out of reach.
- Not certified in this slice, refused by name: tabs, control / wear compensation, the keep-down level link, an overlap set beside the exit, open chains, tilted contours, every other op kind.
- No exit point = byte-identical path (no existing golden or snapshot touched).

## How tested

- `crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs`: `a_picked_exit_cuts_the_whole_ring_then_leaves_at_its_projection`, `an_exit_on_the_seam_is_the_path_without_one`, `exit_picks_the_law_cannot_hold_are_refused_by_name`, `a_picked_exit_no_lead_out_fits_at_is_refused_not_moved`, `a_picked_start_no_lead_in_fits_at_is_refused_not_moved` (the PR 1478 review's request: narrow 40 x 6.4 bore, 20 mm perpendicular lead).
- `crates/app/tests/contour_start_point.rs`: `the_exit_point_rides_the_command_undo_the_file_and_the_stamp`, `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_the_exit_point`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.

## Not exercised

- No UI row or viewport pick (item 2 of #1473), so no structural test or screenshots owed yet. No new golden CL (the motion tests pin the geometry).
- Not run on a post / simulation: the exit run re-cuts the ring itself, so no new geometry reaches the verifier.
- `contour.rs` was already over 400 lines (438) before this slice; it grows by 5 lines of wiring, the logic is in `contour_start.rs`.

## Left for #1473

Items 2-7: viewport pick + property row, start/exit with tabs, with control compensation, open chains, tilted contours, other operations.

Changelog: Contour: a user-set exit point on closed 2D contours - the ring is cut all the way round and the lead-out leaves at the pick, or the operation is refused by name

title: feat(motion): 2D rest area and rest pocket passes after a larger tool
body:
First slice of #1446: the rest-machining generator in the motion crate. The operation parameter, its undoable edit, the project file, the dialog group and the MCP parameters are not in this PR (follow-ups below), so nothing a user can reach changes yet and no posted G-code changes.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs` (new):
  - `rest_plan(region, tool_diameter, stock_to_leave, &RestParams) -> RestPlan`: the rest area (what a larger previous tool could not reach) and the cutter-center area that touches it.
  - `rest_pocket(region, &PocketParams, &RestParams) -> Toolpath`: the pocket's ring passes over that area only.
  - `RestParams`: previous tool diameter, previous tool corner radius, stock the previous operation left on the walls, rest allowance. The previous tool is entered, and the path says in a note that it is trusted.
- `pocket.rs`: the body of `pocket()` is now `pocket_over(region, center, p, notes, hold_crossings)`, shared with the rest pass. `pocket()` computes its center area and calls it with no notes and the switch off: the plain pocket posts as before. `PocketStrategy` moved to `pocket_strategy.rs` (structure only; `pocket.rs` 456 -> 427 lines, still over the 400-line law it was already over).
- `docs/decisions/1446-rest-2d.md`: the decisions taken.

## How the rest area is read

Rest = pocket minus the opening of the pocket by the previous tool's disc (inward offset by its radius, then outward). It is read large, never small:

- the cleared area is shrunk by 0.01 mm (`REST_MARGIN`, two offset arc tolerances) before it is subtracted;
- a previous tool with a corner radius sweeps only its flat; stock left on the walls is rest material; the allowance only grows the area (negative is refused);
- the one reduction is a film thinner than 0.02 mm (`REST_FILM`), without which every wall would read as rest material;
- the cutter-center area is the rest area grown by the tool radius plus 0.05 mm (`REST_REACH`), cut to the plain pocket's own center area: a rest pass cannot touch a wall the plain pocket would not.

No rapid relies on the estimate: below the top of the cut every move is a plunge or a feed, and separate rest areas are linked by a retract. A wrong previous tool costs a heavier cut, not a rapid into stock.

Refused by name: a previous tool that is not larger than this tool; non-finite or negative values; a corner radius larger than the tool radius; `Zigzag` (its rows left residue in the corner in the coverage test); `Adaptive` (not built for rest areas); nothing left to cut (`GenError::Empty`, "no rest material"); a pocket narrower than the tool. `Auto` reads as `Waterline` for a rest pass. A previous tool that fits nowhere leaves the whole pocket: the path equals the plain pocket's, with a note.

Two things found while testing, both recorded in the decisions file: fitted arcs crossed each other at the thin horns of a rest area (verifier Crossing law, neck fixture), so the rest rings go through the existing `arc_cross` proof as the Adaptive plan does; and the bare-radius reach left slivers along the pocket's own center boundary, hence `REST_REACH`.

## Readings (fixture: 60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, previous tool 12 mm, this tool 4 mm)

- Rest area: 4 loops, one per corner, each inside its 6 mm corner box; area within -0.05 / +1.5 mm2 of the exact 23.18 mm2; 0 of more than 1500 grid points of certain residue missing; 0 grid points of rest area deeper than 0.2 mm into cleared floor.
- Rest passes (Waterline, Offset rings, Auto): verifier (`Mode::Area`) clean; every cutting move within 8.3 mm of a corner; the only rapids below the top of the cut are straight lifts; every certain-residue grid point is under the tool at the floor; cutting length at the floor under 25 % of the full pocket's.
- Neck fixture (two bays joined by a 6 mm neck): the neck is rest material and is cut through; 9 center areas, none a sliver; verifier clean.

## Pinning tests

`crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs` (10 tests): `rest_area_is_the_four_corners_and_never_reads_small`, `rest_passes_cut_only_the_corners_and_cover_them`, `rest_pass_is_far_shorter_than_the_full_pocket`, `previous_tool_not_larger_is_refused_by_name`, `bad_rest_parameters_are_refused_by_name`, `nothing_left_is_refused_not_cut`, `previous_tool_that_fits_nowhere_leaves_the_whole_pocket`, `a_neck_the_previous_tool_could_not_pass_is_rest_material`, `allowance_stock_and_corner_radius_only_grow_the_rest_area`, `degenerate_pockets_error_and_never_panic`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green on the head (motion suites 242 s, app suites 463 s, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The toolpaths were not run on a machine.
- No stock simulation: "no pass over cleared floor" and "no plunge into uncut stock" are read from the path geometry and the verifier, not from a simulated roughing pass followed by the rest pass.
- No golden CL (the golden helpers live in the app tests; the motion tests pin readings) and nothing through the app, the UI, the project file or MCP: none of it is wired.
- The previous tool is entered and trusted. A roughing pass that did not reach the stated depth, or used another tool, is not detected.
- Adaptive and Zigzag with rest are refused, not built. Pockets with islands and stock to leave on this operation are covered by the construction but have no fixture of their own.
- Windows only; debug build.

## Literature

- J. Serra, "Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology", Academic Press, 1982 (erosion, dilation, opening).
- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, Springer, 1991 (offsets and the machinable area).
- D. Veeramani, Y.-S. Gau, "Selection of an optimal set of cutting-tool sizes for 2.5D pocket machining", Computer-Aided Design 29(12), 1997.
- Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta, D. S. Nau, "Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems", Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003.

The citations were found by a literature search and checked by title and venue; the papers' full texts were not read line by line, and the construction used is the textbook opening they share. No code or text from stevecad/camlib or any other CAM product was read or used; no HSMWorks material.

## Follow-ups

- #1489: the Pocket operation parameter (default off), its undoable edit, the project file, the dialog group, the MCP parameters, the golden CL through the app and the stock-simulation reading.
- #1490: Adaptive over a rest area, entry from already-cut space, the previous tool read from the carried stock, Zigzag.

No UI change, so no screenshots.

Changelog: 2D rest machining generator in the motion crate: the rest area a larger previous tool left and the ring passes that cut only it; not wired to an operation yet

Effort: max (no escalation)

Refs #1446

title: chore(process): the merging session is the one writer of PROCESS_VERSION
body:
Process change: yes (this PR bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 62 to 63 itself, the last PR to do so).

**What changed.** The merging session is the single writer of `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. Process PRs no longer edit it and say `Process change: yes` in the body; after a merge batch with a process PR the session runs the new `cargo xtask process-bump` (+1), merges a one-line PR and posts the #681 announcement. AGENTS.md, the PR-reviewer agent, and the review-prs, merge-ready and resolve-conflicts skills are updated. A fork still compares the same file, so nothing changes for it. Choices and dropped alternatives (merge-commit count, merge driver, Action) are in `docs/decisions/1153-process-version-single-writer.md`; no Actions trigger is added and no per-clone git config is needed.

**Tests.** `xtask/src/process_bump_tests.rs` (bump +1, refusal of non-integer/overflow, file rewrite and argument refusal); quick gate green (xtask unit tests).

**Not exercised.** The follow-up bump PR flow itself (first use is the merge of this PR); `merge-plan` still lists the file as MECHANICAL, kept for old branches.

Changelog: none

title: fix(sim): draw lathe chuck bores inscribed so the collision solid never drops steel
body:
## What changed

- `camcraft_sim::chuck::ring`: the bore (inner) polygon is now **inscribed** in the true bore circle (vertices on the circle, flats inside it by r(1 - cos(pi/64)), about 0.12 % of r). Outer faces are unchanged: flats on the true circle, vertices outside (circumscribed).
- The module comment claimed the bore was conservative while the code drew it the unsafe way round; it now says what the code does and why.
- `crates/sim/tests/lathe_chuck.rs`: the envelope is pinned to the tessellation allowance. New helper `ring_envelope` probes, at every polygon vertex and every flat middle (128 angles), steel 1e-3 mm inside each true outer face and 1e-3 mm outside each true bore wall, and air 1e-3 mm past each face's allowance. The jaw tip, gripping face and side are probed at 1e-3 mm too. The old probes stood 0.5-1 mm off the rim and jaw tip and never touched the bore wall.

## Which direction is safe, and why

The collision solid is the steel; a bore is the absence of steel. A bore polygon whose flats touch the circle (circumscribed, what PR 1469 shipped) puts its vertices *outside* the bore, so the true steel between r and r/cos(pi/64) near every vertex was missing from the solid: a tool could pass there unflagged. Inscribed, the drawn bore is smaller than the true one: the solid can only claim extra steel, never drop real steel. Net rule now: every drawn face is on or outside the real steel.

Cost accepted (recorded in `docs/decisions/1470-chuck-bore-inscribed.md`): the drawn steel stands up to that sag into the bore. The part/stock-versus-fixture clash check is a warning only and counts past 0.05 mm, so it stays quiet for bores up to about 83 mm.

## Existing test changes

- `crates/app/tests/builtin_accessory.rs` `every_kind_builds_closed_shells_of_its_dimensions`: its expected chuck volume used the circumscribed polygon area for the bore; it now uses the inscribed area (n sin cos r^2). The solid's volume goes up by that sliver (more steel); bounds are unchanged (outer faces untouched).
- `crates/sim/tests/lathe_chuck.rs`: probes tightened as above (each old steel/air probe is replaced by a stricter one at the same feature). No golden or snapshot changes.

## How tested

Failing first: with only the test change, `three_jaw_envelope_is_pinned` and `collet_envelope_is_pinned` failed with "steel just outside the bore wall at 0.0000001 rad" (the bore vertex). With the fix:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: sim lib + `sim:lathe_chuck` (6 passed), `app:builtin_accessory` - green.
- Also `app:lathe_chuck` (3) and `app:mcp_accessory` (2) - green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test builtin_accessory -D warnings` - clean.

Pinned by `three_jaw_envelope_is_pinned`, `collet_envelope_is_pinned` (sim) and `every_kind_builds_closed_shells_of_its_dimensions` (app).

## Not exercised

- The rest of the app suites (batch tier) and the release heavy lanes.
- Pixel snapshots: a chuck render would differ by a sub-pixel sliver at most; not run, not regenerated.
- The `fixture_clash` warning on a large (>83 mm) bore holding a part exactly at the bore: reasoned, not tested.
- The GUI.

Changelog: Lathe chuck collision solids are drawn with their bores inscribed, so the solid is never smaller than the real chuck anywhere (#1470)
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1470

Rides the bore door: the tool must fit the hole, a stepped hole is refused, no centre-cutting requirement. Never chosen by Auto. Radial (cross) reaming refused by name.

title: fix(kernel): refuse far-off .sc body coordinates; fuzz the body decoder
body:
Stacked on PR 1464 (base `issue/1456-solidcraft-import`); retarget to `main` before 1464 merges.

## What changed
- `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::MAX_COORD_MM = 1e6` mm. After `native::decode`, the reader checks every vertex of the final body: a non-finite coordinate or one past ±1e6 mm is refused by name ("the final body's vertex i lies at ... past the 1e6 mm coordinate limit"). Before this, only the decoder's own bound (1e12) applied.
- New test binary `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_hostile.rs`. It splices edited or damaged bodies into the sample and fixes up the slice table, both SHA-256 digests and the CRC-32s, so each case reaches the body decoder:
  - `hostile_coordinates_are_refused_by_name`: covers 1e9, just past the limit, -5e7, and NaN/±inf/1e13 patched over a sentinel's f64 bytes. Each is refused, naming the final body.
  - `damaged_bodies_never_panic_or_hang`: 24 bodies with random byte flips, 0xFFFFFFFF length words or truncation, run under a 120 s bound. Every refusal must name the final body. Result: 0 panics, and 6 still import because the damage landed in metadata.
  - `a_deflate_entry_past_its_declared_size_is_cut_off`: 64 MiB of deflate output declared as 64 bytes is refused with "65 bytes, the directory says 64".
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1467-sc-reader-hardening.md` (why 1 km).

## Tests
`cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test solidcraft_hostile --test solidcraft_import`: 3 + 7 pass (Windows, debug, about 40 s each). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- Vertex tolerance is not checked again, because the record's validator already refuses anything outside (0, 1e3].
- For 1e13 the decoder's wording is "non-finite metadata", which is solidcore's text, not ours.
- No Linux or macOS run.

title: feat(fixtures): generate 3-jaw, 4-jaw and collet lathe chucks
body:
## What changed

First slice of #1442: lathe chucks generated as built-in fixture accessories.

- `camcraft_sim::chuck` (new): `JawChuck` (body diameter/length, through bore, grip diameter, jaw length/width/height) and `ColletChuck` (body, nose diameter/length, collet bore). Each builds closed steel shells (body annulus + 2..12 jaws, or nose over body) and validates its figures by name: non-finite, zero, negative or absurd sizes, a bore past the body, jaws reaching past the body or meeting each other, a collet bore past the nose, a nose wider than the body.
- `app::accessory`: three new kinds `three_jaw_chuck`, `four_jaw_chuck`, `collet_chuck` ("3-jaw chuck", "4-jaw chuck", "Collet chuck") with generic default figures; placed by the undoable `InsertAccessory`, resized by `SetAccessory`, one undo each.
- New placement `AccessoryPlacement::OnStock` (`accessory::chuck::fit_to_stock`): closes the chuck on the setup's round stock on its axis (jaw face at the stock's underside; a collet the nose length deeper). Square stock, no stock, or a non-chuck kind is refused by name.
- MCP `add_accessory`: the chuck kinds, their dimensions in the schema, and a `fit_to_stock` flag.
- The UI dialog lists the new kinds through `accessory::KINDS` and places them by pose (no UI code change).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1442-lathe-chuck-fixtures.md` (frame, conservative facetting, no mill refusal, chucks not `fixed`).

## How tested

- `camcraft-sim` `tests/lathe_chuck.rs`: `three_jaw_envelope_is_pinned`, `four_jaw_has_four_jaws_at_quarters`, `collet_envelope_is_pinned` (body diameter and length, jaw reach and height, nose, bore - by bounds and point containment), `jaw_chuck_nonsense_is_refused_by_name`, `collet_nonsense_is_refused_by_name`, `round_stock_fits_and_square_stock_is_refused`.
- `camcraft-app` `tests/lathe_chuck.rs`: `a_generated_chuck_is_steel_the_holder_law_reads` (an offset holder in the jaws is named and blocks the post), `the_same_holder_above_the_jaws_posts`, `a_chuck_fits_on_round_stock_and_refuses_by_name`.
- `tests/mcp_accessory.rs`: `lathe_chucks_are_placed_fitted_to_the_stock_and_undone_over_mcp`; `tests/builtin_accessory.rs` updated for the nine kinds.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green (sim suites 18 s, app suites 45 s). Clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. UI `fixture_accessory` lib tests: 6 passed.

## Not exercised

- The chucks' look in the viewport and the dialog in the running app were not seen; a screenshot is owed by the maintainer.
- No "Fit to the stock" toggle in the UI dialog yet; inside grip, stepped jaws, independent 4-jaw offsets, rpm limit, 4th-axis chuck on a mill, camcraft-mcp skill row: filed as #1468.
- Release lanes and pixel snapshots were not run.

title: feat(kernel): read a Solidcraft design's cached final body
body:
First part of issue 1456: the kernel-side reader for Solidcraft `.sc` designs. The app wiring is not in this PR (see "Not in this PR").

## What changed
- `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft(k, bytes, stop)` reads a `.sc` container and returns the cached **final body** as the same checked solidcore `StepSolid` the STEP reader hands out (mm, closed, positive volume), plus the design name, units and the writing app's version. It does not read parameters, sketches or feature history.
- It reads only a cache that is provably this document's: `solidcraft-container/1`, document `solidcraft/<n>` in `mm`, cache format `solidcraft-model-cache/8` (the sample) or `/10` (the published source), producer `solidcraft-truck-adapter/4`, kernel `solidcore`, SHA-256 of `document.json` and of `cache/bodies.bin` both matching the manifest. The final state follows Solidcraft's own published rule (the last feature not skipped).
- Refused by name: empty, not a ZIP, no end record, ZIP64, multi-disk, encrypted, a name listed twice, over 10,000 entries, an entry over its cap (container 4 KiB, manifest 32 MiB, parts 256 MiB), CRC-32 or length mismatch, a directory or data outside the file, an unknown method, an unknown container/document/cache version, another producer or kernel, inch (or any non-mm) units, no model cache, a **stale** cache (the document digest does not match), a payload digest mismatch, slices that overlap, leave gaps, run past or leave trailing data, a body run out of range, no evaluated feature, several bodies, a placed copy (assembly instance), a mesh body (`SCMESH01`), a bad magic, a body that does not decode. Entry names are only compared, never used as paths, and nothing is written to disk. A panic in the decoder or kernel is caught and reported; `stop` bounds the time.
- New modules in `crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/`: `zip.rs` (a bounded in-memory ZIP directory reader written from APPNOTE.TXT), `sha256.rs` (FIPS 180-4, pinned by the standard's vectors), `cache.rs` (the manifest, slices and final state), `mod.rs`. `solidcore_step::build_record` is split out of the STEP reader's `build` so both share the same checks (no behaviour change for STEP).
- Fixture: the maintainer's sample, `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (5 MB), marked binary in `.gitattributes`.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1456-solidcraft-import.md`.

## New dependency - needs the maintainer's yes
`camcraft-kernel` gains `flate2 = "1.1"` (deflate for the container) and the workspace's `serde_json`. flate2 1.1.10 is **already in Cargo.lock** (png, tiff, usvg and vtkio pull it), so nothing new is downloaded or built; the lockfile gains two lines (the kernel's two new edges). The `zip` and `sha2` crates were considered and dropped (see the decision file). No new `camcraft-*` edge.

## How tested
- `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import.rs` (Gate map: covers `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft`), 7 tests, all green in debug (~41 s):
  - `sample_imports_its_final_body_at_the_design_size`: body "Body1", design name, mm, volume > 0, and the exact box equals the design's parameters (d1 = 125 mm diameter, d2 = 85 mm height): [-62.5, 62.5] x [-62.5, 62.5] x [0, 85] within 1e-6; the stored-ZIP rebuild of the same parts imports too.
  - `not_a_container_is_refused`, `container_damage_is_refused`, `documents_we_cannot_read_are_refused`, `a_cache_that_is_not_this_documents_is_refused`, `a_bad_body_table_or_body_is_refused`: one corrupted copy per refusal above, built in the test, each asserting its message.
  - `damaged_files_never_panic_or_hang`: 48 seeded byte-mutations/truncations of the sample plus 16 manifest-text mutations, under a 120 s cancel bound: no panic, no hang.
- `solidcraft::sha256` unit test (FIPS vectors and padding edges).
- Unchanged STEP suites re-run for the `build_record` split: `step_import`, `corrupt_input`, `machining_mesh` - green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick` falls back to the whole workspace for a `Cargo.toml` change and does not include camcraft-kernel; I ran the kernel suites above instead (the only crate touched).

## Not in this PR / not exercised
- **No app wiring**: Model > Open filter, drag-and-drop list and the MCP tool. No crate depends on `camcraft-kernel` yet (the app imports through truck until 917 lands); the first app -> kernel edge belongs there. So nothing is reachable from the GUI or MCP, and there was **no hand test in the app**.
- **Finding, filed as 1463**: the machining mesh refuses this body at every chord tried (0.005-0.1 mm; deviation about 2.8x the tolerance). The refusal is the safe outcome, but the body cannot be machined until that is fixed, so the app wiring should wait for it or show that refusal.
- Multi-body designs, assembly instances, mesh bodies, non-mm designs and cache formats other than 8 and 10 are refused, not read.
- Release-mode and other OSes not run.

Changelog: none (kernel-side reader only, not reachable from the app yet)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: ci: post-merge batch gate on the self-hosted Linux runner
body:
Stacked on #1418 (merge it first). Its diff here includes #1418's commits until it merges; #1418 currently conflicts with main (not fixed here).

## What changed
- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: push to `main` + `workflow_dispatch` (input `ref`); `[self-hosted, linux]`; concurrency `post-merge-main`, cancel-in-progress; `cargo xtask gate batch` under `xvfb-run -a`; gate-logs + gate-output always uploaded; no token on disk during tests.
- Sharing with the cut: skips itself (green, notice) when a `cut.yml` run is queued/in progress or a same-repo `release/v*` PR is open (`.github/scripts/post-merge-skip.sh`). Chosen as the simplest rule that cannot starve a cut; the cut's release gate covers main then.
- Reporting (`.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh`, report job only, `issues: write`): one rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)`; red opens it (P1, source:agent, effort:low, area:build) or comments on the open one; green comments the sha and closes it. P0 when a failing step name matches golden|gcode|g_code|post (heuristic on binary names; follow-up: a real "posted output" tag).

title: fix(machines): split the built-in DNM 5700 into a 3-axis machine and a rotary-table variant
body:
Stacked on #1434 (the DNM travel fix, #1410): this branch is cut from `issue/1410-doosan-travel`, so its diff against `main` holds #1434's commit until that merges. The commit that belongs to this PR is the last one.

## What changed

The built-in DNM 5700 declared the catalog's *optional* 4th-axis table (`rot_a`) with no `nose_to_axis`, so the index-swing law (`posting_index_swing.rs`) refused every op on it, plain 3-axis work at A0 included. I took the issue's option 2 and invented no figure. The safety law is not touched.

- `assets/machines/doosan-dnm-3axis.mch` (new) is the built-in **"Doosan DNM 5700"**: the same catalog figures and #1410's strokes, with no A. A 3-axis job now posts.
- `assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch` keeps the A table and becomes the built-in **"Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table"**. Its `general.model` was renamed to match, so the program header reads `(Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table)`. It still states no `nose_to_axis`, so every op on it is refused by name until the setup states its own (`SetSetupNoseToAxis` / MCP `set_setup_nose_to_axis`).
- `posting::MACHINES` lists both. This follows the `Tormach 770MX` / `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4` precedent.
- Old projects: a project file embeds its mounted machine, so a project saved on the old "Doosan DNM 5700" keeps its A table and refuses exactly as before. Remounting the built-in gives the 3-axis machine.
- The A-table file keeps its path, so the post tests, conformance, `doosan_dnm_a_state` and `program_units` read it unchanged. Only the library name and the header changed in `fourth_axis_pose.rs`, `machine.rs` (catalog pin) and `doosan_dnm_post.rs` (header assert).
- Docs: the rotary table in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/_index.md`. Decision: `docs/decisions/1433-dnm-3axis-split.md`.

No new command, so no MCP tool is owed.

Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs`:
- `a_plate_contour_on_the_built_in_dnm_passes_the_stroke_and_posts`: the plain DNM has no rotary, the verification report is empty, and `post_setup` succeeds. Before this change, the test asserted that the nose refusal was the only problem.

title: fix(ui): browser build saves, posts as downloads and greys the file commands it cannot run
body:
## What changed

In the browser (wasm) build the File commands did nothing: every picker went through `file_dialog.rs`, whose wasm half answers "cancelled" and only logs why. Now:

- **Save, Save As and Post download.** The app layer gains `project::save_text` and `posting::post_setup_unwritten` - the same collect, the same gate and engine run, bytes held in memory. The desktop's `save` / `post_setup` now call them and write the result, so the two cannot drift. The UI hands the bytes to the browser (`crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs`: `Blob` + `URL.createObjectURL` + a hidden `a[download]` click, through `eframe::web_sys`; no new dependency). Save As asks for the name with `window.prompt`. A downloaded document is marked clean; the unsaved prompt's Save downloads too. A refused post offers nothing and opens the refusal window, as on the desktop.
- **Everything else is refused by name and visibly disabled.** `browser_files::refusal` is the one table: opening anything (model, project, fixture, machine, post, theme, tool library, tool body) needs the browser file picker (#31, PR #1314); recent files, the fixture library folder and the per-operation folder post cannot exist in a page; setup sheet / tool list / stock STL / tool library exports are not downloads yet (#1437). `State::run` refuses those on the status line before anything else; ribbon cells (Model, Project, Post when per-op) are darkened with the reason as their tip; page buttons are greyed with the reason as their hover text. Context-menu rows and the theme dropdown's Browse row refuse on the status line only.
- `State::browser_build` (set from `cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32")`) carries the law, so the native tests drive it.

Inventory of every dialog call site and what the browser did: issue comment on #1431. Decisions: `docs/decisions/1431-wasm-file-commands.md`.

**Not stacked on PR #1314** (a contributor's fork branch). The open paths stay owed to it; when it lands, its commands come off `browser_files::refusal`. Hence `Refs #1431`, not `Fixes`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/unwritten_post.rs`: `the_unwritten_post_is_the_written_program_byte_for_byte`, `the_unwritten_post_refuses_where_the_written_one_does`, `save_text_is_the_saved_project_file` - 3 passed.
- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` unit tests: `every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_download_name_is_one_clean_segment_with_its_extension`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_files.rs` (structural): `the_ribbon_darkens_open_in_the_browser_and_says_why`, `open_in_the_browser_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `save_downloads_the_project_text_and_marks_the_document_clean`, `post_downloads_the_gated_program_and_a_refusal_offers_nothing`, `a_per_op_post_is_refused_in_the_browser_and_the_cell_says_why`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser` - 8 passed with the unit tests.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 673 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test coolant` and the project file suites touched by `save_text`: 7 and 73 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The real browser: no wasm build was loaded in a browser; the download (`Blob` / anchor click), `window.prompt` and the greyed controls are unseen on the page. **Screenshots are owed for the maintainer** (the File ribbon and the greyed page buttons look different on wasm) before `/merge-ready` offers this PR.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` did not get past `flecs_ecs_sys` (its C build finds no `assert.h` without the wasm sysroot `web/build-app-wasm.sh` sets up), so the `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` half of `browser_files.rs` (the `web_sys` Blob / anchor / prompt calls) is not compiled here. The wasm build at the next cut (or `web/build-app-wasm.sh`) is its first compile.

Changelog: Browser build: Save and Save As download the project, Post downloads the NC program, and file commands the browser cannot run yet are greyed with the reason instead of doing nothing (#1431)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Refs #1431

title: fix(turning): a new Facing faces the stock allowance down to the part's top
body:
## What changed

A new lathe Facing, whether created by MCP `add_operation` (`operation::seed_params`) or the GUI quick-add (`quick_params`), took its heights from the mill fold. That gave `top_z` = Top of Model and the facing plane `bottom_z` = Bottom of Model (the #214 floor). `turning::facing` then laddered from z 0 up to the part's top: it cut the part away and never touched the allowance above it.

- `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` `seed_facing`: the seed now states its own heights, the same way it already overrides the stepdown. `top_z` = Top of Stock + 0, and `bottom_z` (the facing plane) = Top of Model + 0. Both new-op paths retype the same Face draft, so both get these heights. Retyping an existing op into a Facing gets them too.
- `crates/app/src/operation/heights_sel.rs` `depth_sane`: a part already at length (stock top == part top) makes the window level. The heights door used to refuse this as "must cut downward: its top height resolves below its bottom height", which is wrong for a level window. A Facing now passes a level window, as Face already does. `generate` then refuses by name: `nothing to face - the facing plane stands at or above the top of both the part and its stock`. This is the generator's existing `GenError::Empty`, so no new status was needed. A top below the plane is still refused by the door.
- `docs/decisions/1409-face-seed-heights.md` records the decision.

The verify wording note from the issue is not changed. The 0.8 mm saturation of `gouge_mm` is shared by every envelope kind, so rewording it is not a trivial change. Verify semantics are untouched.

## Pins (each mutation-checked)

New suite `crates/app/tests/turning_face_seed.rs` runs the issue's repro over the MCP server: `lathe.mch`, an r 10 × 48 bar as STL, 20 × 50 cylinder stock, `TN-1600-0R8`, then `add_operation` facing.

| Pin | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `a_seeded_facing_faces_the_allowance_not_the_part`: generate gives `ok`; verify gives `findings == []` and `ok`; fanuc-lathe posts the passes `G01 X-1.6` at exactly Z50, 49.5, 49, 48.5, 48 | seed back to `c.top` / `c.bottom` | red: verify findings not empty (the issue's gouge and rapid-in-stock) |
| `the_facing_seed_runs_from_the_stock_top_to_the_part_top` (`seed_params`) | same | red |
| `ui::egui_app::fresh_op_tests::a_quick_add_facing_runs_from_the_stock_top_to_the_part_top` (`quick_params`, and asserts it equals `seed_params`) | same | red |
| `turning::the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar`: reworked to go through the real `seed_params` instead of a hand-built `Carried` with fixed 16/14 heights; asserts stepdown 0.5 and that no CL point sinks below the part top's tangency | same | red |
| `a_seeded_facing_on_a_part_at_length_reports_nothing_to_face` (50 → 48 stock): generate errs with "nothing to face" | remove the Facing arm in `depth_sane` | red: `add_operation` refused ("must cut downward") |

After each mutation the code was restored and every pin was green again.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 58be8266: green. App: lib, heights_selection, plasma_profile, probe_op, probe_search, ribbon, shoulder_adaptive, sinker_burn, sinker_side, tool_law, trochoid_op, turning, turning_face_seed, wire_contour. UI: lib, boundary, boundary_picks, theme_files.
- Extra turning, post and MCP suites, all green: lathe_field_sim, lathe_post, lathe_post_css, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_inch, lathe_post_tormach, lathe_post_tormach_thread, lathe_workholding_kinds, lathe_workholding_mill_post, tormach_lathes, turning_face_approach, turning_stock_approach, sim_lathe_body, setup_mounts_post, post_serves_kind, project_roundtrip, tool_cutting_rows, mcp_cutting, mcp_pick, mcp_verify. These include the fanuc_lathe_inch goldens (lathe_post_inch) and the Tormach lathe goldens.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. camcraft-motion is untouched.

## Goldens

No golden CL/NC files changed. The lathe golden and post suites build their Facing params explicitly, so they do not go through the seed. No snapshot PNGs touched.

## Not exercised

- The GUI quick-add was not clicked in the running app. It is pinned at `quick_params`, which is the function the ribbon action calls.
- No hand test in PathPilot Hub.

title: fix(sim): read a turning nose path's hidden rest as the turned work sees it
body:
## What was wrong

A lathe Facing that only faces the end of a bar was refused at the post when the bar had a groove anywhere along it (#1408). The finish-envelope verdict (law f) reported the groove as the Facing's rest. The cause is in the scan's hidden-rest half, which measures every Z-occluded top against the nearest nose centre:

1. **The scan never turned the work.** The groove floor's rim across the spindle, at (-r, 0, z_floor), was read against a path written in the y = 0, x >= 0 meridian. The issue's figures (17.05 / 10.28 / 15.56) are exactly that distance.
2. **Once turned, the near side was still 14 mm below the faced band.** No nose of the Facing travels that far down the spindle.

The Profile half (austin62jake's comment) shares cause 1: 12.49 / 12.76 on the shaft. Once the work turns, two smaller readings remain. Neither is rest the op owes:

- the groove floor's inner corner, which a 0.8 nose cannot reach (0.33 mm, `r(sqrt2 - 1)`);
- the Profile Rough's own 0.25 leave on the groove floor (0.287 on the shaft; 1.06 on the 2 mm near-top groove, which the rough plus its leave cannot enter).

The visible (ridge) half already lets both stand. They reached the hidden half only through Z-occlusion, and Z-occlusion means nothing to a tool that comes in radially.

## The fix

- `VerifyContext::lathe_axis` (new, default `None`): the spindle a turning nose op's kernel fitted. `operation::turning_axis::lathe_axis_of` sets it for every `Family::Turn` op whose tool states a nose radius, by the same `turning::Frame::about` reading the lathe sim uses. A source no axis fits gets `None`.
- `stock_sim::envelope_scan_turned(facets, moves, r, tol, (axis, leave))` (`envelope_scan_centers` is now `(None, 0.0)` of it). Law (f) passes `cx.lathe_axis` and `cx.stock_to_leave` for nose-centre paths.
- `stock_sim::scan_turned` (new, 174 lines) changes only the hidden-rest half, with four clauses:
  1. **The work turns.** Each hidden top is read at itself and at its two turns into the path's meridian plane. Every sample lies on the top's orbit, so the reading can only be at or above the true orbit distance. It may over-read (a refusal) but never hides rest, even on a path that leaves its plane.
  2. **The band.** A top farther along the spindle than every nose centre, by more than the nose plus the scan floor plus the arcs' bulge, is excused.
  3. **The crease.** A top the nose cannot touch is excused. This uses the ridge law's own accessibility test (`ridge::Access::reachable`, the tangent ball along the normal).
  4. **The leave.** A rough's `stock_to_leave` is its promise, and the crease test reads the ball grown by the leave.
- Gouge half, visible half and every mill path are unchanged. Without a spindle the scan is bit for bit the old one; this is pinned.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1408-turned-envelope-hidden-floor.md`. It covers why this is not a switch to `Mode::Revolve` (that is the blade's boxcar law, and the registry already keeps the nose kinds on law f), why the axis is not world Z, and why the hidden half is kept.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/turning_hidden_floor.rs` builds the issue's 64-segment bars on a lathe document with d20 x 50 stock and TN-1600-0R8, and runs them through `posting::post_script` with `fanuc-lathe.cps`:

- `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`: groove, groove near the top, shaft. Facing posts.
- `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post`: shaft. Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish are clean, and the program is written.
- `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`: groove and groove near the top, with Facing, Rough and Finish.
- `bars_without_a_groove_post_as_before`: plain and stepped post (stepped with Rough and Finish). The bar wider at the free end has no findings.
- `a_facing_that_gouges_the_grooved_bar_still_blocks_by_name`: Facing plane at 47. The `Envelope` warning carries a gouge over 0.5 mm, and the post is refused with "post blocked ... F2 ... finish envelope".

`crates/sim/tests/turned_hidden_rest.rs`:

- `a_groove_floor_under_the_facing_band_is_not_its_rest`: the unturned scan reads more than 15 mm; the turned scan reads at or under the gate; the gouge half is bit-identical.
- `a_hidden_floor_the_nose_could_reach_inside_its_band_still_convicts`: a nose that rides the OD past the 3 mm groove inside its own band reads more than 3 mm of rest, with leave 0 and with leave 0.25.
- `without_a_spindle_the_scan_is_the_old_one_bit_for_bit`
- `law_f_still_blocks_a_real_rest_and_a_real_gouge_by_name`: through `verify` with `lathe_axis` set, both a real rest and a real gouge give a blocking `finish envelope` warning.

Also `scan_turned` unit tests: the band/orbit geometry, and a path on the axis or non-finite.

## Mutation check (standing rule: each new excuse and guard deleted gives RED, restored gives GREEN)

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| M1 delete the band excuse | sim `a_groove_floor_under_the_facing_band_is_not_its_rest`, `law_f_still_blocks_...`; app `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`, `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M2 delete the orbit (turned) reading | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M3 delete the nose-accessibility (crease) excuse | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M4 leave not forgiven (`leave = 0.0`) | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M5 crease test on the bare nose, not nose + leave | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves` |
| M6 app passes no spindle (`lathe_axis: None`, i.e. the pre-fix verdict) | app `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`, `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| restored | all 4 sim + 5 app tests GREEN |

The two "still blocks" tests are guards against over-excusing: they stay green under every deletion above, by design.

## Goldens

No golden changed. Paths are untouched (only the verdict reads differently), and every app `turning*` and `lathe*` suite passed with a clean tree after it (39 suites, `lathe_post` goldens included).

## Gates

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` on every `turning*` / `lathe*` suite: 39 suites, all ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test turned_hidden_rest` and `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test turning_hidden_floor`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 25.5 min wall (sim 184 s, motion 6 s, app 1209 s, ui 130 s; 0 failed)

## Not exercised

- Boring, Chamfer, Taper and Multi-Pass also get the spindle (same `Family::Turn` + nose door). Their suites pass, but no new fixture puts a groove under them.
- A groove the nose fits but the insert's trailing geometry cannot enter is still judged as reachable. This errs toward refusing.
- The MCP repro was not re-run through `camcraft-cli`. The app tests drive the same commands and the same post gate.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 54); this branch is cut from upstream/main 3f6ecb4a.

Changelog: A lathe Facing (and the Profile kinds) on a grooved bar is no longer refused at the post: the envelope verdict reads hidden floors as the turning work sees them, out-of-band, nose-unreachable and leave-covered tops excused; a real gouge or owed rest in the op's own band still blocks (#1408)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1408

title: fix(slice): section touching or stacked solids as their union
body:
## What changed

`testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` laid flat could not be machined by 3D Finish or 3D Pocket. Both were refused with "invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = ...: non-manifold contact".

**Cause.** The model is three closed solids. Two of them are stacked so that, laid flat, their cylindrical walls overlap in Z (1.5875 .. 3.175) on the same vertical seam lines. Every plane in that band meets both outlines at the same 93 points, with four chords at each. Those chords run the same way and are subdivided differently, so welding coincident chords would not apply. `slice()` needs exactly two chords per end, so it refused, and `from_slice` reported the refusal as a parameter error.

**Fix** (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice_bodies.rs`, new):
- `slice()` keeps its plain read. Only when that read returns `NonManifold` does it retry as the union of the soup's closed solids:
  - the facets are split into bodies by shared-edge connectivity (corners welded within 0.1 um, spatial hash);
  - the retry runs only when every body is a closed, consistently wound 2-manifold with positive signed volume;
  - each body is then sliced on its own and the sections are united with the 2D boolean union. This is the same law `material_above_of` already applies to bodies from separate entities (M13.11).
- Everything else keeps the refusal:
  - solids welded along a shared edge or face (they share it four ways, so they read as one non-manifold shell);
  - an open body;
  - an inward cavity shell (sliced alone it would read as material, and the union would fill the cavity).
- A mesh that sliced before never reaches the fallback, so every existing CL/G-code golden is untouched by construction.
- The refusal is reworded to name the model and the fix: "the model's surfaces meet 3 or more ways at z = ... (non-manifold contact: solids welded along a shared edge or face, or a shell touching itself) - repair the mesh, or keep each solid a separate closed shell".
- New `GenError::Model`: the app and motion `from_slice` maps send `Open` and `NonManifold` there, so the message reads "the source model cannot be sliced: ..." instead of "invalid machining parameters: ...".
- `material_above_of` and `material_overhead_of` move with the fallback into `slice_bodies.rs` and are re-exported from `slice`. `slice.rs` goes from 466 to 423 lines.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1407-shared-face-slice.md`. Sources: Requicha 1980 (sections of a regularized union), Botsch et al. 2010 (closed oriented 2-manifold test), Zhang & Chen 2001 (signed volume), Teschner et al. 2003 (spatial-hash weld).

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs`
  - `the_sample_laid_flat_generates_3d_finish_and_pocket_with_no_gouge`: the issue's MCP job, laid flat. Both R1 and S1 now report `status: ok`, the program gate (stock sim) is `ok` with no gouge, and every finish-envelope gouge reading is under 0.01 mm.
  - `the_laid_flat_band_sections_as_the_union_of_the_solids`: every plane in z 1.60 .. 3.15 sections, wider than the lower solid alone, and the islands law reads it.
  - `the_sample_as_imported_still_sections_on_the_plain_read`: 240 planes over the as-imported span all slice.
  - `welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault`: two blocks welded along one edge, through 3D Pocket. Refused with "the source model cannot be sliced ... non-manifold", and never "invalid machining parameters".
  - `the_sample_as_imported_still_generates_both_operations`: `#[ignore]`, heavy lane. The as-imported job spans 118 mm of Z and takes over 15 min in debug.
- `crates/geometry/tests/slice_bodies.rs`: stacked solids, solids touching along a face, welded shared edge still refused (with the new wording), inward cavity shell refused (not filled), open solid refused, nanometre seam drift still welds.
- `crates/motion/tests/islands_model_fault.rs`: `machining3d::material_above` returns `GenError::Model` for the welded soup and the union for stacked solids.

Mutation checks (STANDING RULE). Each line was deleted or changed, the pinning tests went RED, then it was restored and they went GREEN:

| Mutation | RED tests |
|---|---|
| M1: drop the fallback call in `slice()` | stacked, touching, drift (geometry); laid-flat band and laid-flat generate (app) |
| M2: drop the closed/consistent edge guard | `a_soup_with_an_open_solid_is_refused` |
| M3: drop the outward (positive volume) guard | `a_soup_with_an_inward_cavity_shell_is_refused_not_filled` |
| M4: weld tolerance 1e-4 -> 1e-12 mm | `nanometre_seam_drift_still_reads_closed_solids`, laid-flat band, laid-flat generate |
| M5: restore the old refusal wording | `solids_welded_along_a_shared_edge_are_still_refused` |
| M6: drop the app `from_slice` Model map | `welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault` |
| M7: drop the motion `from_slice` Model map | `a_welded_non_manifold_soup_is_refused_as_a_model_fault` |

All restored: geometry 6/6, app 4/4 (+1 ignored), motion 2/2.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, which falls back to batch for a geometry change) on head `6726c1b8`: green except the ui step, where `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` died with SIGSEGV under 6 test threads. These are the software-GPU (`headless_gpu`) suites, and this diff touches no ui or trace code. Re-run on the same binaries with `--test-threads=1`, they pass: 5/5 and 4/4. Steps: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app suites ok (app 1194 s); clippy ok; wall 31.7 min. Clippy `-D warnings` on geometry, motion, app and ui: clean.

Goldens: none changed. The fallback only runs where the old code refused.

## Not exercised / left open

- On the laid-flat sample, the finish envelope's **rest** half still holds S1's post: "finish envelope near move 2728: 0.0081 mm gouge, 4.5756 mm rest". The gouge reading is under the gate; the rest is the steep walls a parallel finish leaves. The same finding appears on the body pairs that never needed the union (bodies 0+2: 3.17 mm rest; bodies 1+2: 3.17 mm), so it is how 3D Finish behaves on this geometry, not something this fix introduced. The post is held, never silently passed.
- The heavy as-imported generation test was not run here.
- `GenError` gains a variant. One exhaustive match in a test (`motion/tests/ruling.rs`) was updated.

Changelog: 3D Finish and 3D Pocket machine a model made of stacked or touching closed solids (such as the sample STEP laid flat) as their union; genuine non-manifold meshes are refused as a model fault, not as invalid machining parameters (#1407)

Effort: high (no escalation). Branched from upstream/main 3f6ecb4a; fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 54.

Fixes #1407

title: ci: cut pipeline - release gate on a self-hosted Linux runner, then tag and release
body:
## What changed

A **Cut** pipeline that runs the release gate tier on the self-hosted Linux runner and then **triggers the existing `release.yml`** for the tag. It does not replace `release.yml`: that file is unchanged (its jobs, runners and publishing as they are). It already has a `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so not even a trigger had to be added.

- **`.github/workflows/cut.yml`** (new). Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only. Inputs: `version` (X.Y.0), `stage` (`gate` | `tag`) and `dry_run`. Every job is `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`. `concurrency: cut` allows one cut at a time and never cancels a running one.
  - `stage: gate` runs before the release PR merges. It checks out `release/vX.Y.0` with `persist-credentials: false`, so no token is on disk while tests run. It refuses a branch whose `Cargo.toml` or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` doesn't name the version, or whose tag already exists. Then it runs `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`, inside `xvfb-run -a` when there is no display. It always uploads `gate-logs/` and `gate-output.txt` as an artifact and writes the gate summary to the job summary. When green and not a dry run, it uploads the tested commit as `cut-tip-vX.Y.0`. It tags nothing.
  - `stage: tag` runs after the release PR merged. It finds the newest green gate run for the version and takes its tip. It refuses unless main's head `m` is the release PR's merge of that tip (`m^2 == tip`), `git diff $tip $m` is empty (AGENTS.md step 4's rule, kept), the tag is free on origin and `Cargo.toml` names the version. It then runs `git tag -a vX.Y.0 $m`, pushes the tag, and runs **`gh workflow run release.yml --ref vX.Y.0`** with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A tag pushed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow by itself; a `workflow_dispatch` from it does. On a tag ref, release.yml's `publish` and `pages` see `refs/tags/...` exactly as they do on a pushed tag. Only this job has `contents: write` and `actions: write`.
  - `dry_run`: the gate stage prints its plan (`--dry-run`); the tag stage runs every check and stops before the tag and the dispatch.
- **xtask**: `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots` is the release plan without the two pixel-snapshot lanes (`--lib --ignored snapshot` and `--test gpu_render --ignored snapshot`). The flag is refused on any other tier. Pinned by `release_without_snapshots_drops_only_the_pixel_lanes`.
- **AGENTS.md**:
  - the release tier entry in the gate tiers list
  - "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted": self-hosted jobs bill nothing, triggers stay `workflow_dispatch`, no fork-triggerable trigger on a self-hosted workflow, and the billed minutes of one cut, with a placeholder to fill in from the first real cut
  - new "The cut runner" section: requirements, registration and safety, written generically with no host-specific names
  - cut steps 2-4 and "Every cut tag is published"
  - the local cut stays as the fallback when the runner is down
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`** 54 -> 55 (process files: AGENTS.md, xtask). The final number is settled at merge.
- **`docs/decisions/1413-cut-pipeline.md`**: the decisions below.

## Open questions settled (details in the decision file)

- **Where the tag is made.** The gate runs on the release branch tip before the release PR merges, so a red gate leaves no untagged release on main. A second dispatch (`stage: tag`) after the merge checks `m^2 == tip` and that `git diff $tip $m` is empty, then tags. The empty-diff rule is kept and is now machine-checked.
- **Windows-only pinned readings** (issue 1402's per-OS move counts). The Linux gate checks only the Linux arm. A local Windows check stays **optional** at a cut, named in step 2. If nobody runs it, the Windows arm drifts until the next Windows run, and the release PR says it was skipped.
- **UI snapshot lane on Linux.** Skipped on Linux (`--no-snapshots`) and kept as a local Windows step at the cut. The goldens are Windows renders, and a GPU-less Mesa render would differ in pixels every cut, or need a second set of goldens kept in step. Their structural twins still run in the ui suites on Linux.
- **Version bump, zip, installer.**
  - The bump stays local on the release branch: `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.0 --no-tag --skip-gate`.
  - `release.yml` already builds the published zip, installer and packages from the tag, and nothing about that changes.
  - The local zip and installer are now a hand-test build only.
  - The installer stays Windows-only, in release.yml's Windows job.

## Runner (already registered)

AGENTS.md lists the requirements generically: Linux x64, labels `self-hosted`/`Linux`/`X64`, disk of at least 100 GB, the toolchain on the service PATH, `git` and `gh`, the build packages from release.yml's linux job, `xvfb` plus Mesa software drivers, and sccache configured in `.env` with no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It also gives the `config.sh` registration and the service setup. **Runner prerequisite to check:** `gh`, `xvfb` and the Mesa and dev packages must be installed on the box. The workflow can't install them, because the runner has no sudo.

## How tested

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 (release binary in a scratch dir, sha256 checked against the release's checksums file, not added to the repo): clean on `cut.yml` and every other workflow. shellcheck was not installed, so the `run:` scripts were not shellchecked.
- YAML parse (Ruby Psych): trigger `workflow_dispatch` only; inputs `version`, `stage`, `dry_run`; jobs `gate` and `tag`, both `[self-hosted, linux]`.
- `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots --dry-run`: 12 steps, namely every debug suite (kernel included), ui, clippy, and the motion and app heavy lanes, with no snapshot lane.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: xtask unit tests 90 passed, 1 failed. The one failure is `gate_maps_tests::no_gate_map_names_a_moved_module_as_app`, which **already fails on a clean upstream/main 3f6ecb4a** (ten test headers name moved modules as `app::`), so this PR did not cause it. Filed as #1417. With that test skipped, all 90 pass, including `release_without_snapshots_drops_only_the_pixel_lanes`, `batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` and `cli_parses_the_gate_forms`.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No product Rust code changed.

## Not exercised: maintainer's post-merge check

A workflow can only be dispatched once it is on the default branch, so **no real run happened**: not the runner, not xvfb or the UI suites under it, not the artifact hand-off between stages, not the tag push or the release.yml dispatch. After merge, run in this order:

1. `gh workflow run cut.yml -R NeoTech/Camcraft -f version=<test X.Y.0> -f stage=gate -f dry_run=true` checks the runner picks the job up and prints the plan (it needs a `release/v<test>` branch whose Cargo.toml and RELEASE_NOTES.md name the version).
2. The same command without `dry_run` runs the real gate. Expect about 75 min or less. It should prove the UI suites pass under xvfb. A deliberately red commit on the scratch branch should also make no tag (step 3 refuses, since there is no green gate run).
3. After the scratch release PR merges (or on a throwaway fork): `gh workflow run cut.yml -R NeoTech/Camcraft -f version=<test> -f stage=tag -f dry_run=true`, then the same command without `dry_run`. Check that the tag lands on the merge commit and that release.yml starts on the tag and attaches its artifacts to the GitHub release. Then fill in AGENTS.md's "measured cut" placeholder from that run's Usage. Branch protection and tag rulesets must allow `github-actions[bot]` to push tags.

Changelog: none
Effort: high (no escalation)
`.github` change: expected to get `needs-maintainer` at review.

Fixes #1413
