title: feat(pick): circle and arc centres as opt-in feature points
body:
The last part of #692 still owed: arc and circle centres from a round feature edge, offered as **feature points** only where a picker asks for them. Branched from upstream `main` at 8174f37d (the newest tag reachable from it is v0.18.0).

## What changed
- **Pick service (`crates/app/src/pick/`)**
  - New `centre.rs` with `centre_selection`, `centre_of` and `centre_point`. A centre pick is stored as the round run it comes from (`FeatureSel::Chain(run)`) and read back through #759's `circle_of_run`. A straight or non-circular run is refused by name, wrapping `CircleRefusal`.
  - `selection_of` now maps a `Centre` target to that run. Before, it returned `None`.
  - `circle_centre_in` is `circle_centre` with the frame passed in, so point slots can read the centre in the document frame.
  - **Visibility:** a centre is offered when its *edge* is in sight. Up to 8 segment midpoints around the run are tested; the centre's own position is not. Pick-through works as before.
  - **Snap sort:** ray distance is compared to the nanometre, so two centres stacked on one axis tie and the nearer one wins. Before, float noise could pick the far rim.
- **Opt-in, not a global change:** `PickKinds::ALL` still leaves centres out. In `feature_click::ask` only two pickers ask for them: the three-points draft (in Vertex mode) and an axis by two points. The plain pick modes, the plane row, an axis by edge, fixture locate and the WCS role draft never snap to a centre.
- **Point slots:** `pick::points` (three points) and `pick::axis` (a pair of points) read a circular edge chain as its centre and refuse any other edge by name. `points_pick::take` and `axis_pick::take` accept a centre and refuse a straight edge with the reason. The axis readout shows a centre as a point.
- **MCP:** `lay_part_on_points` and `set_part_axes` (point pairs) accept a circular-edge chain id for its centre, through the same functions. Tool descriptions and the camcraft-mcp skill rows are updated. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes from 54 to 55 (a process file changed; settled at merge).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/692-centre-points.md`. It records why there is no new `FeatureSel` variant and no `centre:` id form.

## Pins (each one was mutation-checked: guard removed, test red, guard restored)
| Pin | Test | Mutation |
|---|---|---|
| A round edge gives its centre when the picker opts in | `centre_pick::a_round_edge_yields_its_centre_when_the_picker_opts_in` | `selection_of` Centre -> `None`: red |
| A picker that doesn't opt in never gets a centre | `centre_pick::a_picker_that_does_not_opt_in_never_gets_a_centre`, ui `vertex_pick_tests::only_the_point_takers_that_read_a_centre_ask_for_centres` | centre tier also offered for points/edges: red; `ask` opt-in line removed: ui red |
| A straight edge is refused by name | `centre_pick::a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name` | straight check in `circle_of_run` removed: red |
| A hidden round edge's centre: not offered with Pick-through off, offered with it on (ortho and perspective) | `centre_pick::a_hidden_round_edge_offers_its_centre_only_when_picking_through` | edge-visibility check replaced by `true`: red |
| The MCP centre pick goes through the same service and refuses by name | `centre_pick::mcp_point_picks_take_a_round_edge_centre_and_refuse_a_straight_one_by_name`, `centre_pick::three_points_read_a_round_edge_as_its_centre` | `centre_point` guard in `pick::points` removed: red |

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran 20 app suites (pick, align, MCP align/setup/WCS, fixture locate and others) and the ui lib.
- The full ui lib run single-threaded from `crates/ui`: 663 passed.

title: fix(post): floor a capped lathe C-section feed word that rounds over its cap
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, the C-axis live-tool G01 (`liveMove`):

- **#1392, the floored word.** The cap is kept as its own value (`capF`, from #1395's prelude `rotaryFeedCap(Infinity, ...)`), and F goes through `capWord(v, cap)`. It returns `fm(v)` unless that word is over the cap; then it floors the word to the 0.1 step at or under the cap. No tolerance: flooring without one is only ever on the safe side.
- **#1398, posted words.** The cap is measured between the words the control reads. X is read back from its rounded diameter word, Z origin-relative at 0.001, C at 0.001. This is the same rule as `rotaryFeed`'s `q()`/`org` for the mills (#1395). Before, it was measured on the unrounded points, and a short move that rounded longer could drive X/Z about 7% over the maximum feed. The planned F is still scaled by the raw composite length, so feeds away from their cap post byte-identically.
- **F0 refused.** A word under the 0.1 mm/min step is refused by name and not written. One refusal covers a machine-rate cap that floors to F0, another a planned feed that small.
- Merged upstream/main (#1395 rewrote `liveMove`). The merge keeps #1395's `rotaryFeedCap` and every #1395 refusal, as M3 resolved it in review.
- Feeds away from their cap post byte-identically. **No recorded or golden program changed.**

## How tested
- `crates/post/tests/lathe_live_feed_cap.rs`, 8 tests:
  - the 4 #1392 floor tests;
  - `a_capped_move_is_judged_on_its_posted_words` (M3's probe, X20.001 -> X20.008, C30 -> C30.01; rates recomputed from the posted words stay within fmax and the C rate, for both the fmax-binding and the C-binding machine);
  - `an_off_lattice_stream_is_judged_on_its_posted_words` (C, and Z with an off-step origin, rounding differently from the raw point);
  - `a_cap_that_floors_under_the_f_step_is_refused_by_name` (M3's probe: C rate 0.05, a 90 degree turn, planned feed 50000);
  - `an_uncapped_feed_under_the_f_step_is_refused_by_name`.
- Mutation check: 13 mutants, every one RED, and GREEN once restored. The table is in the review-fix PR comment.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 433 passed, 0 failed.
- App suites `rotary_feed_cap`, `c_axis_fixture`, `c_axis_live` (golden), `c_axis_unwind`, `program_units`, `recorded_post_streams`, `conformance`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_g76`: all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green on 6a58d35b (post suites 3 s incl. lathe_live_feed_cap, 27 app suites 82 s, 0 failed)

## Not exercised
- Inch C sections: fanuc-lathe refuses them, so there is no inch path. The read-back still converts if that ever changes.
- A real control. How a Fanuc lathe handles the X-diameter rate needs a desk review or a tester.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1392-floor-capped-feed.md` (review note dated 2026-11-13).

Fork synced at v0.18.0; merged upstream/main 38699549.

body:
The actual STEP bore spent 277.759 s in its release import/generate/verify test on the frozen baseline. With this change repeated release/debug tests pass in 5.866/31.308 s. Observed bounds on this Linux i7-1360P are 15 s release and 40 s debug for the complete test, including every growth level; these are measured bounds, not universal real-time guarantees.

Simplify each growth opening's input at 0.25 um using iterative Ramer/Douglas-Peucker, erode an extra 0.51 um, and intersect the result with the original region. The intersection is the containment backstop; approximate simplification does not inherit the exact opening's nesting proof. Invalid simplifications or changed loop/hole counts fall back to the original outline. Load, travel and geometry budget limits and final path guards are unchanged.

Independent verification on Linux x86-64:

- Actual STEP bore: baseline 15561/14837/1561 moves/planar-feeds/arcs; candidate 16029/15372/1427 in release and debug. The first candidate run failed only the old exact-count pin after its safety checks; only the measured Linux triple is updated, and the repeated release test passes.
- Six planar adaptive fixtures pass: bore R12.5, rectangle and L-pocket unchanged; narrow slot stays HSM with 0 in-cut breaks, 14262 -> 14664 moves and 15.4 -> 15.7 % D load. Island and channel retain their named Offset rings fallbacks (100 % D and 42/40 breaks, existing fallback behavior, not HSM-law successes).
- All six rotary fixtures pass with no new fallback/refusal: bar's deepest band 18.4 -> 18.0 % D, window's deeper bands 18.4 % D, neck bands 17.3/17.7 % D; no in-cut break over 5 degrees. Fitted arcs/move counts change; the Offset rings digest is unchanged.
- Both annular-band refusal tests and all four motion stepped-pocket tests pass. Small-helix crossing regression passes. Seven new simplification tests pass in release/debug, including whole-region difference containment for acute notches, nearby components, thin walls/holes/nested islands, cyclic seams and degenerates. The 56 s debug growth-cost pin remains covered in the explicitly named heavy lane; the six defaults pass in 15.16 s.
- Motion/app clippy `--all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` pass (271 default tests, 12 ignored heavy, 51 s, no VOID). Full release adaptive-unit run passes: frozen baseline 45 tests in 314.244 s, candidate 52 in 244.970 s, including budget twins and twenty slot perturbations.

Full fixture count/load/break comparisons, commands, timing caveats and rejected alternatives are in the [decision record](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/issue/882-adaptive-opening/docs/decisions/882-adaptive-open-simplify.md). No safety thresholds are relaxed to accept a changed plan.

Limitations: Windows/macOS were not run; their previously measured exact STEP triples remain unchanged and need remeasurement on those platforms. Graphify is unavailable on PATH. No snapshot or golden files change.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, process version 52. The issue branch alone merges upstream main for the already-landed blockers; baseline tree equals upstream `4c229ed3`. Fork main stays on the released product baseline.

Changelog: adaptive ring opening avoids repeated fine-outline offsets while preserving containment and safety checks.
Effort: max; no escalation.

title: fix(wire): stamp the wire contour's side by its own value and an open run's clearance
body:
## What changed

`OpParams::stamp_with`, Wire Contour arm (`crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`): the side was written as `u8::from(side == Punch)`, so Die, Left and Right digested alike, and the run-out clearance was never written. An open run turned left <-> right, or given a new clearance, kept its stamp, so its old path (kerf on the side the user no longer states) read Ok and could post.

The side now writes its own discriminant, and an open run also writes its clearance:

| Side | Bytes written |
|---|---|
| Die | `0` (as before) |
| Punch | `1` (as before) |
| Left | `2`, then the clearance |
| Right | `3`, then the clearance |

**Existing stamps:** die and punch stamps are byte-identical to before, so no closed cut goes Stale on upgrade, and a closed cut's clearance (which it never reads) still moves nothing. An open (Left/Right) run generated before this change reads Stale once after load and clears on regenerate. That is the one-time churn every stamp change causes. No golden or roundtrip fixture pins a wire stamp value: no committed `.ccam`/JSON fixture holds a `wire_contour`, and `golden_cl` pins CL output, not stamps.

The change is limited to the one stamp arm, plus a new test file. Open wire PRs #1163, #1181 and #1218 touch or move the same arm (they add `taper_deg` next to it and keep the old `== Punch` byte). Whichever merges second keeps both changes.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/wire_stamp.rs`:
- `an_open_runs_side_and_clearance_each_mark_its_path_stale`: a generated open cut-off is saved, its side is turned (and, separately, its clearance re-stated) in the file, and it is reopened with its old path and stamp. It reads Stale in both cases. Through the commands, the edit reads Stale and undo reads Ok.
- `the_four_sides_stamp_apart_and_a_closed_cut_ignores_the_clearance`: all four sides give distinct `current_stamp`s. Die and punch ignore the clearance. Left and right read it.
- `an_unrelated_edit_and_a_round_trip_leave_the_cuts_ok`: another operation's edit, a closed punch's clearance re-stated in its file, and a plain save/load all leave the cuts Ok.

The first two tests fail on `upstream/main` without the fix (checked by reverting `params.rs`), and all three pass with it.

Suites run green: `wire_stamp`, `wire_contour`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_verify`, `project_roundtrip`, `operations`, `golden_cl`. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` both pass on the final head.

**Why the file door:** `EditOperationParams` drops the stamp on every edit, so an edit always reads Stale and cannot prove the digest. The paths that keep a stamp are a project file and the stored stamp it reloads, so the pin goes through the file.

## Not exercised

The GUI wire page, and a real EDM control.

Changelog: An open wire run edited left <-> right, or given a new run-out clearance, now reads Stale instead of keeping its old path (#1370)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at upstream PROCESS_VERSION 46); branch from upstream/main ebaceb1c.

Fixes #1370

title: fix(post): refuse a cut with the spindle stopped in every spindle mill dialect
body:
**Stacked on #1367** (branch `issue/1357-cycle-feed-spindle`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #1367 merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch merged with upstream main through #1367's branch.

## What changed
- **The spindle rule in every spindle mill dialect.** #1357 gave `tormach.cps` a spindle-state rule, and the #1367 review fixed its touch-probe exemption. That rule is now ported to `fanuc`, `haas`, `sinumerik`, `mazak`, `heidenhain`, `doosan-dnm`, `grblhal`, `tinyg` and `carvera`.
  - Each post tracks `spindleOn` from its preamble's spindle start (`S.. M3`; Mazak `MOTON S..`; Carvera `M3 S..`) to the next stop: every section end, and a touch probe's stop.
  - A feed, arc or canned cycle with the spindle stopped is refused by name and nothing is posted for it, e.g. `feed move G1 with the spindle stopped - no spindle start (S.. M3) precedes it; state the operation's spindle speed`. One message per program.
  - **Probe exemption:** the section must state 0 rpm **and** `PARAM ToolKind touch probe`. A cutter at 0 rpm, or a 0-rpm section that states no tool kind, is refused. The kind resets at every section end.
  - **tinyg and carvera** write no canned cycles; their holes are plain feeds, so the feed check covers holes.
  - **Heidenhain** checks its native cycle last, after the tapping refusals. A tap with no spindle speed keeps its own refusal ("tapping needs a positive integral spindle speed"). The cycle stays open, so the hole's chain is swallowed, not posted.
- **Exempt posts:**
  - `tormach-plasma` and `wire-iso` have no spindle.
  - `fanuc-lathe` and `tormach-lathe` do not share the mill pattern, and they already refuse a cut with no spindle speed their own way:
    - feed per rev (G99) needs a spindle speed;
    - fanuc-lathe's only feed-per-minute mode (G98, C-axis live tooling) needs a live-tool speed.
  - So no lathe post changed.
- **Fixtures:**
  - `conformance.rs` now posts every mill dialect's golden from `as_program` (`tests/common/legacy_program.rs`): tool change, spindle speed, setup/operation/tool comments and cycle feeds, on the same generic VMC. The pinned `.cl` files are untouched.
  - `legacy_program::operation_for` gains a `trochoid_` arm (6 mm end mill, "Trochoidal slot").
  - These hand-written streams gain a `SpindleSpeed`:
    - post crate: `fanuc_post`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `arc_planes`, `axis_direction_cli`;
    - app: `fourth_axis_pose`, `tinyg_post`.
  - `heidenhain_block_form` uses `as_program`, and so does `program_units`' grbl-family test, plus the `ClearancePlane` a real stream states (both posts lift to it at a tool change).
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/1359-spindle-rule-all.md`.

## Goldens moved: 115 files, regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`
**Only added lines.** Diffed with the N block numbers stripped, **0 lines were removed or changed** across all 115 files. The added lines are:
- the setup, operation and tool comments;
- the tool change, in each dialect's own form: `T.. M6` + `G43 H..`; Sinumerik `T.. D.. M6`; Heidenhain `T.. G17 S..`; Carvera `M6 T..`; TinyG `M5`/`M9`/lift/`T.. M6`/`M0`/frame restate;
- the spindle start: `S.. M3`, or Mazak `MOTON S..`, Carvera `M3 S..`, Heidenhain `M3`.

Heidenhain and Sinumerik renumber their N words.

- **fanuc** (top level, 14): contour_disc_hole, contour_plate_with_hole, contour_tangential_lead, drill_peck, drill_plate, face_square_40x40, face_square_40x40_stepped, pocket_waterline_plate_with_island, pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island, slot_fullwidth_centerline, slot_wide_channel_rows, tap_plate, trace_plate_with_hole, trochoid_slot_small
- **haas** (13): the 13 conformance goldens (the 13 above, without trochoid)
- **sinumerik** (13): the same 13
- **mazak** (13): the same 13
- **doosan-dnm** (13): the same 13
- **heidenhain** (12 changed + 1 new): the 12 without tap_plate changed. **`heidenhain/tap_plate.nc` is new.** That golden was a named refusal (`REFUSED`) only because the bare stream stated no spindle speed. With 500 rpm stated (the M10x1.5 tap: 750 mm/min over a 1.5 mm pitch) it posts G207, so its `REFUSED` entry is gone.
- **grblhal** (12), **tinyg** (12), **carvera** (12): the 12 without tap_plate. tap_plate stays refused by name there: no G84, or no spindle reverse.
- **tormach:** no golden moved.

## Pins: `crates/app/tests/post_spindle_rule_all.rs`, table-driven over the 9 dialects
- `a_feed_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`: refused once, and the same section with a spindle speed posts clean.
- `an_arc_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`
- `a_hole_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`: a canned cycle (Heidenhain: its drilling cycle; tinyg/carvera: the plunge feed). With a spindle it posts clean.
- `a_cutter_stating_zero_rpm_is_refused_and_a_touch_probe_is_not`: a cutter at 0 rpm and a 0-rpm section with no kind are refused; a touch probe at 0 rpm is exempt; a no-kind 0-rpm section after a probe section is refused again.
- `a_section_after_the_stop_that_states_no_speed_is_refused`

**Mutations** (the post file is edited and the pin binary re-run; every mutant is caught):

| Mutant | Fails |
|---|---|
| Rule off (`spindleStopped` never refuses), in each of the 9 posts, one at a time | all 5 pins, each time |
| fanuc: the cycle check dropped | the hole pin |
| heidenhain: the cycle check dropped | the hole pin |
| haas: the arc check dropped | the arc pin |
| mazak: exemption on 0 rpm alone (the pre-review Tormach bug) | the 0-rpm pin |
| grblhal: probe never exempt | the 0-rpm pin |
| sinumerik: the tool kind not reset at section end | the 0-rpm pin (the probe-then-no-kind case) |
| doosan-dnm: M5 not clearing `spindleOn` | the section-after-stop pin |
| tinyg: M3 not setting `spindleOn` | 3 pins |

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` at b0d50c6f is green: post suites ok, app suites ok (548 s).
- camcraft-post: all suites pass.
- App: `conformance`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `tinyg_post`, `fourth_axis_pose` and `golden_cl` pass. Before the merge of main, the whole camcraft-app test set (every binary) ran green after the two fixture fixes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The `--ignored` heavy lanes and the release-tier UI snapshot lane.
- **No controller run.** The changed goldens are for the generic VMC dialects, not the 770MX, so no Hub run applies.
- A mid-section `SpindleSpeed` change still takes effect only at the next preamble. This was pre-existing and is unchanged here.

Changelog: Every spindle mill post (Fanuc, Haas, Siemens 840D, Mazak, Heidenhain, Doosan DNM, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera) refuses a feed, arc or canned cycle with the spindle stopped by name; a touch-probe section is exempt only on a touch-probe tool.
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1359

title: test(app): read a reset or EOF as the idle drop in the trickling-client test
body:
What changed: in `a_trickling_client_is_dropped_on_the_idle_schedule` (crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs) the read after the idle deadline now accepts EOF, or ConnectionReset/ConnectionAborted/BrokenPipe, as the drop. When the idle note does arrive it is still asserted. A read timeout (client still connected past the schedule) still fails, as do the window timing asserts (>= 350 ms, < 1500 ms). No retries, no longer sleeps. Test code only; the server is untouched.

Cause: the server writes the idle note and closes while the trickler's bytes are still unread, so the kernel may send RST and discard the note; the client's read then returns ECONNRESET (errno 54 on macOS), which the test read as "never dropped".

Siblings: `an_idle_client_is_dropped_by_name_and_the_next_one_is_served` sends nothing, so no unread data and no reset; it already reads the post-note EOF with `unwrap_or(0)`. Unchanged. The other tests do not use this read.

Tested: whole `mcp_live` binary 20/20 with every core saturated by busy loops; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Not exercised: macOS (the reporting host).

Changelog: none
Effort: medium
Fixes #1366

title: fix(post): refuse a canned cycle with no feed and a Tormach cut with the spindle stopped
body:
## What changed

**Refusals (Prime Directive: refuse by name instead of posting something silently wrong)**
- **A canned cycle with no feed is refused by name.** If `FeedRate` is missing or not > 0, the post emits `canned cycle G73 has no feed rate - refused: ...` through the post's `msg()` / `refuse()` path and writes no G7x/G8x. This applies to every post that writes a cycle with its own F: `tormach`, `fanuc`, `haas`, `sinumerik`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `grblhal` and `fanuc-lathe`.
- **heidenhain** keeps its fallback to the hole chain's own feed (`ChainFeedRate`), but no longer falls back to the program's last modal feed. With neither feed, its existing "missing/invalid positive cutting feed" refusal fires.
- **tinyg, carvera and tormach-lathe** post drilling as plain chain moves with their own F, so they need no change.
- **`tormach.cps`: a cut with the spindle stopped is refused by name.** This covers G1, G2/G3 and canned cycles: `feed move G1 in operation X with the spindle stopped - no spindle start (S.. M3) precedes it; ...`.
  - `spindleOn` is true from the preamble's `S.. M3` to the next `M5`. Every section ends in M5, so a later section that states no speed is refused too.
  - A touch-probe section (a stated 0 rpm, #574) is exempt.
  - The other spindle mill posts get the same rule in follow-up **#1359** (P2, effort:high, area:post). Every one of their conformance goldens is a bare legacy stream with no spindle, so doing it here would move about 120 more goldens.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the new law.

**Goldens**
- The `.cl` goldens are generator outputs that `golden_cl.rs` pins, so they are not edited. Instead, the new `crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs` builds the streams the tests post:
  - `with_cycle_feeds`: each `; CYCLE` marker gets its own chain's cutting feed. This is what `post::dump` synthesizes for a generated cycle.
  - `as_program`: also prepends the records a real operation's stream carries: SetupName, OperationName, OperationKind, ToolKind, ToolDiameter, `TOOL`, `SpindleSpeed`.
  - The post crate's `fanuc_post.rs` and `arc_planes.rs` include the same file by path, so the shared `nc/*.nc` goldens come from one stream.
- **The Tormach goldens are runnable programs.** `conformance.rs` now posts the Tormach mill goldens for the **770MX** (`tormach-770mx.mch`, inch) instead of the generic `3axis-vmc.mch`. They now open `(Tormach 770MX)` and carry:
  - `(SETUP: Setup1)`, `(OPERATION: Drill1 - DRILL - G54)` and `(T4 6MM HSS DRILL - DRILL D0.2362)`;
  - `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30` / `T4 M6` / `G43 H4` / `S1500 M3`;
  - an F on the G73 (`G73 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z-0.9449 R0 Q0.7087 F2.36`) and on the tap (`G84 ... F29.53`, a 1.5 mm pitch at 500 rpm).
  - The tool diameters are the ones `golden_cl.rs` generated each path with.
- **`index_4face_microarc4.nc` showed the bug itself.** Its hand-built stream stated the spindle once. The old golden then cut sections 2-4 after their predecessor's M5 with no restart. The test stream now states `SpindleSpeed` per section, as `post::dump` does, and the golden gains `S6000 M3` (and the belt note) in each section.

### Goldens regenerated (WRITE_GOLDEN=1)
- `nc/drill_peck.nc`, `nc/drill_plate.nc`, `nc/tap_plate.nc` (Fanuc): an F on each cycle block, nothing else.
- `nc/haas/`, `nc/mazak/`, `nc/sinumerik/`, `nc/doosan-dnm/`: `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `tap_plate`. An F on each cycle block, nothing else.
- `nc/grblhal/drill_peck.nc`, `nc/grblhal/drill_plate.nc`: an F on each cycle block (grblhal refuses the tap, so it has no tap golden).
- `nc/tormach/`: all 13 legacy goldens (`contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`). These are now inch programs for the 770MX with the full preamble.
- `nc/tormach/index_4face_microarc4.nc`: `S6000 M3` in sections 2-4 (above).
- heidenhain, tinyg and carvera goldens did not move. No UI snapshot PNG was touched.

### Tests updated to post real programs
`tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_end_units.rs`, `tormach_machines.rs` (`tap_on`) and `tormach_fourth_axis.rs` (a `SpindleSpeed` per section) used bare legacy streams. They now use `as_program`. Their assertions are unchanged, except `an_inch_machine_posts_every_length_and_feed_in_inches`: it skips the 770MX's belt-range note line, because the metric reference machine states no belt ranges.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/post_cycle_feed_spindle.rs`)
Each one fails when its fix is mutated away:
- `a_canned_cycle_with_no_feed_is_refused_by_name`: every cycle post. It fails with the tormach check disabled, with the fanuc check disabled, and with any heidenhain fallback put back.
- `the_lathe_drill_cycle_with_no_feed_is_refused_by_name`: fanuc-lathe. It fails with the check disabled.
- `a_tormach_cut_before_any_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name`: a bare contour (G1) and a fed bare G73 are refused; the same paths as programs post clean. It fails with the spindle rule disabled.
- `a_tormach_section_after_m5_with_no_spindle_speed_is_refused`: it fails with the rule disabled, and also when `spindleOn` is not cleared at M5.
- `the_tormach_drill_golden_is_a_runnable_program`: the G73 has a positive F, and `T.. M6` then `S.. M3` come before it. It fails against the old golden.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post` (all debug suites, not `--ignored`). Before the test updates, 6 targets failed, all expected bare-stream fallout. After the updates they all pass.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 28 s, app suites 799 s, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- The PathPilot Hub run of the new goldens. Copies of `drill_peck` and `contour_plate_with_hole` (inch, 770MX) are in the user's hub-tests folder for that run.
- The spindle rule in the other mill dialects (#1359).
- The release-lane `--ignored` suites and the UI suites (no UI code touched).

title: test(setup): pin that undoing DeleteSetup keeps the setup order and the posted program
body:
## What changed

The reported bug does not reproduce, so there is no code change. Instead, new tests pin the contract the issue asks for.

- **How setup order is stored:** it is the name order. `setup::setups` reads `model::named_entities`, which sorts by name. No index field, list component or entity-id order holds it. When undo re-spawns a deleted setup, it sorts back into its old place. The operation order (`setup::operation_order`, ranked by setup) and the post follow from that.
- **Where the report came from:** PR #1361's MCP test made "Front" then "Back" and saw `["Back", "Front"]` after the undo. That was already the order before the delete (name order, not creation order). The setup did not move.
- New suite `crates/app/tests/setup_delete_order.rs`:
  - `undoing_delete_of_a_middle_setup_restores_its_place_and_the_program` sets up three setups, created out of name order (`A_First`, `C_Last`, then `B_Middle`). Each has its own stock, and Face ops sit in the first and last. It deletes `B_Middle` and undoes, then asserts the setup names, the active setup, the operation order, and that the **full posted G-code text** equals the program posted before the delete. It then redoes, which deletes the setup again, and undoes again.
  - `undoing_delete_of_the_first_setup_puts_it_back_first` checks that the setup `None` resolves to comes back first after undo.
- `docs/decisions/1362-delete-setup-undo-order.md` records this finding.

## Related commands checked

- `CreateSetup` undo removes the setup it made.
- A datum-transfer clone is a `CreateSetup`; its undo is pinned by `setups::datum_transfer_clones_the_world_and_undoes_exactly`.
- Main has no setup reorder or setup rename command, so nothing else can move a setup.
- If an explicit, hand-set setup position is added later, these tests fail when its undo loses the position.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran app:`setup_delete_order` (2 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Both tests also pass on unchanged main, which is the finding.

## Not exercised

- GUI Setups page. It lists through the same `setup::names`.
- MCP `delete_setup`. That tool is in the unmerged PR #1361; its test could drop the `sort()`.

Fork synced at v0.18.0; upstream/main merged into the branch.

title: fix(project)!: load pre-v59 meshes as "fidelity unknown" and refuse them by name until re-imported
body:
Point 2 of #1056 was still open: a project saved before #911 with an over-budget STEP mesh loaded as full fidelity, with no re-check. Points 1, 3 and 4 shipped in #1127. Points 3 and 4 are checked against their pins in the issue comment.

## Decision (docs/decisions/1056-fidelity-unknown.md)
- **Re-measuring on load is not possible.** The chord error is measured against the B-rep, and the file keeps only facets.
- **A v58 file cannot be narrowed.** #911 did not bump the version, so the file cannot tell a pre-#911 save from a later fine one, and it does not say which meshes came from STEP and which from STL/OBJ.
- So: **"fidelity unknown", refused by name**. It is not tightened, because no bound on the unknown chord exists.

## What changed
- `PROJECT_VERSION` goes to **59**. Loading an older file runs `project::fidelity_migrate`, which marks every mesh without a recorded `coarse_mm` "fidelity unknown": models with facets, fixtures and from-model stock copies. Each marked mesh gets one load note. A recorded chord from a #911-era file is kept.
- The mark is the sentinel chord `model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM` (1e12 mm) on the existing `ReducedFidelity` component. It therefore rides every path the flag already rides: copies, setup clones, delete/undo and `UpdateModel` propagation. No path can drop it silently.
- **Gate:** every op judged against an unknown mesh is refused by name ("... saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older) ... re-import the model to verify its operations"). An unknown part refuses the program verdict through `verdict_tol`, and an unknown fixture gets a `gate_problems` line of its own. Through `program_tol`, the program sim and the eye judge nothing.
- **Display:** the model page, MCP `get_job` and the script API say "Fidelity unknown" in words (`summary`, `facts` with `fidelity_unknown: true`). The sentinel is never shown as a number.
- **Fixtures:** an unknown fixture keeps its plain box at generation. Growing it by the sentinel would make it collide with everything, and the gate refusal blocks the post.
- **File format:** the mark is saved as `"fidelity_unknown": true`, so a re-save can never turn it into "fine". A row carrying both `fidelity_unknown` and `coarse_mm` is corrupt and refused before any world write. Only a fresh import clears the mark, and undoing that import restores it.
- `examples/first-part.camproj` and the microARC kit project are re-stamped v59 by hand. Their meshes are exact (an OBJ generator, and a mesh built in code), so they are known full fidelity.
- Follow-up #1339 (P7) covers an undoable "vouch for this mesh" command with its MCP tool, for models whose source file is gone or whose mesh is exact.

## How tested
- Pin: `fidelity_copies::a_project_saved_before_fidelity_was_recorded_loads_unknown_and_refuses_until_reimported`. It loads a v58 file and checks:
  - the model reads unknown (never full fidelity);
  - the recorded chords of "blank" and its stock copy are kept;
  - the load note is present;
  - `op_problem`, the verification report, `program_tol`, `verdict_tol`, `summary` and `facts` all say the named line;
  - a re-save writes `fidelity_unknown` (no `coarse_mm`) at v59, and that file is not migrated again;
  - `UpdateModel` clears the mark and its undo restores it;
  - a row with both keys is refused.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 65deeffd: app suites ok (175 s), ui suites ok (7 s). The run covered 94 app suites, including project_roundtrip, mcp, microarc_test_part, model_fidelity, coarse_laws, step_budget and the setup/fixture suites.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- ui lib (`--test-threads=1`): model_fidelity, step_budget, and `tool_body::the_simulated_tool_reaches_from_its_tip_into_the_body_on_the_users_document` (it loads the v56 `step_block_371.camproj`): ok.

## Not exercised
- The GUI by hand: opening a real pre-#911 project and reading the load notes and the model page line.
- The release-lane gpu_render docs test, which opens `examples/first-part.camproj`. Only that file's version number changed.

## Breaking
- Older builds refuse a v59 file (the version check), as with every version bump.
- Every project saved before v59 refuses its operations until each model is re-imported. That cost is deliberate; #1339 tracks removing it.

Changelog: Projects saved before mesh fidelity was recorded (v58 or older) open with each model marked "fidelity unknown" and their operations refused by name until the model is re-imported, instead of being judged as full fidelity (project v59) (#1056)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(ui): drag a part along an axis with move handles (#1198 b)
body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203.

**GUI hand check needed.** The handles, the drag feel and the readout were tested only through the kittest harness and headless state tests. Nobody has looked at them on screen yet.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A seventh bar button (a four-armed cross) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default, it is view state like pick-through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the part's bounding-box centre and each ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at any zoom. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** Pressing a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. Empty space still orbits. While the button is down, the preview slides the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows just above the bar. The distance is where the cursor ray comes closest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the Model page's own `MoveModel::new`, with the rotation copied bit for bit. That means one undo step, the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. No new placement path.
- **What adds no history step:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends where it began, and turning Move off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag happens in that setup's frame. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, so no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`, and the MCP `move_model` tool already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make every move a drag makes.

## How tested

title: fix(verify): the mid-turn overhang backstop reads the whole turn
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. **Stacked on #1319** (#1313's swept cells, not yet on main): this branch is based on `issue/1313-midturn-swept-band`; its own change is the last commit.

## What changed

Law (c3)'s overhang backstop - stock hidden under a ledge, which no column sample sees - still asked 4 path stations x 5 turn fractions per band, each at that pose's bottom plane. A holder or shank swinging through hidden stock between two of those poses got no `SweepHit` (#1316).

It now asks over the same reachable set #1313's column law reads, on its own coarser cells:

- New module `crates/sim/src/verify/turn_hidden.rs`. Per live band, #1313's cells (hull of the column's two end discs, grown by the proven sag, swept along each tip chord) with the turn split so the sag is at most 0.05 mm (`BACKSTOP_SAG`, a tenth of the hidden law's 0.5 mm XY spacing), capped at 20 intervals (`BACKSTOP_PLANES`). The tip's chords are grouped into at most 4 runs, and at most `20 / intervals` of them.
- One ask per (interval, run): at the lowest bottom any column of its cells reaches, over the union of their footprints. A point counts only where some position of a cell stands the band over it outside the flutes' kerf at that same tip position (`Cell::bottom_over`, unchanged).
- New entry point `Rest::hidden_in_cover` in `hidden.rs`: the hidden region's boundary samples in the box, plus footprint probes (disc centres and rings at 5 tip positions per chord, built only when the plane has hidden stock near the box), filtered by that membership. A failed slice still convicts.
- `turn_cells.rs`: `push_cells_with` (a stated sag budget and cap; `push_cells` keeps 0.001 mm / 64), `Cell::floor`, `Cell::probes`, `Cell::interval`. `sweep.rs` drops `backstop_columns`, `path_point` and the 4 x 5 grid.

**Slice count per move:** at most 20 distinct planes per live band (`BACKSTOP_PLANES`), the same as the old 4 x 5 grid, so the slicing budget does not change. Pinned by the unit test `a_move_asks_at_most_twenty_planes_per_band`. Past the cap the cells only grow: a 90 degree turn at 150 mm reach overstates by 0.12 mm, still on the safe side.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/midturn_hidden_backstop.rs` - `a_holder_crossing_hidden_stock_between_two_sampled_poses_is_convicted`: a holder 100 mm up the stack swings B 0 -> 80 under a ledge. At the old poses (20 and 40 degrees) its disc stands beside the hidden stock, and at 30 degrees it is inside it. Against the #1313 branch's `sweep.rs` it reports nothing (`[]`); here it reports `SweepHit { at: 0, part: false }`. Twins `the_same_swing_beside_a_bare_post_is_clean` and `a_swing_that_stops_short_of_the_hidden_stock_is_clean` stay clean.
- Unit tests in `verify::turn_hidden`: the plane bound (straight and 50-chord ramps, turns from 1 to 120+ degrees, non-finite letters), and an ask covering the holder between its end poses.
- `overhang_laws` (13) and `midturn_swept_band` (2) green, no assertion edited.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green - sim (25 suites incl. lib), motion (2) and app (47) gate-mapped suites, 75 binaries, 667 passed, 0 failed (7.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The release lanes (`--ignored`, the big posed fixtures) were not run, so false convictions and verify time on large real 5-axis programs near overhangs are not measured.
- Pre-existing limits kept: one plane per ask (hidden stock the band meets above its bottom plane is not asked here), and the hidden region is sampled in XY by its own law.

Decision note: `docs/decisions/1316-hidden-swept-backstop.md`.

Changelog: Verify's mid-turn overhang backstop reads the whole turn instead of 4 x 5 sampled poses, so a holder or shank crossing stock hidden under a ledge between samples is reported
Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1316

title: fix(verify): the mid-turn sweep reads the whole turn, not five poses
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Reach law (c3), the mid-turn sweep, read the band stack's column at 4 path stations x 5 turn fractions. Between them a holder or shank could cross uncut stock with no `SweepHit` (#1313).

It now reads the whole reachable set, by construction:

- New module `crates/sim/src/verify/turn_cells.rs`. Per band, one *cell* per tip chord and per interval of the turn. A cell is the convex hull of law (c)'s column at the interval's two end poses, grown by a proven sag, with its bottom at the lower end bottom less the sag.
- The sag bound: the letters lerp and bend the axis no faster than their own sweep, so inside a cell the axis strays from the chord of its end axes by at most `(sweep in the cell)^2 / 8`; times the band's reach above the tip. The cell count keeps it at 0.001 mm or less, capped at 64 cells per band (a 90 degree turn at 150 mm reach then overstates by 0.011 mm, still conservative).
- The tip's travel is not sampled either: the hull is clipped against the tip chord exactly, the bottom rides the chord's Z, and the flutes' kerf excuses a column only for the tip positions that stand over it.
- `sweep.rs` asks a cell one question (`bottom_over`); the column memo and the worst-offender rule are unchanged. `midpose::pose` became `pub(super)` to share the letter lerp.

A refusal is the safe side here: the new reading is a superset of the old one at every pose and station the old grid read.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/midturn_swept_band.rs` - `a_holder_crossing_a_stock_post_between_two_sampled_poses_is_convicted`: a holder 100 mm up the stack swings through a stock post between the 20 and 40 degree samples of an 80 degree turn. Run against main's `sweep.rs` it reports nothing; here it reports `SweepHit { at: 0 }`. Its twin `a_turn_that_stops_short_of_the_post_stays_clean` keeps a clear swing clean.
- `verify::turn_cells::tests::no_band_position_of_a_random_turn_lies_outside_the_cells` - the issue's brute-force probe: 240 random turns (A and B up to +-85 degrees, a third also in C), 5,076,000 band positions (the true cylinder's surface and law (c)'s own column, 9 path stations x 25 turn fractions). Zero outside the cells, in XY and in Z. The old grid misses 272,961 of the same positions.
- Three more unit tests: the sag bound at a wall, the kerf following the tip, degenerate bands and non-finite letters.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: sim, motion and app suites green (48 gate-mapped suites, every existing mid-turn test, no assertion edited). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The release lanes (`--ignored`, the big posed fixtures) were not run, so false convictions on real 5-axis programs are not measured. In the debug suites there are none.
- Verify time on a large posed program was not measured. A small turn needs fewer cells than the old 20 states per band; a large one up to 64.
- The overhang backstop (stock hidden under a ledge) still asks the old 4 x 5 grid: filed as #1316.

Decision note: `docs/decisions/1313-midturn-swept-band.md`.

Changelog: Verify's mid-turn sweep (law c3) reads every pose and tip position of a turn instead of five sampled poses, so a holder or shank crossing stock between samples is reported
Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #1313

title: fix(sim): verify refuses a non-finite or zero tool axis and normalises a scaled one
body:
## What changed

`verify` passes the path through one door before any law runs (`crates/sim/src/verify/axis_door.rs`, new; wired in `verify/engine.rs`):

- An axis with a **non-finite** component, **zero length**, or a length that **overflows** is refused by name with `Warning::NonFinite { at }`. The NonFinite law now covers `axis` as well as `from`/`to`; its text now reads "non-finite coordinate or tool axis". The refused axis is kept as stated, so each law's own guard still fires. For example, the radial rapid law's conviction of a zero pose stands.
- A **finite, non-unit** axis (`|a|²` more than 1e-12 off 1) is **normalised once** in a copy that every law reads.
- Already-unit axes pass bit for bit through a borrowed `Cow`: no copy, and no existing verdict or golden moves.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1312-verify-axis-refusal.md`. The reachability search the issue asks for is on the issue: no generator, CL import or MCP path emits such an axis, so the issue stays P3.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/sim/tests/axis_door.rs` (new, 5 tests). Four of them fail on main and pass here:
  - `a_non_finite_axis_is_refused_by_name`: reproduction 1, `[1e-12, 0, inf]` and others.
  - `a_scaled_axis_is_judged_as_its_unit_direction`: reproduction 2, the 7x axis at 2e-9 rad keeps its `ShankHit`.
  - `a_zero_or_overflowing_axis_is_refused_by_name`
  - `one_bad_axis_refuses_only_its_own_move`
- Unit tests in `verify::axis_door::tests` (2).
- `radial_rapids::a_rapid_on_a_pose_that_is_no_direction_convicts_itself`: its exact assertion now also expects the added `NonFinite { at: 0 }`. The `RapidInStock` conviction is unchanged.
- Quick-gate plan (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): every sim suite whose gate map names `sim::verify` plus the sim lib, 272 tests, all green on the final head. Motion `real_tip` and `solid_law` green. The 47 mapped app suites ran green (533 s) on the first variant of the door, which dropped a refused axis to upright. That gate run was VOID only because I edited files during it. The final variant differs only for refused axes, which no app suite feeds verify (grep-checked).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The mapped app suites were not re-run on the final head. See above for why.
- The other public law entries the post gate calls directly (`bands_vs_fixtures`, `rapids_vs_fixtures_spindle`) do not go through the door. The search found no path that feeds them a bad axis.
- Release-lane heavy tests were not run.

Changelog: Verify refuses a move whose tool axis is non-finite or of zero length, and judges a non-unit axis by its unit direction (#1312)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(ui,app): an async file picker opens models and projects in the browser
body:
Part of #31, the app and UI on wasm. This slice adds an **async file picker**, so a model or a project can be opened in the browser build. Until now every picker there answered "cancelled".

Fork synced at v0.18.0. The branch merges `upstream/main` (53a52f88) so that it diffs clean against `main`.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui/src/file_pick.rs`** (new): the browser picker. On wasm32, `open()` makes an `<input type=file>` whose `accept` comes from the dialog's filters, clicks it and returns at once. When the user has chosen, the file's name and bytes go into a thread-local inbox, and the next frame is woken through the egui context, which `shell_web` registers.
  - Files over 256 MiB (`BROWSER_READ_LIMIT`) are refused by name before they are read. A failed allocation in wasm aborts the tab.
  - The input and its change closure are held in one slot until the next pick, not `forget`ed, so a cancelled picker does not leak.
  - The inbox, `accept_attr` and `too_big` are plain Rust on every target.
- **`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`** (new):
  - `open_model_dialog` / `open_project_dialog`: rfd's synchronous dialog on native (unchanged), the async picker on wasm32.
  - Each frame, `drain_actions` turns every inbox entry into a `CommandKind::OpenPicked`. A model goes through `ImportModel::from_bytes` and `finish_import`: one undo step, and a same-named model is an update. A project goes through `project::open_noted`.
  - A failed read, a refused import, or a project that is not text or not JSON is said on the status line ("import refused: …" / "open failed: …") and changes nothing.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`**: `ImportModel::from_bytes(file_name, data, budget)`. It shares the path import's laws through `checked_budget`: IGES and unknown extensions refused, the STEP budget's bounds. It adds the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` cap and the finite-mesh gate. `geometry::import::parse_model_graded_within` is now `pub`.
- **`crates/ui/src/state.rs`**:
  - Two new `CommandKind` arms route to the functions above.
  - The model and project dialogs' filters are factored out (`mesh_dialog`, `project_dialog`) so both pickers ask with the same ones.
  - `open_project_path`'s reset is factored out as `reset_for_open`, so the bytes open retires the old document the same way. Behaviour is unchanged.
- No dependency added. The picker uses `eframe::web_sys` features that eframe already enables (`HtmlInputElement`, `File`, `FileList`, `Blob`).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `crates/app/tests/import_bytes.rs`:
    - `picked_bytes_import_like_the_same_file_from_disk`: the same name, mesh and fidelity as the disk import, for STL, OBJ and STEP.
    - `picked_bytes_are_refused_by_name_never_a_panic`: IGES, an unknown extension, no extension, empty or corrupt files of each format, and a budget given for a non-STEP file.
  - `crates/ui/src/file_pick_tests.rs`:
    - `a_picked_model_imports_through_the_undoable_command`
    - `a_picked_file_that_cannot_be_used_is_refused_by_name`
    - `a_picked_project_opens_in_place_of_the_document`
    - `the_browser_picker_accepts_the_dialogs_extensions`
    - `a_file_over_the_browser_read_limit_is_refused_before_it_is_read`
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. The app suites (lib, import_bytes, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export, bore_facet_sagitta) passed in 21 s. The ui suites (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, theme_files) passed in 19 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (native, macOS).
- **wasm check**: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` passed on macOS, using the official rustc 1.99.1 with the wasm32 std and Homebrew LLVM's clang for the wasi C.
  - It linked `camcraft-cli.wasm` and `camcraft_ui.wasm`, ran wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and laid out `target/web`. The shim answers all nine WASI imports.
  - camcraft-ui raised no warnings.
  - `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passed.
  - The script needed two local workarounds, which are not part of this PR: a GNU-`sed -i` shim, and a bash-3.2 empty-array fix for `"${PROFILE_ARGS[@]}"` under `set -u` (line 104). As shipped, the script does not run on stock macOS bash/sed. Worth a small follow-up.

## Not exercised - browser hand check needed
- **The picker was not run in a browser.** It needs a hand check: serve `target/web`, then use File > Open model on an STL, OBJ and STEP file and File > Open project on a `.camproj`. Also check that cancel does nothing and that a file over 256 MiB is refused on the status line.
- The input is clicked from the egui frame (requestAnimationFrame), not from the DOM click handler itself. Browsers allow this within the click's transient user activation. That is the main thing to confirm by hand, Safari included.
- Still owed on #31 (see the decisions file):
  - Save, Save As and Post in the browser, which need a download.
  - The other pickers: fixture import, machine, post, theme and tool library.
  - Dropped files.
  - Inline playback, a WebGPU run, the in-browser CI job, console diagnostics for the app crate, and the shell.rs split.

Changelog: The browser build opens models (STL, OBJ, STEP) and projects through an async file picker (#31).

title: test(post): move the probe and arc post suites out of app on recorded input
body:
Slice 2 of #926. Slice 1 was PR #1002 (the recorded edge-case streams and the per-`.cps` script suites). This PR moves the ten app suites named in the issue to `crates/post/tests`. They used app only to generate a toolpath before posting it; now they read recorded input instead.

## What changed
- **Moved to `crates/post/tests`:** `fanuc_post`, `probe_dialects`, `probe_guard`, `probe_report`, `probe_tormach`, `inverted_probe`, `arc_planes`, `inverted_equivalence`, `inverted_post`, and the posting half of `vertical_arc_entry`. Their helpers `inverted_support/` and `macro_b/` moved with them.
- **Recorded inputs (`crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/`):**
  - 28 probe `.cnc` streams, one per distinct (cycle, dump) pair the old tests built.
  - 5 probe paths as `.cl`. `cl::text` carries no touches, so `probe_guard`'s "every GUARD is a positioning feed of the path" law needs the path and the stream side by side.
  - 3 contour `.cl` paths for `vertical_arc_entry`.
  - The inverted-axis fixture stream.
- **Generator-side guards.** Each one compares byte for byte and rewrites the file with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`:
  - App's `recorded_post_streams` (slice 1's guard suite) guards the probe streams and paths, generated by `motion::probing::probe_cycle` and `post::dump`. App is still the only crate that sees both motion and post. Its new `every_recorded_input_has_a_generator` fails on any file in `inputs/` that nothing writes.
  - `crates/motion/tests/vertical_arc_entry.rs` is the generator half: true arcs, tangency, the oblique note and verify. It also guards the three contour recordings.
  - Post's `inverted_post` guards `inverted_probe.cnc`. App's `inverted_axis_display` reads that file, so app no longer carries a copy of `inverted_support`.
- **Stays in app:** the `ArcDto` project-file test, now in `float_roundtrip`, as the #919 research said.

title: fix(sim): crossing law reads a shared vertex a rounding apart as a touch
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream main 0757563d; not stacked on #1134, which carries `needs-rework`).

## What changed

The verifier's crossing law (a) read orientation signs exactly, so two moves meeting at one vertex reached twice, a rounding apart, could read as a proper crossing and hold the post with `Warning::Crossing`.

- `crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs`: new `pub const CROSSING_TOUCH: f64 = 1e-9` (mm), documented (f64 rounding at 1e4 mm is ~2e-12 mm; cutting tolerances are microns), re-exported as `camcraft_sim::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH`. New `proper_cross_touch`: `proper_cross` with a chord end that stands within `CROSSING_TOUCH` of one of the other chord's **end points** read as on that chord's line (orientation 0, a touch). The test is a point-to-point distance (`hypot`), not a raw cross-product magnitude, so it does not scale with chord length.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs`: law (a)'s pair predicate asks `proper_cross_touch`. `proper_cross` itself is unchanged, so `dist2_segs` and the arc-wall law keep the exact predicate.
- Doc comment and decision file say the law is the reference: the planner's `guard::crosses` (#1048, PR #1134's `TOUCH`) should use or match this constant and this end-point reading.

**Why end points, not the line (as #1129's text proposed).** The #1134 review showed that excusing an end within `TOUCH` of the other chord's *line* hides a real pass-through: a walk crossing a chord at a vertex 0.5 pm off its interior makes both of its chords there read as touches. That review said #1129 must not port that test to the verifier. Every case the issue names is a shared vertex, so the end-point reading fixes them and keeps that probe reported. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1129-crossing-tolerance.md`.

## How tested

Pins, `crates/sim/tests/crossing_touch.rs` (each checks the bucketed law against the all-pairs reference):
- `a_shared_vertex_a_rounding_apart_does_not_warn`: a joint 1e-12 mm apart in 16 directions, origins 0 / 37.25 / 1000 mm, chords 1 um / 0.5 / 20 / 1000 mm. Each scale asserts the old exact test tripped on at least one jitter. This test fails with the old predicate (checked).
- `a_crossing_a_micron_through_still_warns`: same scales, B starting 1 um short of A's end and 1 um below its line (a quarter chord for the 1 um chord).
- `a_walk_through_a_chord_at_a_vertex_a_picometre_off_its_line_still_warns`: the #1134 review's probe, vertex at -0.5 / +0.5 pm, at y 0 and 1000 mm.
- `collinear_overlaps_keep_their_reading`: partly overlapping collinear chords at 4 angles and 3 scales give the exact-sign verdict; an exact retrace stays no crossing.
- `a_joint_just_past_the_touch_keeps_the_exact_reading`: at 2e-9 mm the exact verdict is kept, so the edge itself is pinned.

Gate (macOS arm64, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: lib and all 58 test binaries green (incl. `crossing_touch` 5, `crossing_buckets` 3).
- `camcraft-app`: `verify` 21 (2 ignored), `golden_cl` 25, `verify_arc_reading` 7, `carried_verify` 8, `warned_moves` 2, `operations` 117 (6 ignored), `solid_law_goldens` 5, `shoulder_adaptive` 3, `trochoid_op` 5, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 (1 ignored): all pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib adaptive`: 26 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

No existing verify test or golden changed verdict.

## Not exercised

- The planner side: `motion` `adaptive::guard` is untouched. PR #1134 should adopt `CROSSING_TOUCH` and the end-point reading when it is reworked.
- The release `--ignored` heavy lanes and the UI suites were not run.
- Residual, same in kind as before: two walks crossing in an X exactly through a shared vertex were never reported by the exact-sign law; this extends that reading to a vertex a picometre apart. No new class of miss.

Changelog: The verifier's crossing law no longer holds the post when two moves share a vertex a rounding apart (within 1e-9 mm); a real crossing, including a pass-through at a vertex near another chord's interior, still blocks (#1129).

Fixes #1129

title: fix(sim): the posed fixture sweep reads a band as a flat-ended cylinder
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

## What changed

The posed sweep of fixture laws (c2)/(d2) (`crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel.rs`) placed each band of a leaning tool stack as a capsule. A capsule's caps reach one whole band radius past each band end, so an r 15 holder standing 0.5 mm over a clamp was convicted `FixtureHit` at any lean at all.

A box the capsule reaches is now read a second time against the band as the flat-ended cylinder it is (`flat_band_clear`):

- per interval: the tip chord `p0..p1` swept exactly + the cylinder `lo..hi`, radius `r`, about the midpoint pose + a ball of `pad = bulge + swing * hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)`;
- fixed steel under a rotary: that set carried by the midpoint turn and grown by `dth * (rho_max + r + pad)`, `rho_max` over the parallelogram's four corners;
- cleared only on a GJK proof of a separating plane wider than `pad + FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (`fixture_mesh::band_clear_of_box`: the mesh law's existing `SweptBand`/`Boxed` supports and `gjk::separated`, pointed at a fixture box).

This is the enclosure `verify/mesh_posed.rs` already proves for the fixture mesh law; the box law now reads the same geometry. Leaning by θ the rim reaches R sin θ past the end plane, not R, and the verdict turns at the lean where the true band touches.

## Why it is still conservative

- Both enclosures contain the swept band (proof in the module header and in `docs/decisions/1305-posed-band-cylinder.md`); a box is struck only when both reach it, so nothing the true band touches can be cleared.
- The cylinder's swing arm is `hypot(hi, r)` (the rim's distance from the tip), not the capsule's centreline arm `|hi|`.
- "Clear" is only the supporting-hyperplane bound over exact support mappings. Non-finite input, a zero axis, a degenerate rotary or an exhausted search is "not proven": the capsule's hit stands.
- Every verdict that was clear is clear by the same arithmetic (the capsule still runs first); only capsule hits can change. No golden moved.

## Tests

New, `crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel_tests.rs` (unit, on `posed_hits` / `sweep`):

- `a_holder_just_over_a_clamp_is_clear_at_a_small_real_lean` - the issue's evidence case (r 15 holder, clamp top 0.5 mm under it): clear from 1e-7 to 1.5 degrees (0.01 degrees included).
- `the_holder_is_struck_once_its_rim_really_reaches_the_clamp` - convicted as `Holder` from 2.2 degrees.
- `the_verdict_turns_once_and_at_the_true_touching_lean` - 1000 leans, 0.005 to 5 degrees: the verdict flips exactly once, within 0.006 degrees of the analytic touching lean (2.130 degrees).
- `a_fixed_clamp_under_the_stood_up_holder_is_clear_at_any_lean` - machine frame, clear at 29.5 and struck at 30.5.
- `steel_at_any_point_of_the_true_leaning_band_is_struck` - the property: 4800 specks of steel at sampled points of the true band (rims and end faces weighted) on moves whose pose swings, path frame and under a rotary, all struck.
- `a_non_finite_band_or_box_is_never_proven_clear`.

New, `crates/sim/tests/posed_band_cylinder.rs` (public laws): fixed clamp under a rotary clear at any lean / convicted when it reaches into the holder (`bands_vs_workholding`, `rapids_vs_workholding`); a 5 degree lean still convicts through `bands_vs_fixtures`.

Mutation checks (not committed): dropping the swing term from `pad` fails the property test; removing the second reading fails the three clearance tests.

## Gate (final head e15b633e)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green - sim suites (lib + 20 binaries, `posed_band_cylinder` among them), motion (`real_tip`, `solid_law`), app (46 binaries); 3 steps, 0 failed, 3.4 min.
- By hand: `posed_fixture` 7/7, `posed_fixture_midpose` 3/3, `stock_posed` 3/3, `fixture_mesh` 9/9 (1 ignored, release lane).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised / known limits

- **`main` has neither #938 nor #1303.** PR #973 (`UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD`) is open and #1303 is open with no branch pushed, so this is built on `upstream/main` alone and `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` does not exist here. In the path frame, law (c2) also runs its own column enclosure (`stack_span::band_struck`), which still drops a leaning band by its whole radius - that is #1303. Until it merges, `bands_vs_fixtures` on the evidence case is still convicted at 0.01 degrees by the column, not by the sweep. The sweep's verdict is pinned directly, and end to end where the sweep alone decides (fixed steel under a rotary).
- PR #973 changes one line of `posed_steel.rs` (`is_vertical` -> `is_upright`), away from these hunks; whichever merges second should merge cleanly.
- A move whose pose CHANGES keeps the swing ball (`swing * hypot(hi, r)`, intervals of 0.5 mm of far-end travel): continuous, but wider than a constant-pose move's reading.
- `mesh_posed.rs` already sweeps flat-ended bands (read in full). `probe.rs` was skimmed, not audited; unchanged.
- No release-lane (`--ignored`) suites were run.

Changelog: The posed fixture sweep reads each band of a leaning tool as the flat-ended cylinder it is, so a holder just over a clamp is no longer reported as a fixture hit at a small tilt (#1305)

Fixes #1305

title: fix(sim): a tilted band's column dips by the rim's exact R·sin θ
body:
**Stacked on #973** (branch `issue/938-tilt-tolerance` @ 9b01def4, which already carries current `main`). This PR's own change is the single commit de1d8641; until #973 merges the diff against `main` also shows #973's commits. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Since #938 a pose within 1e-9 rad is judged upright. Just above it the reach laws took the tilted column, which stood each band's bottom one **whole radius** under its foot. An r 12 holder 5 mm clear of a part was clean at 1e-9 rad and `ShankHit { part: true }` at 2e-9 rad or 0.01 degrees.

The tilted column now dips by the rim's exact `R·sin θ`. One helper, `verify::tilt_band::lean` (new module `crates/sim/src/verify/tilt_band.rs`), builds the column; the four copies of the formula are gone. Consumers:

| Law | File | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c) reach vs rest material | `reach.rs` | bottom `- R` | bottom `- R·sin θ` |
| (c3) mid-turn sweep | `sweep.rs` | bottom `- R` | bottom `- R·sin θ` |
| (c2) fixture band column | `stack_span.rs` | z planes `-/+ R` | `-/+ R·sin θ` |
| (d2) tilted rapid, flute column | `laws.rs` | z planes `-/+ R` | `-/+ R·sin θ` |

The column's centre and radius are the sums they were. Every upright branch is untouched. The posed capsule sweep, the mesh-steel law, the solid law and the contact law place the real pose and do not share this column; they are not changed.

## Derivation (full text in `docs/decisions/1303-tilt-band-dip.md`)

A band is the cylinder of radius R about the unit axis `a` (tilted θ off +Z) between axial stations `above` and `above + len`: points `tip + s·a + ρ·w`, `0 <= ρ <= R`, `w` a unit vector square to `a`.

- **z.** Write +Z as `cos θ·a + sin θ·h` with `h` unit and square to `a`. Then `w·Z = sin θ·(w·h)`, at most `sin θ`, reached at the rim point `w = ±h`. The axial part `s·az` is linear, so its extremes are the two ends. Lowest point: `tip.z + min(above·az, (above+len)·az) - R·sin θ`; highest: `max(..) + R·sin θ`. Both ends are in the `min`/`max`, so the band's own height is included.
- **Sideways** (unchanged): `s·a` stays within `len/2·sin θ` of the mid-station's foot and the disc adds R or less, so radius `R + len/2·sin θ` about `mid·(ax, ay)` holds it.

**Never under.** `rim_sine` = `min(1, max(h, h/|a|))`, `h = hypot(ax, ay)`: the sine itself for a unit axis, the larger reading for an axis off unit length, and 1 (the old whole radius) for a zero or non-finite axis. Never more than the old reading, never less than the true dip.

## Verdicts and goldens that moved

- Tilted moves only, toward clean only, and only where the old extra depth (between `R·sin θ` and `R`) was what met the material.
- `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` (#938's pins): `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_is_still_judged_tilted` expected the r 15 holder 5 mm over the stock to convict at 1.01e-9 rad and 0.001 degrees. That was the cliff. It is now `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_reads_like_upright_and_a_real_dip_convicts` (clean at both, convicted at 20 degrees where the rim is 1.9 mm into the stock). `a_leaning_shank_and_holder_report_one_shank_hit_per_move` moved its tilt to 20 degrees so the holder group still convicts beside the shank group.
- No golden, no posted output, no other existing test changed.

## How tested

Pins (new):
- `crates/app/tests/tilt_band_dip.rs`, on the `beside_wall` plate:
  - `a_small_tilt_of_a_holder_standing_clear_over_the_part_no_longer_convicts` - 1e-9, 2e-9 rad, 0.01 and 1 degree clean;
  - `a_tilt_that_brings_the_rim_into_the_part_still_convicts` - 0.4 degrees clean (rim 0.016 mm clear), 0.6, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60 degrees `ShankHit { part: true }`;
  - `the_verdict_is_monotone_in_the_tilt_across_the_upright_tolerance` - 20 tilts from 0 to 60 degrees, clean then convicted, never back, turning between 0.4 and 0.6 degrees;
  - `the_mid_turn_sweep_dips_by_the_rim_too` - law (c3).
- `verify::tilt_band` unit tests: a 4000-case property (random tilt 0..180 degrees, azimuth, R, foot, length; every sampled band point inside the column, and the column's planes reached by the samples), the limits, the unreadable-axis fallback, and the (c2) column read directly.

Mutation check, by hand: the whole radius (old reading) fails all four app pins; half the dip (an under-read) fails the conviction pins and the property test.

Gate on de1d8641, local:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: sim suites ok, motion suites ok, app suites ok (190 s), 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: 59 binaries ok, 486 passed, 0 failed.
- app `tilt_band_dip`, `tool_body_bands`, `tool_body_judged`, `sim_tool_body`, `verify`, `posed_contact`, `rotary_verify`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`: 76 passed, 0 failed.
- motion `multiaxis`, `multiaxis_avoid`, `multiaxis_rough`, `swarf_pose_continuity`, `swarf_reentry`, `pivot5d`: 33 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised / known

- Batch and release tiers and the `--ignored` heavy lanes were not run.
- The fixture verdict on a posed move is still the OR of the column and the posed capsule sweep, whose capsules reach a whole radius past each band end. A clamp just under a holder is still convicted on any tilt above the tolerance (`the_fixture_band_law_reads_noise_as_upright_and_a_real_tilt_as_tilted` is unchanged). Filed as #1305.
- Law (c3) still samples the turn (4 stations x 5 pose fractions). The decision file argues the sampled bottoms bound the in-between ones in z; that argument is not pinned by a test.
- No hands-on check in the GUI or on a machine.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Changelog: A tilted tool's holder and shank bands are enclosed by the rim's exact dip (R·sin θ) instead of the whole radius, so a small commanded tilt no longer reports a false shank or fixture-column collision (#1303)

Fixes #1303

title: fix(sim): a shipped build ignores CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE; a field-engine verdict names its engine
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

## What changed
- **A shipped build ignores `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE`.** The switch (#637) is honoured only where `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED = cfg!(debug_assertions)` holds (dev and test profiles); a release build never reads the variable and always carries stock on the column engine. The read is now the pure `engine_from_switch(value, honoured)` (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_held.rs`, re-exported as `stock_sim::carry_engine_from_switch`). This was the only reader of the variable.
- **A field-engine verdict names its engine, never silently.** New `stock_sim::carry_engine_note()`: `None` on the column engine, else "carried stock judged by the field engine (band N, development switch CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE), not the shipped column engine". It rides the post gate's visible, non-blocking line (`posting::sim_clause` -> post result, status line, G-code header), the setup sheet's `SIM:` line (`setup_sheet::simulate_verdict`) and the GUI Deviate readout (`crates/ui/src/actions.rs`).
- On the column engine nothing changes: no golden, no shipped verdict text moves.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1168-carry-engine-switch.md`: `debug_assertions` chosen over `cfg(test)` (integration tests link the lib without it, so the carried suites could no longer be run whole on the field arm) and over a cargo feature (a build change, plus `--features` on every field-arm run). No Cargo.toml change. The agreement lane is unaffected: it selects engines per call tree with `with_carry_engine`, in release too.

Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/carried_engine_agreement.rs`, default lane):
- `a_shipped_build_ignores_the_carry_engine_switch` - `engine_from_switch(_, honoured = false)` is the column engine for `field`, ` FIELD `, `column`, empty and unset; honoured, `field` selects the field engine; `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED == cfg!(debug_assertions)`.
- `a_verdict_the_field_engine_judged_names_the_engine` - on a carried two-setup document, `sim_clause` and `simulate_verdict` name the field engine (and the switch) under `with_carry_engine(FIELD)`, and add nothing on the column engine.

title: fix(thread): start the thread mill's feed at the operation's R plane
body:
Stacked on #1219 (issue/988-thread-pass-control @ 0d3a6a21), which stacks on #1137 (issue/985-external-threads @ 4f15b9b3); #1045 and #1005 are merged to main. Merge order: #1137 -> #1219 -> this PR. Retarget to `main` before #1219 merges.

Refresh 2026-11-12 (UMA): merged #1137 @ 4f15b9b3, then #1219 @ 0d3a6a21 (which carries upstream/main 440a6b8d), then upstream/main (already contained).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **Kernel** (`camcraft-motion`, `machining2d::thread_mill`): `ThreadParams` gains `r_z: Option<f64>`, the R plane. Each feature's rapid stops at `max(R, the ride's run-out)` and the feed down the axis (or beside the boss) starts there; the ride climbs back to it at feed before the link rapid. `None` is the #894 ride, so every existing kernel golden is byte-identical. An R plane below a feature's top, above the link plane, or not finite is refused by name.
- **App** (`thread_op::kernel_params`): passes the resolved `top_z` ("R plane (feed starts here)") as `r_z`, for internal and external threads.
- **Door** (new `operation::thread_r_plane`): a fixed `top_z` below a listed hole's or boss's top is refused when the operation is created, edited or re-tooled. A referenced height resolves at generate, where the kernel asks. The door's R check runs after the tool and feature laws, so their refusals keep their own wording.
- **Stock law** (`thread_r_plane::judge`, called at generate before the #992/#985 way-in laws): every vertical rapid down is read in the prior grid over the mill's full disc. Stock above the rapid's end is refused by name with the stock height and the fix ("raise the R plane (feed starts here) to z ... or above, or machine that stock away"). An unknown prior or an unreadable disc is left to the way-in laws, which already refuse both by name.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1212-thread-r-plane.md`. It covers how the default is seeded: unchanged, Top of Model, and every golden fixture already states R on the feature top.

## Tests (pinning)

- Kernel: `machining2d::thread_tests::the_ride_rapids_to_the_r_plane_and_starts_its_feed_there` (internal and external; an R on the top equals the #894 ride move for move), `an_r_plane_under_a_top_or_over_the_link_plane_is_refused_by_name`.
- Golden (new): `golden_cl::thread_mill_raised_r_plane_matches_golden` -> `tests/golden/thread_mill_raised_r_plane.cl` (R 2 mm over the tops of two holes). **No existing golden moved.**
- App: `thread_entry::the_operations_r_plane_is_where_the_rapid_stops_and_the_feed_starts` (generates, verifies clean, posts through the gate), `an_r_plane_under_the_holes_top_is_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `an_r_plane_that_ends_the_rapid_in_the_stock_left_ahead_is_refused_by_name`. Unit: `operation::thread_r_plane::tests::*` (door, stock law).
- Fixture changes: two MCP tests (`mcp::thread_milling_over_the_tools`, `external_thread_milling_over_the_tools`) typed a mouth at z 20 above a 15 mm block, under the default R (top of model). They now sit on the block's top, and the #992/#985 refusals they pin are unchanged. `thread_boss::impossible_bosses_are_refused_when_the_operation_is_made` states R on its 25 mm boss so that the reach refusal it pins is still the one reported.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/988-thread-pass-control` on the final head: green (2 steps, 0 failed, 4.1 min) on cfb25dd2. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion and camcraft-app: clean.

## Not exercised

- Through the UI page: the Heights tab already shows the R plane, and no UI code changed.
- Posted NC golden with a raised R plane: the CL golden pins the moves, and the post is unchanged.

Changelog: Thread milling rapids to and starts its feed at the operation's R plane (top_z) instead of each hole's or boss's top; an R plane below a feature's top, or one whose rapid would end in stock left by the program ahead, is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)
