title: fix(app): judge a tap's cutting moves at its thread's core in the op verify
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

### What changed

The second half of #266. @austin62jake's PR #713 (merged) made the program sim sweep a Tap-kind tool at its thread's core (`tool_law::cutting_radius`, ISO 724 basic minor diameter, `d/2 - 0.5413 p`). As their PR noted, a tap on a tap-drill hole still did not post: the op's own verify convicted the tap's feed in and out (`move 1/2 cuts past the finish surface`) because its tangency and solid laws read the full major diameter against the hole wall.

- New `operation::tap_core` (`acquit`, `core_tool`): for a Z drill cycle with a Tap-kind tool, generate re-runs the same cutting laws (`verify_bodies` + the containment solid law) with the tap cut to its core, and drops each `Gouge` that the core run does not also raise.
- Only `Gouge` is re-read. Rapids, shank, holder and fixture verdicts keep the full diameter (a tap must never rapid into its thread band). It can only remove convictions, never add one; a pitch with no core leaves the full verdict standing.
- Out of scope, unchanged (full diameter, over-reports only): the helical thread mill (`Thread` op), cross holes, tilted (3+2) taps.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-core-verify.md`.

Credit: the rule (`cutting_radius`), the sim half and the `tap_sim.rs` fixtures are @austin62jake's (#271 / #713); this PR builds on them. No code of theirs is re-committed here, since it is already on main.

### Readings (M6 x 1 catalog tap, block with a blind square hole)

| Case | Op verify before | Op verify after | Program sim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | Gouge at moves 1, 2 (blocks post) | no blocking warning | clean |
| Ø4.6 hole (under D1 4.917) | gouge | gouge | gouge |
| Ø0.5 slit (no pilot) | gouge | gouge | - |
| Ø5 hole, tap 3 mm past the floor | gouge | gouge | gouge |
| Ø6 drill in Ø5 hole | gouge | gouge (unchanged) | - |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_tap_drill_hole_carries_no_blocking_warning` - fails on main (Gouge at moves 1 and 2), passes with the fix.
- Guards: `a_tap_in_a_hole_under_its_minor_diameter_is_still_convicted`, `a_tap_deeper_than_its_hole_is_still_convicted`, `a_tap_with_no_hole_under_it_is_still_convicted`, `a_drill_at_its_own_diameter_keeps_the_full_verdict`; austin62jake's two sim tests still pass.

### How tested (Linux)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 74c5ba8b: app suites (lib + 131 suites incl. `tap_sim`, `solid_law_goldens`, `drill_prior`, `posting`, `tapping_mode`, `verify`-adjacent) ok in 639 s, ui suites (boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, feedback, machine, operations) ok in 114 s; 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `tap_sim` alone: 7 passed. The new pinning test reproduced on main as `Gouge { at: 1 }`, `Gouge { at: 2 }` before the fix.

Goldens: no golden file changed (paths are untouched; only warnings are re-read). `solid_law_goldens` (tapped hole modelled at the major diameter) unaffected.

### Not exercised

- Through the GUI / `camcraft-cli mcp` post end to end (the post gate reads exactly these warnings plus the program sim, both pinned).
- Thread mill, tilted frames, Windows/macOS.

Changelog: A tap on a hole modelled at tap-drill size no longer carries false "cuts past the finish surface" warnings, so it posts (#266)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #266

title: fix(ui): no console window on Windows double-click
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

**What changed.**
- `crates/ui/src/main.rs` gets `#![cfg_attr(windows, windows_subsystem = "windows")]` (debug and release), so a double-click opens no console.
- New `crates/ui/src/win_console.rs` (`#[cfg(windows)]` only, a few `extern "system"` kernel32/user32 declarations, no new dependency: windows-sys is only transitive here):
  - `attach_parent_console`: `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)`; after a successful attach, each of STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE / STD_ERROR_HANDLE whose `GetStdHandle` is NULL or INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE is pointed at `CreateFileW("CONOUT$")` via `SetStdHandle`. Valid handles (`> log.txt 2>&1`, pipes) are left alone. Rust's std calls `GetStdHandle` on every write (`library/std/src/sys/stdio/windows.rs`, `write` -> `get_handle`), so `std::io::stderr` (the tracing writer) picks up the new handle.
  - With no console attached: a `MessageBoxW` from `main` when `run` returns non-zero, and a panic hook chained after the previous hook doing the same with the panic text. One box per process. The hook only formats and calls MessageBoxW (nothing that can panic).
- Linux/macOS unchanged; the CLI binary is untouched and stays a console app. Decision: `docs/decisions/1278-windows-no-console.md`.
- **No-console log destination:** with no console and no redirect the log is still lost; a per-user log file is follow-up #1323.

**Verified (Linux).** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (ui lib). For the Windows target (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`): `win_console.rs` compiles and is clippy-clean with `-D warnings` standalone (`rustc`/`clippy-driver --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --emit=metadata`). A full `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p camcraft-ui` could not run: `flecs_ecs_sys`'s C build needs `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`, not installed here. So the `main.rs` Windows block is not compile-checked against the crate.

**Not exercised. NOT run on Windows.** Please, a Windows tester, confirm the 4 cases:
1. double-click: no console flash, app opens;
2. launch from cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash: log appears in the terminal;
3. `camcraft-ui.exe > log.txt 2>&1` and a pipe: the file/pipe gets the log;
4. a forced start-up failure by double-click (e.g. `CAMCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=bogus` set system-wide): an error message box appears.
No automated test can open a console or a message box.

Changelog: Windows: double-clicking the app no longer opens a console window; terminal launches still log to the parent console, and a start-up failure without a console shows an error box (#1278, PR #1287)
Effort: medium

Fixes #1278

title: feat(finish3d): land model - fill closed openings on the drive surface
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed

A 3D Finish option, **Fill openings** (`fill_openings`, mm, off by default), for the land case in #1196: the finish flies over bolt holes and small pockets at their rim instead of diving down their walls.

**The fill rule** (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/fill.rs`, new):
- Sample the model's top-down height field on a grid (cell = width/12, coarsened to at most 4M cells; a width too fine for the model at that cap is refused by name). Cells over no facet read as the model's lowest Z.
- Grey-scale morphological closing with a flat disk of the stated diameter (Serra 1982; Soille 2003). A cell raised by more than the finish tolerance is an opening cell.
- A connected group is filled only when it is **closed**: none of it on the grid border, and every bordering cell is material standing at the lid's level (within one cell's 45-degree rise + tol). Slots or valleys that run out to an edge, or a lid that would spill over a lower rim, are never filled.
- Lids (horizontal rectangles at the closed height, never below the surface) cover the group plus its neighbour ring.

**Safety:** the drive facets are the model's facets, unchanged and first, plus lids, so a path planned on them can rise but never bite the model deeper. Only the path is planned on the lids. The verifier still gets `material.facets` (the real model), so a gouge under a lid is still caught. The path gets a `land: N closed opening(s) narrower than W mm filled at their rim and flown over, not cut ...` note.

**Plumbing:** `OpParams::Finish3D.fill_openings: Option<f64>` (undoable through `EditOperationParams`; sanity refuses a non-finite or non-positive width at the door). The optional `fill_openings` file key is absent when None. The MCP params door carries it (`edit_operation {"fill_openings": 5.0}`). The stamp digest gets bytes only when a width is set. There's a "Fill openings" field on the 3D Finish page. Geodesic + fill is refused by name, because the lids would be new open boundary for its march. There's no project-file version bump: an older reader ignores the key and cuts the model itself, which is a valid finish, not an unsafe one. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1196-finish3d-land-fill.md`.

**Option off is byte-identical:** no file key, no digest bytes, and the generators get `&material.facets` as before. No goldens moved.

## Tests
- `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` (new):
  - `land_finish_flies_over_the_bolt_holes_and_verifies_on_the_real_plate`: a 40x20x8 plate with two 3.4 mm through holes and a 3 mm ball. Waterline and Parallel with fill on: no tip inside a hole below the top. The deepest ball bite measured on the REAL plate is within tol. The same path sunk 0.5 mm is caught on the real plate. The raster crosses the mouths at the top with fill on and doesn't with it off.
  - `a_blind_pocket_is_lidded_and_a_gouge_into_its_floor_is_convicted`: off dives to the pocket floor and on never does. A plunge planted through the lid into the pocket floor is caught on the real model.
  - `an_opening_wider_than_the_width_or_open_to_the_edge_is_not_filled`: a 3 mm width doesn't fill a 3.4 mm hole (output is exactly the model), and an edge-to-edge slot stays open.
  - `nonsense_widths_are_refused_by_name`: 0, negative, NaN, inf, a too-fine width and an empty model.
- `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` `finish3d_fill_openings_lands_over_a_pocket_and_verifies_on_the_model`: end to end through `GenerateOperation`. Off rides the pocket floor. On never descends, status Ok (the real-model verify is clean), and the land note is present. A negative width is refused at `CreateOperation`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs` `fill_openings_rides_the_params_door_and_undoes`: off by default, set over MCP, 0 refused, generate ok, and undo restores off.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on the final head: green on 0754f88c (motion 190 s, app 599 s, ui 74 s; 0 failed). Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on motion, app and ui.

## Not exercised
- The reporter's STEP part (not attached). The fixtures are square-hole plates.
- The finish3d heavy (`--ignored`) envelope lane: no existing generator changed, and the fill is opt-in.
- The UI field is only compile-checked. No snapshot PNGs changed.

Changelog: 3D Finish can fill closed holes and pockets narrower than a stated width on the planned surface ("Fill openings"), flying over them as a land finish while the verifier still judges the real model (#1196)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1196

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- `site/config.toml`: `build_search_index = true` with a `[search]` block: `index_format = "elasticlunr_javascript"` (so the index is `search_index.en.js`), title, description and path indexed, body indexed truncated to 2000 characters.

Results are a dropdown under the box, built with `textContent` (no `innerHTML`). Keyboard: Down from the box enters the results, Up/Down move between them, Enter follows the first result on submit, Escape closes and returns focus to the box. title: feat(vise): self-centering grip jaw - a step the stock sits on
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed
- `vise::SelfCentering` gains `grip_depth` / `grip_width` (mm, 0 = off): a grip jaw, a step cut into each jaw's inside top edge. The jaw profile walks down the face to the ledge, in along it, down to the floor; the frame's z = 0 is the ledge (the floor the part sits on), so the vise body drops by `jaw_height - grip_depth`. Fit and an in-place `SetVise` edit both keep the stock seated on the ledge; the fixture/collision laws, stock simulation and the post gate read the stepped mesh.
- Law (`check_grip`, refused by name at command creation): both figures or neither; finite, non-negative; depth < jaw height; width < jaw thickness; opening > 2 x width (ledges would meet under the stock); dovetail lip and grip step not both ("a dovetail or a grip jaw, not both").
- `ViseParams::seat_height()` / `SelfCentering::seat()`.
- Project: two optional keys on the `self_centering` object, written only when non-zero; older files read as no step and a stepless vise writes byte for byte as before. No project version move.
- Dialog: "Grip step depth" / "Grip step width" rows with tooltips (dovetail rows get one too); the fit line says the stock sits on the grip steps and how far above the vise floor.
- MCP: `add_builtin_vise` / `set_vise` `dimensions` take `grip_depth` / `grip_width`; the vise view reports them.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1274-grip-jaw.md`.

## Tests
- `crates/app/tests/self_centering_grip_jaw.rs` (new): `the_grip_jaw_carries_the_step_and_its_seat_is_the_frame_origin` (volume, bounds, steel/air at ledge and jaw), `bad_grip_figures_are_refused_by_name`, `a_grip_vise_seats_the_stock_on_the_ledge` (vise sits 12 mm lower than bed-seated for a 3 mm step on a 15 mm jaw), `the_fixture_law_judges_the_stepped_jaw` (face pass at z 9.5 struck by bed-seated jaws, clear on the grip step; pass at z 1 into the step blocks the post), `an_older_vise_key_reads_and_writes_unchanged_and_a_grip_round_trips` (old key byte for byte; save/reload; undo/redo).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_self_centering_vise.rs`: grip dims through `set_vise`, refusals named, undo count.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_self_centering_tests.rs`: grip rows present for self-centering only; `a_grip_jaw_seats_the_stock_on_its_steps_and_places_in_one_step` (structural; no snapshot PNGs).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) and clippy `-D warnings` on app/ui on the final head f0e63454: green (app suites 18 s, ui suites 83 s; 0 failed); clippy clean.

## Not exercised
- Posed (tilted) grip vises in the 5-axis fixture laws beyond the shared mesh path; setup sheet (it does not state jaw forms).
- An older build re-editing a grip vise would drop the step (it keeps the saved facets until edited) - noted in the decision file.

Changelog: Self-centering vises get an optional grip jaw - a step (depth, width) on each jaw's inside top edge that the stock sits on; the fixture checks judge the stepped jaw (#1274)

title: fix(post): refuse by name a post that does not serve its setup's machine kind
body:
## What changed

A post now writes only for what its setup's machine can run (#1232):

- **Kind door** (`crates/app/src/posting_serves.rs`, wired into `post_setup`/`post_script`, `post_mounts`/`post_mounts_script`, `post_per_op`/`post_per_op_script` - so the GUI, script verb and MCP `post` get it too): a mount whose post does not serve its machine's kind is refused by name (setup, ops, post, machine, kind) before anything is written. Shipped posts are judged by the picker's law (`post_serves`); a user's script by its `capabilities` mask (`work_voice`).
- **Section door** (maintainer's decision, 2026-11-12, "Refuse it"): a section that turns the work - a turning op or an on-centre drill, as `lathe_voice::voice_of` reads it - posts only through a turning post (`work_voice` = `WorkSpindle`). Through a milling post it is refused by name, on a mill-turn as on a lathe. Milling and C-axis sections on a mill-turn still post through a milling post. The shipped Mill-turn machine's default post is unchanged.
- ~27 lathe tests in 14 suites were themselves posting through the Fanuc mill post (this bug); they now select Fanuc Lathe. `lathe_cross_drill`: the generate-only tests stay on the plain lathe; only the posting test uses a mill-turn. `lathe_work_spindle`: the on-centre drill on a mill-turn through the Fanuc mill post is now refused. `lathe_stroke`: the built-in Mill-turn turning job selects Fanuc Lathe.

## Pinning tests

- `post_serves_kind`: `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name`, `a_lathe_program_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_on_every_single_file_path`, `a_mill_setup_on_a_lathe_post_is_refused_and_the_lathe_on_its_lathe_post_still_posts`, `an_edm_mount_refuses_a_cutting_program_by_name`, `a_turning_section_on_a_mill_turn_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_by_name` (Haas own post and Fanuc document post, on post_mounts, post_per_op and post_setup; nothing written; a turning post serves it).
- `lathe_workholding_mill_post`: `a_mill_turn_facing_op_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_and_held_to_the_chuck` (was "posts at the chuck limit"; now refused by name at the limit too - stricter). `a_mill_turn_milling_section_through_a_milling_post_is_not_judged` and the kind x dialect x section walk still pass (milling section on a mill-turn through Fanuc/Haas posts).
- No golden, recorded post stream or snapshot touched: a lathe on a lathe post, a mill, and C-axis sections post byte-identical.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head, plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` on head d1fec88a: whole app crate (shared `tests/common/bore.rs` maps quick to every suite) 2313 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored (heavy lane); clippy clean.

## Not exercised

The `crates/ui` suites (UI code untouched), the release-tier heavy lanes, MCP/script end to end (they call the gated entry points). Not addressed here (review notes, non-blocking): the undeclared-script hint to settle with #1213, a label for a script handed by path, a builtin-mask agreement unit test, the `lathe_workholding_kinds` test name.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Changelog: A post now refuses by name a setup whose machine kind it does not serve, and a turning section (turning op or on-centre drill) through a milling post on a lathe or mill-turn; existing documents with a lathe or mill-turn turning op on the default Fanuc post now refuse until a turning post is picked (#1232).

Fixes #1232

title: docs(site): keyboard shortcut and mouse reference
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923fc858b4ba3c4c600504020ef2489f1b0).

## What changed

- New guide page `site/content/guide/keyboard-and-mouse.md` (weight 7): every keyboard shortcut and mouse gesture bound in `crates/ui`, with Windows/Linux and macOS columns. Egui's `command` modifier is Cmd on macOS. Pick modifiers use the physical Control key on every platform.
- `site/content/guide/first-run.md`: one paragraph linking to the new page.
- Docs only. No Rust, no snapshot, no test changes.

## Verified rows (source)

Keyboard, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs` `shortcuts()`:
- New Ctrl/Cmd+N, Open model Ctrl/Cmd+O, Open project Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O, Save +S, Save As +Shift+S, Post +P: gated by `cmd && !typing`.
- Quit Ctrl/Cmd+Q (same block). macOS Cmd+Q also via `egui_app/os_quit.rs`.
- Undo Ctrl/Cmd+Z (no shift/alt). Redo Ctrl/Cmd+Y or +Shift+Y. Not gated by typing.
- Copy operation Ctrl/Cmd+C (needs a selected operation), Paste Ctrl/Cmd+V: `cmd && !typing`.
- Delete key (`Key::Delete`), gated by `!typing`. On a Mac this is Fn+Delete (forward delete) - not checked on hardware.
- F frames all (`!typing && !cmd && !alt`). Bare P toggles perspective/ortho (same guard).
- Enter commits a typed value: `egui_app/op_page.rs:83`, `egui_app/step_budget_row.rs:24`.

Viewport mouse, `egui_app/shell.rs` (~L415-520) and `interact.rs`:
- Left drag past `CLICK_TRAVEL_PX` (4 px) orbits; middle drag orbits.
- Right drag pans. Right click with no movement does nothing; the viewport has no context menu.
- Mouse wheel and `smooth_scroll_delta` dolly toward the cursor (`cam.dolly_cursor`). Two-finger scroll is the same path on a trackpad.
- Pinch (`zoom_delta`) is read only in `egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, not in the viewport: listed under Not bound yet.
- Left click (release within 4 px) picks through `interact::pick_at`; a miss clears the model selection (`pick_model`).
- ViewCube: `egui_app/viewcube.rs` `click()` orients the view on a cube hit, and runs nav buttons.

Picking modifiers, `interact.rs` `Mods` (`ctrl` = physical Control), `edge_pick.rs`, `feature_click.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`:
- Feature pick: plain replaces; Ctrl or Shift appends (`feature_click.rs:191`). Adding an already-picked face or vertex is refused with "already selected" (`interact.rs` `queue_feature_pick`).
- Edge mode: Ctrl toggles one edge (removes it when already picked), Shift takes the whole face loop, Alt one segment (`feature_click.rs` `ask`, `edge_pick.rs`).
- Boundary: Ctrl toggles, Shift closes around the face loop, plain replaces (`boundary_draft::PickMods`).
- Box-select: no code path (no marquee in `crates/ui`). Not bound.

Right-click, `egui_app/browser_pane.rs` (`hit.menu`), `tree_menu.rs`, `fixture_menu.rs`, `egui_app/panes.rs` (L1066 pin, L1454 error line), `painted.rs`:
- Operation row: operation menu. Model row: fixture menu. Setup Operations row: Paste. Ribbon cell: pin/unpin. Error line: Copy message.

## Not bound yet

Listed on the page under "Not bound yet": box-select, a Run shortcut, shortcuts for Paths/Simulate/Deviate and the Setup groups, Ctrl/Cmd+A outside a text field, pinch-zoom in the viewport, Ctrl/Shift/Alt drag pan, arrow keys, Escape to close dialogs (comments mention it; no Escape handler exists), middle-click alone.

## Mac checks not done

- No Mac available: Control-click on macOS is reported as a secondary (right) click by the OS (the PR #1242 description says so). The page says "not checked on a Mac" for that and for two-finger click/drag pan.
- Fn+Delete as the forward-delete key: assumed from egui's key mapping, not verified on hardware.

## Pick modifier note

PR #1242 (`fix(ui): pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier`) moves add-to-selection from Ctrl to the command modifier (Cmd on macOS). The page documents main's current behaviour and has a note on it.

## Gate

Docs-only: no test binary touched, so no quick gate run. `zola` is not on PATH in this environment, so `zola check` was not run; the internal links were checked by hand (`@/guide/keyboard-and-mouse.md` resolves to the new file; the `#not-bound-yet` anchor matches the heading).

title: test(machine): pin that a machine switch is judged again at the post
body:
## What changed

This PR adds tests and a decision record. It changes no product code.

Issue #1241 asked whether a toolpath generated and cleared on machine A can post on machine B without being checked against B. A remount happens two ways: through the setup's own machine (`SetSetupMachine`) or through the document's machine (`LoadMachine`), which the setup follows. The new suite `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` traces both.

**Result: only the display is stale. No path posts on B without being checked.** For every law the post checks the cached path again, against the machine the op's setup mounts now:

| Law (path made on A, mounted on B) | Op status after the switch | Gate / post on B |
|---|---|---|
| Travel (B: +/-10 mm) | Ok | refused: `machine TightMill: ... Face1: move N reaches ... the stroke is -10.000..10.000` |
| Spindle max rpm (B: 1000) | Ok | refused: `Face1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs ... above the machine's 1000` |
| Rotary (tilt-head to VMC 3-axis, leaning pocket) | Ok | refused: `P: move N tilts the tool; ... states no tilting rotary` |
| Machine kind (mill to Lathe) | Ok | refused: `Face1: a ... operation cannot run on its setup's ... machine` |

Every refusal writes no file. The same results hold through each switch route (setup and document), after undo (A is back and the program posts), after redo, and after save and reopen.

The op still reads Ok after a switch on purpose. This is the M2.3 "roomy-one" law: machine limits and workholding feed the post's live gate and are never part of the op stamp. It is pinned by `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath` ("loading a machine must not re-generate the program"). M3.2 B once tried a machine digest term in the stamp and reverted it. So the issue's "Done means" is met by its "or the issue records why it need not" branch. `docs/decisions/1241-machine-switch-live-gate.md` records the decision, the options I dropped (stamping the machine identity, or only the fields generation reads), and what it would cost to change if the maintainer wants a switch to show ops as stale.

## How tested

- Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` (6):
  - `a_setups_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `a_setups_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`
  - `a_setups_new_machine_of_another_kind_refuses_the_family`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_of_another_kind_refuses_the_family`
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 6 of 6.
- Neighbouring suites: `setup_mount`, `fixtures`, `post_not_judged` and `machine` all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The per-mount post (`post_mounts`), where setups run on different machines. It uses the same `machine_problems` gate.
- The spindle-body and table steel after a switch. These are checked by the live fixture gate (`fixture_struck` reads the setup's current machine), and the existing fixture suites pin that.
- The UI. The UI test comment the issue quotes (`setup_mount_pages.rs`) is not on upstream main.

Effort: high (did not escalate)
Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch cut from upstream/main 37482923.

Fixes #1241

title: fix(ui): pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 7580cd21).

## What changed

Edge and feature picks added to the selection on Ctrl. On macOS Control is the secondary (right) click, so a Mac user could not Ctrl+click to add an edge chain to an operation's picks, while the keyboard shortcuts already use the command modifier.

- `interact::Mods.ctrl` is renamed to `Mods.command`. It is built from egui's `modifiers.command` (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) through a new `From<egui::Modifiers>` impl, which the shell now uses.
- Pick add/toggle reads `mods.command`: `edge_pick::queue_edge_pick`, `interact::queue_boundary_pick` (boundary toggle), `feature_click::click` (feature add), and the `ui.input` conversion in `egui_app/shell.rs`.
- Shift keeps its meaning exactly (add in feature modes, whole loop in Edge mode, close in boundary mode).
- Windows/Linux: egui sets `command` whenever Ctrl is held, so behaviour is unchanged there.
- UI hint strings are not touched (#1239).
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1238-pick-command-modifier.md`.

## Tests

Pinning test: `the_command_modifier_from_egui_toggles_and_control_alone_does_not` (crates/ui/tests/edge_loop_pick.rs). It converts `egui::Modifiers::COMMAND`, Shift and Control-alone, asserts Control alone does not add on macOS, and that the command modifier toggles an edge in.

Updated, still green: `command_click_toggles_one_edge_in_and_out` (was ctrl), and the boundary_picks CTRL constant is now CMD (`command: true`). Shift tests unchanged.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test edge_loop_pick --test boundary_picks`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: ok (ui lib, boundary, boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, operations, theme_files).

## Not exercised

- No Mac was used. The macOS behaviour rests on egui's `command` mapping and the converted-`Modifiers` test; it was not run on hardware.
- The feature-mode add path in `feature_click::click` is changed but has no direct test (the function is `pub(crate)`); it is covered only by the rename compiling and the existing suites staying green.

Changelog: fix: edge and feature pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); Control alone no longer adds on macOS (#1238)

Effort: low

Quick gate green on the final head (post + app suites); clippy -D warnings clean on camcraft-app and camcraft-post.

title: feat(thread): thread-milling pass control - decreasing passes, finish and spring passes, depth allowance, M4 cutters
body:
Stack order: #1005 (merged) -> #1045 (merged) -> #1137 (open, issue/985-external-threads @ 4f15b9b3) -> this PR. Merge #1137 first; this branch already carries its head. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Thread milling (internal and external) gains pass control, one value `ThreadPasses` on the kernel's `ThreadParams` and on `OpParams::Thread`:

- **Decreasing pass depths (constant chip area)**: `pass_schedule: constant_area` - cumulative depth after pass i of n is `D x sqrt(i/n)`, the infeed is the first (largest) pass, `n = ceil((D/infeed)^2)`, capped at 64 (refused by name past that). The last roughing pass lands exactly on D.
- **Finishing pass** of its own radial depth (`finish_depth`) and **spring passes** (`spring_passes`, at most 4) on the final radius.
- **Depth allowance** (`depth_allowance`, radial): the last pass lands on standard depth - allowance. A negative allowance (past the major diameter of a hole / the design root of a boss) and one over a quarter of the thread depth are refused by name.
- **Spindle and cutter hand** (`spindle_reverse` = M4, `cutter_left_hand`): climb sense flips under M4 (the helix keeps the drawing's hand); a right-hand-cut mill under M4 or a left-hand-cut one under M3 is refused by name. M4 reaches the post via a new `PARAM MillSpindle reverse` (`post::ask_reverse_spindle`) and manifest flag `millSpindleReverse`; `fanuc.cps` declares it and writes `M4`; the engine refuses such a section by name for every other script (the lathe's #629 `SpindleDirection`/`threadHands` is deliberately not reused).
- Gated at the door (create, edit, retool via `thread_op::door`) and again in the kernel. File/MCP keys flattened into the Thread params, additive, written only when not default; the digest clause appears only when not default. Page: Passes tab (schedule, finish, spring, allowance), Feeds tab (spindle, cutter hand).

Defaults are the #894 ride: every existing thread golden (`.cl` and `.nc`) is byte-identical.

## Sources

Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook" (thread cutting: constant-area pass depths, spring pass); Machinery's Handbook ("Thread milling", "Thread cutting": finish pass, climb vs cutter rotation, cutter hand vs spindle); ISO 724 / ISO 965-1 (depths, tolerance scale). No HSMWorks / Fusion material. Decisions in `docs/decisions/988-thread-pass-control.md`.

## How tested

- Kernel (`camcraft-motion`, `machining2d::thread_pass_tests`): `constant_area_passes_decrease_and_each_takes_the_same_chip_area`, `a_finishing_pass_and_spring_passes_land_on_the_final_radius`, `an_allowance_leaves_the_stated_depth_uncut_and_is_refused_past_its_tolerance`, `an_m4_spindle_with_a_left_hand_cut_mill_flips_the_orbit_and_keeps_the_hand`, `a_cutter_hand_against_the_spindle_and_other_nonsense_are_refused_by_name`.
- App (`tests/thread_passes.rs`): clean verify + Fanuc post for decreasing/finish/spring/allowance; M4 left-hand ride posts `M4` on Fanuc and is refused by name on Haas; door refusals at creation; edit gated, undo, project-file round trip.
- Golden: `thread_mill_constant_area_spring_pass.cl` (`golden_cl::thread_mill_constant_area_spring_pass_matches_golden`).
- MCP: `mcp::thread_pass_control_over_the_params_door`.
- UI: `thread_mill_page_tests::the_pass_control_rows_edit_the_draft_and_apply_undoes`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/985-external-threads`: green on the final head (post, motion, app, ui suites; 13.5 min); clippy -D warnings on motion/app/post/ui.
- Refresh (2026-11-13) @ 0d3a6a21: merged #1137's head 4f15b9b3, then upstream/main up to 440a6b8d. Resolutions: tests/mcp.rs and post/js.rs keep both sides (#1196 test, #533 wireEdm flag beside #988's); fanuc.cps keeps both manifest flags (programUnits #902, millSpindleReverse) and the S word takes main's ni() with the PR's M4/M3 choice; main's #1005/#1045 thread fixtures (thread_mill_rim, coarse_rims, hole_wall_flats) state the default ThreadPasses. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 2d6effbb (the head before the last clean merge of main) (post, motion 147 s, app 893 s, ui); after it, thread suites, golden_cl, mcp, posting, recorded_post_streams, the post crate and clippy -D warnings (motion/post/app/ui) re-run green. No existing golden changes; one new CL golden (thread_mill_constant_area_spring_pass.cl).

## Not exercised

- M4 on posts other than Fanuc (they refuse by name). No machine run.
- The issue's last bullet (feed starts at the op's `top_z` R plane rather than each hole's entry) is split out to #1212.

Changelog: Thread milling: decreasing (constant chip area) pass depths, a finishing pass, spring passes, a depth allowance and M4 / left-hand-cut thread mills, internal and external (#988)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #988

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Merge-time refresh (merge of upstream main df90b031, head 9673a77e): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 21.1 min; 3215 tests passed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; golden `wire_taper_angle_punch.nc` unchanged.
- Gate on the pre-refresh head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.
- The `arc` corner rule (lean change rounded over a stated radius) is not offered.
- No UI page field for `edm.taper_angle`. It is machine-file data only, like `edm.codes`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a machine can state an angle-word taper dialect (edm.taper_angle: side rule and mitre/cone corner rule). The wire post writes the angle word, and the verify judges the lean the stated corner rule cuts.

### Review fixes at b1c287a0 (the mutation check on 9673a77e)
Tests only, plus one behaviour-neutral extraction: the angle-word lean in `posting_wire::stream` moved into `angle_lean()` so its three door-shadowed refusals can be unit-tested. No golden or snapshot changed. Each line below was deleted (or neutralised) and its test went RED, then went GREEN again once the line was restored.

| Line (review) | Mutation | Killing test |
|---|---|---|
| `operation/wire_op.rs:176-177` stamp of `taper_angle` | both `h.write` lines dropped | `wire_taper_angle::the_corner_rule_and_the_dialect_each_move_the_stamp` (mitre != cone, U/V != mitre, U/V != cone) |
| `wire-iso.cps:205` `angle4` | refuse line deleted | `script_wire_iso::an_angle_word_section_posts_and_each_missing_piece_is_refused_by_name` (zero taper; WireFourAxis) |
| `wire-iso.cps:210` `acode` | refuse line deleted | same test (no `edm.codes.taper_angle`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:216` `angtpl` | refuse line deleted | same test (template without `{angle}`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:305` `ang` | refuse line deleted | same test (`WireAngle` with no dialect) |
| `posting_wire.rs:166` 4-axis refusal (now in `angle_lean`) | `if false && four` | `posting::wire::tests::an_angle_lean_refuses_a_four_axis_cut_an_unstated_rule_and_an_unresolved_top` |
| `posting_wire.rs:170` `complete()` | rules defaulted | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:171` top unresolved | `top.unwrap_or(0.0)` | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:326` lean changes side | `return Err` deleted | `posting::wire::tests::a_lean_that_changes_side_or_never_leans_is_refused_by_name` |
| `posting_wire.rs:333` no leaning side | `sign.unwrap_or(1.0)` | same test |
| `edm_taper.rs:89` not an object | `if false && !v.is_object()` | `machine::edm_taper::tests::a_taper_angle_not_an_object_or_a_garbled_side_refuses_the_file` |
| `edm_taper.rs:103` `positive` garble | `.unwrap_or(AngleSide::TopLeft)` | same test |
| `edm.rs:81` `"taper_angle"` in `WIRE_KEYS` | key dropped (array of 5) | `machine::edm::tests::a_sinker_stating_taper_angle_is_refused_as_a_wire_key` |
| `motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:222` cone turn-back | `if false && phi.abs() > ...` | `wire_edm::taper::tests::the_cone_rule_refuses_a_ring_that_turns_back_on_itself` |

Why 166/170/171 are pinned and not removed: generation's door (`wire_op::corner_rule`) and the stamp keep these cases out of a real post today. They stay as the post's own guard, so a 4-axis path never posts with angle words if it reaches the post some other way. `angle_lean` makes that guard testable.

Gate on b1c287a0: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (post 7 s, motion 41 s, app 1365 s; 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. title: fix(post): an undeclared post script posts only C sections on a lathe or mill-turn
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- `app::lathe_voice::at_post` (the #1190 door) reads the script's dialect through main's `post::dialect::work_voice` (#1174) - no second parse of `capabilities`:
  - `WorkSpindle` (mask has the turning bit): the door fires for every operation, as before.
  - `ToolSpindle` (mask 1 alone): passes, as before.
  - **`Undeclared`** (no mask naming 1 or 2: absent, 0, 4, a string, negative, non-finite): on a setup whose machine has a work spindle (lathe or mill-turn), the door refuses **every section except a C-axis live-tool section** (`voice_of` == `LiveTool`). That covers milling sections (a turning post would open them on the work spindle) *and* sections that turn the work (a turning kind, an on-centre Drill): only a turning post may post those (maintainer, 2026-11-12, #1232 / PR #1265), an unstated script is not known to be one, and a user's milling post without the line would post them as milling (tool change, `S M3`, the work standing still). The refusal says the script has no `capabilities` line and what to add (`capabilities = 1;` mill, `= 2;` turning), and for a turning section why. On a mill or with no machine an undeclared script passes, as before.
- `at_post` takes the script's name for the refusal (`Option<&str>`): the per-mount post (`posting_mounts.rs`) and the per-op post (`posting_per_op.rs`) pass the setup post's registry name or path from `script_of`; the single-file `post_script` and an explicit script for all mounts pass `None` ("the post script").
- `setup_workholding::work_speed`: the `(Undeclared, Some(_))` arm is unchanged; its stale comment now says what the door does.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1199-undeclared-dialect.md`: option (b) of the issue, with the stricter undeclared rule, a cell-by-cell table, the residual case (an undeclared *lathe* script on a mill / no-machine doc meets no door; not covered by #1265 either) and what was dropped.

Behaviour change for users: a user's own script without `capabilities`, posting anything but a C-axis section on a lathe or mill-turn setup, is refused by name with the one-line fix. Every shipped post states its mask, so no shipped post, golden or registry pairing changes.

## How tested
Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-app` lib `lathe_voice::tests::an_undeclared_script_is_held_to_the_door_on_a_machine_with_a_work_spindle`: undeclared scripts (none, `"2"`, `-1`, `0`, `4`) on a lathe and a mill-turn refuse Face, off-centre Drill, Facing and on-centre Drill by name (missing line, machine, both fixes; turning sections say only a turning post may post them), pass a C-stating live-tool section, and name the script when given; declared `1` / `2` on the same machines behave as stated; on a mill and with no machine everything passes.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_workholding_mill_post.rs` `every_machine_dialect_and_section_cell_gives_its_verdict`: the `undeclared` row is "not judged" on lathe / mill-turn for both sections (the door refuses first), and those cells assert the door's text.
- Unchanged and green: `lathe_voice::tests::the_door_refuses_on_every_turning_dialect_and_passes_every_milling_one`, `post::dialect` tests (main's), `lathe_workholding_kinds::an_undeclared_script_takes_the_stricter_reading` (mill machine, unchanged).

Gate on head `27dee0df` (macOS, debug, all green): camcraft-app lib (147), camcraft-post lib (38); app suites `lathe_workholding_mill_post`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `lathe_workholding_live`, `posting`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `lathe_post`, `per_op_files`, `setup_mounts_post`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, plus every other suite that posts on a lathe / mill-turn machine or touches the post door: `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `lathe_post_g76`, `drill_prior`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `c_axis_live`, `mcp_live`, `setup_post_options`, `post_not_judged`; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Merges cleanly with upstream main (not merged in).

## Not exercised
- The GUI/MCP post entry points end-to-end with a user `.cps` file on disk (they all reach `at_post` through the three post bodies).
- The rest of the app suites (batch tier).

Changelog: A post script that does not state `capabilities` posts only C-axis live-tool sections on a lathe or mill-turn setup; every other section (milling or turning) is refused by name with the manifest line to add, instead of being read as a mill post (#1199)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1199

title: fix(motion): land a rapid only on swept stock; hold the developed band's bore exit and lap kinks to the bar's laws
body:
Stacked on #1138 (on #1080, #1007). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

**#1169 - a rapid landed on a wall strip thinner than a planner cell (safety floor).**
The microlift plan read its landings on the planner's cell bitmap (D/120 = 0.083 mm). A wall strip thinner than a cell that falls between two rows of cell centers is invisible there: the easing laps drop it as "air" and it stands until the last lap. On the narrow slot 14x60 the return over the retract plane (`LinkLaw::high`) rapided to 0.3 mm over the floor at (17.407, 8.956) with a 0.075 mm strip under its rim - the verifier's `RapidInStock`.

- New `adaptive::lift_swept::Swept`: the segments the plan's pieces have cut so far, exactly. `high` lands only where the whole footprint (r - 10 um, the verifier's own footprint) is within r - 12.5 um of a cut segment (2.5 um arc fit + the 10 um chords the verifier reads a posted arc on). The proof is a quadtree over the disc on exact segment distances (1-Lipschitz bound per square, divided to 1 um); where it does not close the landing is refused. Nothing is sampled. The cell test stays as the cheap first reading. The verifier is untouched.
- The hop's landing (`lift_link::landing`) takes a lead point the pieces swept before one only the cells read clear. The hop comes down at plunge feed from over the stock, never in rapid, so with no point proved the cells' choice stands.
- A piece starting exactly where the tool stands is ridden on to at the floor (`lift::ride`) instead of a retract and plunge on one spot. That hop, not the strip, was the slot's "4 descents for 2 levels" (the growth's last piece handing over to the first easing lap at (5.135, 7.312), both in cut).

**#1050 - the held fix (16e129bb), now landable.** `adaptive::conform`: the disc phase out of the entry bore is held on the planner's rim and on a rim twice as coarse (the worse kept); the closing laps' fillet kinks are spread at 4 degrees. The measured pins `R62_LOAD_FACTOR`, `R62_BREAKS` and `BAR_50_BREAKS` are removed; the pins hold the whole bar's laws. No law and no bound loosened.

## Readings (release, Linux x86-64)

Narrow slot 14x60, with #1050's change:

| | verifier | descents (2 levels) | returns | over the retract plane | rides | hops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1 `RapidInStock` | 4 | 200 | 3 | 0 | 1 |
| after | silent | 2 | 199 (1365 mm lifted) | 0 | 2 | 0 |

Out of cut 0.88x the cut (law 1.5), load 15.4 % D, 0 breaks, 14262 moves.

Rotary bars (0.1 mm dexel, law 19.8 % D, no break past 5 deg):

| level | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| r6.2 / 5.7 | 20.3 % D, 0 breaks | 17.3 % D, 0 breaks |
| r6.2 / 5.2 | 20.3 % D, 3 breaks | 17.7 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 6.5, 6.0 | - | 19.5 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 5.5, 5.0 | - | 17.3 %, 18.4 % D, 0 breaks |

Other `adaptive_hsm` fixtures: bore 15.4 % D, rectangle 15.4, L-pocket 15.7, 0 breaks, 2 descents each; island and channel fall back to Offset rings as before.

## Verdict moves

- Narrow slot: `RapidInStock` -> silent; its three returns over the retract plane (leads along the walls, not provable at 12.5 um) became routed lifted returns; one retract hop became a ride.
- r6.2 neck levels and r7 level 5.0: measured pins removed, now under the whole bar's laws.
- App `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (the STEP bore's per-platform exact triple, moves / planar feeds / arcs): the plan moved, as the pin says a planner change will. Linux x86-64 had no triple of its own (it rode the band of the other two, 16100-16260 moves); it now reads **(15561, 14837, 1561)**, two release runs identical, added as its own exact arm. Every level still verifies clean and none falls back (Z 20: 56 microlift returns, 7 rides, 1 retract hop). **The Windows (16197, 15458, 1581) and macOS (16160, 15432, 1571) triples were measured before these changes and could not be re-measured here; they are left as measured, not widened, and will fail on those platforms until re-measured there.** That re-measure is owed before this merges or at the latest at the cut (release tier).
- No golden file and no snapshot changed.

## Tests

New: `lift_swept::tests::a_rapid_landing_on_a_sub_cell_wall_strip_is_refused` (a 0.04 mm strip the cells read clear: `high` refused, allowed once the strip is cut; the hop landing's preference), `lift_swept::tests::a_disc_is_covered_on_the_cut_and_not_a_hair_past_it`, `lift_tests::a_piece_starting_where_the_tool_stands_is_ridden_on_to`.

Run on the final planner code (ba3cdd8e; the commits after it change only docs and the app pin's Linux arm), release, `--include-ignored`:
- motion `adaptive_hsm` 6/6 (`hsm_report_full_resolution` green), `adaptive_band` 2/2, `rotary_adaptive` 6/6, `level_links` 12/12, `pocket3d_hsm` 4/4, `adaptive_orbit_seam` 1/1
- motion lib `adaptive` filter 35/35 (both #1051 budget twins, the slot sweep, the new unit tests)
- app `shoulder_adaptive` 3/3, `roughing2d` 7/7, `pocket_overhead` 2/2, `whole_model_pocket` 5/5 (release, default lane)
- app `pocket3d_hsm` 2/2 (with the Linux triple added; first run red on the band, see Verdict moves)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1051-planning-budget-edge`: green (motion lib + 5 suites, debug)

title: feat(ui): WCS page applies its origin from the footer beside Close, and says where the origin is
body: #870: a Makera Z1 user cut air on their first program because they hadn't understood where the origin was. Then it "took a while to find out how to actually save the setting, as the 'set origin' button is crammed next to a lot of other options". Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a. ## What changed - **Set origin in the footer.** The WCS page's apply button leaves the page body (where it shared a row with *Level*, among the quarter turns) and moves into the property pane's fixed footer, beside *Close* (`egui_app::wcs_footer`). Every other page keeps its plain *Close*. - **Pending edits are flagged.** While the typed X/Y/Z or angles differ from the placed WCS, the footer shows **Origin not applied** in the warning ink. - The position is compared to 1e-9 mm. The angles are compared as rotations, so yaw 360 is not an edit. A non-finite field reads as pending. - The drafts survive a close and reopen, so closing loses nothing silently. Closing does not apply them either. - **The origin in words.** A new pure module, `app::setup_origin`, places the origin against the box the page anchors on (the stock box, else the model's bounds). - A point on one of the 27 anchor points is named, e.g. `top of stock, front-left corner`, `top of stock, centre` or `mid-height of stock, front edge, centred`. - Any other point is given as signed distances from the box's left side, front and top, so it never claims a corner it is not on. - The WCS page states it under its heading: `G54 origin: top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)`. The setup sheet gains an `origin:` line under the WCS numbers. - **Viewport marker:** the WCS axis triad already marks the origin; nothing was added. - **Docs:** `docs/user-guide/work-origin.md`, a short page on where the origin is shown and how to change it. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/870-wcs-set-origin-footer.md`. **Overlap with #759** (@mkinney, open draft, `conflicts`): it splits the WCS page body out of `pages.rs` into `wcs_page.rs` and keeps its own *Set Origin* in the quarter-turn rows. This PR touches the page body in one place only, removing that button. The new code lives in its own files (`wcs_footer.rs`, `setup_origin.rs`). Whichever lands second drops the body button and calls `wcs_footer::origin_line` from the page. ## How it was tested New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/wcs_footer.rs` (structural: painted text, AccessKit labels, coarse placement): - `the_page_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` - `set_origin_sits_in_the_footer_beside_close_and_nowhere_else`: one row, Set origin before Close, below the page body, exactly one apply button, no flag on a fresh page. - `a_typed_origin_is_flagged_until_set_origin_applies_it`: the flag appears, a click on Set origin places the typed X and clears it, and yaw 360 does not raise it. - `app::setup_origin` unit tests: `every_anchor_point_is_named`, `a_point_off_the_anchors_is_given_as_distances_never_as_a_corner`, `a_non_finite_origin_or_box_says_so`. - `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs`: `the_setup_sheet_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` (corner, centre, off-anchor). Two existing ui tests got a taller window, 1280 x 900 instead of 720. The new origin line makes the WCS page one to two rows taller, and at 720 px the bottom of the page scrolls under the footer. The page scrolls; nothing is lost. - `one_wcs::the_wcs_page_shows_the_work_offset_dropdown_and_no_setups_page_pointer`: its bottom note was out of view. - `origin_page_shows_the_anchor_grid_and_arms_pick_mode`: its SE cell click missed. Gates on 8b850a18: - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (CWD `crates/ui`): all green. The lib has 596 passed and 5 ignored; every integration binary passes. - App suites that read the setup sheet or the WCS: `setup_wcs`, `setup_sheet`, `rotated_wcs`, `setup_align`, `program_entry`, `inverted_axis_display`, `setup_stock_source`: all pass. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib setup_origin`: 3 passed. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - No snapshot PNG touched. ## Not exercised - Not looked at in the running app. The layout is pinned structurally only. - On a rotated or aligned setup (#326), "left" and "front" are the world box's, as the anchor grid's compass names already are. - The release-lane pixel snapshots were not run. If one frames the WCS page, it moves at the cut's regeneration. Changelog: WCS page: Set origin sits in the footer beside Close, unapplied edits are flagged, and the page and setup sheet say where the origin is in words ("top of stock, front-left corner") (#870) Effort: medium (the issue's label). Not escalated. ## What it looks like **Before:** the typed origin was applied by a *Set Origin* button tucked into the row of quarter-turn buttons, beside *Level*. It was easy to type new X/Y/Z values, press *Close*, and leave the origin where it was, with nothing on the page saying so. **After:** *Set origin* sits in the footer beside *Close*. A line under the heading says where the origin is in plain words (for example "top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)"). While a typed value is not applied yet, the footer says **Origin not applied**. Fixes #870 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(edm): sinker side burn - a lateral electrode move that burns one wall out by a stated amount
body:
**Stacked on #1166** (#544, `issue/544-sinker-orbits`), which stacks on #1131 (#541) → #560 (#531) → #551 (#530). Retarget it to `main` once its parents merge. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed
- **New op kind, Sinker Side Burn** (`OpType::SinkerSideBurn`, stored id 42, appended; file key `sinker_side_burn`). Its params are `SinkerSideBurnOp { burn: SinkerBurnOp, direction, amount, undersize }`:
  - The burn's plunge is #541's struct, embedded whole, with the op's **own** condition. It takes no orbit; an orbit is refused by name.
  - Then one lateral Feed of `amount` along +X, -X, +Y or -Y at the floor, the same Feed back to the burn point, and the rapid retract.
  - #541's door (`sinker::check`) and condition read (`sinker_op::condition_gap_as`) are reused, not copied.
- **Allowance law** (`motion::sinker_side`): `allowance = undersize - gap`. Refused by name:
  - a move past the allowance ("... toward +X burns into the part - the side's allowance is 0.150 (undersize 0.200 less spark gap 0.050)");
  - a gap the undersize can't honour;
  - a non-finite, zero or negative amount;
  - a bad undersize;
  - an orbit.
- **Validated at command creation** (`gates::sinker_gate`, on CreateOperation, PasteOperation, EditOperationParams and ChangeOperationKind, ahead of `is_sane` so the refusal is by name):
  - always: the structural refusals above;
  - once a condition is named on a sinker EDM: an unknown condition, the gap against the undersize, and the allowance.

  An unnamed condition stays a draft (the ribbon's seed) and is refused at generation. Generation, the staleness stamp and the sim plan re-run the whole law (`sinker_side_op::side_gap`). A machine that later re-states a wider gap therefore refuses the stored op by name.
- The stock sim sweeps every move with the existing box atom. No new sim law.
- **MCP:** through the params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation` with `direction` / `amount` / `undersize`). `list_operation_types` lists the kind. No new command, so no new MCP tool.
- **UI:** only the minimal rows on the existing sinker page's Passes tab (wall, amount, undersize, in place of the orbit rows), plus the contour glyph for its row. The full pages are #548's. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- **Files:** an appended DTO variant (the burn's keys flattened, plus the three side keys). Old files load unchanged.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/545-sinker-side-burn.md`.

## How tested
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_side.rs` (new):
  - `a_side_burn_moves_the_faced_wall_by_its_amount_in_the_sim`: for each of the four directions, at a 0.05 column grid:
    - the faced wall stands at electrode + gap + amount: the column centre just inside it is burned to the floor and **the next column out is untouched**;
    - the far wall and the walls across the move stay at the plunge's gap;
    - the program verdict reports 0 gouge cells.
  - `a_lateral_move_past_the_allowance_is_refused_by_name`:
    - refused at creation: a move past the allowance, past the undersize, a gap past the undersize, an unknown condition, a NaN/inf/negative/zero amount, a bad undersize;
    - at the allowance exactly, the op is admitted; an edit past it is refused;
    - after a remount with a wider gap, generation refuses by name and the op is left unchanged.
  - `an_undersize_overstated_against_the_part_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`: the part's cavity lacks the claimed undersize, so the sim reports a gouge.
  - `the_side_burn_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: save and load, then `list_operation_types`, add, generate, an edit past the allowance refused, edit, undo.
  - `sinker_side_burn_matches_golden`: new golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_side_burn.cl`, read by hand. Rapid to (12.5, -7.5, 25), plunge to Z 14.05 (floor 14 + gap 0.05), lateral -Y 0.15 to Y -7.65, back to -7.5, rapid to Z 25. Five moves.
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_side`: `sinker_side_moves_along_its_axis_by_the_amount_and_back` and `sinker_side_refuses_past_the_allowance_by_name`.
- `ribbon` (the last kind is now SinkerSideBurn) and `coarse_laws` (SinkerSideBurn is a stated refusal on a reduced model, like SinkerBurn).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 7bdd2505. Tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites, and every app integration binary, were green. That includes coarse_laws, sinker_burn, sinker_orbit, sinker_side, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, operations, ribbon and mcp. The app lib's `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` failed on the kind count (42 -> 43); b8191744 bumps the pin, and `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` is green on the final head (138 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- Not exercised on a real EDM control: the conditions are synthetic.
- Posting waits on #542 (the sinker post). This PR emits no new PARAM.
- No wear compensation (#546) and no electrode generation (#547).

Changelog: Sinker EDM side burn: a lateral electrode move burns one wall out by a stated amount, bounded by the op's own undersize less its condition's spark gap; a move into the part is refused by name (#545)
Effort: high

Fixes #545

title: feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule
body:
Stacked on #1163 (`issue/536-wire-taper` @ b14882ea, merged into this branch first). The wire base #1139, #1144, #1147 and #1160 are merged to main; #1150 and #1158 are pending. Merge order: #1163, then this PR. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A Wire Contour can now cut the ruled surface between two profiles given separately (#290 D2).

- **Op.** `WireContourOp.four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>` (`pairing`, `sync`, `tolerance`); absent by default, omitted from the file when absent, so a one-profile cut's file, stamp, CL and NC are unchanged. The pairing rule has no default in the file. Edited through `EditOperationParams` / the MCP parameter patch (the same JSON door); the page shows the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
- **Profiles.** The selection is read as two picks (a face's one outer ring, or a closed edge chain), each flat; the higher is the upper profile. Their heights must be the op's top and bottom planes (`app::operation::wire_ruled`).
- **Pairing** (`motion::wire_edm::pairing`). One monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors: by normalised arc length from each profile's point nearest the start hole, or by sync pairs with arc length between them. A ruling at every vertex of either ring; each move ends on a ruling's lower point, its pose the wire toward the upper point; upright at the start hole. The path's note states the rule.
- **Laws** (`motion::wire_edm::ruled_laws`). Fold: consecutive rulings whose ends run against each other (`a . b < 0` - the section turns back inside the part height). Crossing: the wire's section at a quarter height crosses itself. Ruled kerf: at 33 heights the wire's section stands off the stated surface by #1163's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)`.
- **A twisted ruled surface.** A straight wire cannot touch it along its whole height, so offsetting both profiles by the kerf gouges between the planes (about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf). The generator widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear at every height read, says in the notes how much stands on the profile planes, and refuses past the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm). A constant taper needs exactly #1163's `1 / cos(angle)`.
- **Refused by name:** crossed sync points ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"), doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points, a folding or self-crossing pairing, open profiles or one open and one closed, a ruling past `edm.max_taper_deg` (unstated refuses), a twist past the tolerance, profiles that are not two / not flat / not on the op's planes, a taper angle stated beside the two profiles, a lead whose leaning kerf enters the surface. The U/V stroke, U/V axes, guide planes and guide reach are #1163's machine check, unchanged (it reads poses).
- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's; kerf, threading and slug run at every judged height; a gouge blocks the post.
- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; `wire-iso.cps` writes the same `taper_on` / `uv` / `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes` as a tapered section and names the cut in a comment.

## Sources (Clean Room)

Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surface between two parametrised curves, chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", CAD 27(12), 1995. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`.

## Refresh (2026-11-13: #1163's refresh merged in, then upstream main @ a5d1a763)

- Kept both sides (also `operation/types/mod.rs` against main's `SinkerPass` export): #1163's burnout, open-run clearance and sinker fields sit beside `four_axis` in the op, DTO, job, page and every `WireContourOp` test literal.
- A 4-axis cut with a no-core burnout is refused by name (the burnout is cut vertical only), like #1163's taper + burnout refusal. Open profiles and a left/right side stay refused by the ruled generator.
- Verify still reads a 4-axis cut's poses as the wire's lean, and the leaning kerf is judged at every height. The new `burnout` flag is carried through.
- Main's posted-golden law asks a gate to judge every posted golden. `crates/app/tests/posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs` regenerates `wire_4axis_punch.cl` (byte-identical) and judges it with `taper: true` against the loft's own mesh, sliced at 25 heights: no finding, and the punch frees the part (`solid_law_goldens::the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates`). No law was loosened.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wire_4axis.rs`
  - `a_square_to_round_punch_posts_its_golden_and_verifies` - goldens `tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` (a pose on every move) and `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` (synthetic fixture); the wire clause reports no problem.
  - `a_constant_taper_by_sync_points_is_the_taper_golden_and_arc_length_differs` - the CL equals #1163's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte, the NC equals `wire_taper_punch.nc` but for the comment naming the cut; arc length on the same two profiles gives other rulings.
  - `crossed_folded_and_unpaired_sync_points_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pairing_past_the_machine_or_off_the_planes_is_refused_by_name` (max taper at generation, U stroke at the post, one profile, taper + 4-axis, planes off the profiles)
  - `a_ruling_that_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
  - `the_four_axis_block_round_trips_and_its_rule_is_never_defaulted` (JSON door, stamp, undo, the door's refusal of a NaN tolerance)
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_tests.rs` (8 tests): square-to-round keeps the kerf out and a zero tolerance refuses it; arc length vs sync points; the constant taper equals `wire_contour_tapered` move for move; crossed / folded / unpaired / off-profile / doubled sync points; open and mismatched profiles; steep rulings; a conical die.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/536-wire-taper` green on the final head 263442bc (motion lib, the whole app suite set - a new golden is shared test input - and the mapped ui suites; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture with invented codes.
- The die side at the app level (the motion crate pins a conical die); a die whose start hole is equidistant from several sides has no single nearest point - its arc-length seam is then the first tie, and a pairing that folds or twists for it is refused, not guessed.
- A model whose tessellated twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface of its two end profiles is refused by the wire laws as a gouge (the fixtures here are split along the inner diagonal). Follow-up #1170.
- Sync points are numbers on the page, not viewport picks (#1171). Fans and profiles stitched from several runs are refused by name (#1172). Open-profile 4-axis waits for #1109.
- UI: the new rows have no structural-test assertion of their own; no snapshot PNG was changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's DTO notes are not updated (a process file); the block rides `params` through the existing tools (#1108).

Changelog: Wire EDM 4-axis: a Wire Contour cuts the ruled surface between separately picked upper and lower profiles, paired by arc length or by sync points; crossed, folding or unpaired pairings, rulings past the machine's taper and U/V limits and a twist past the stated tolerance are refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #537

title: fix(turning): read a lathe holder body on the holder's own side of the axis
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 7e3c75f9).

## What changed

The holder law (#369) read a lathe body point at `|X + x|`, with `X` signed along the path's signed meridian (`SignedMeridian`). That frame takes its + side from the path's **first** off-axis point, which need not be the side the holder stands on. Take a rear tool that starts a hair past centre: every later tip is at X < 0 of that frame, and the body was read mirrored through the axis. A lip reaching the part was judged clear, and a clear body was judged to cross the axis.

- New `crates/app/src/operation/turning_holder_side.rs`: `sided` gives the holder's side as a property of the whole path, read from its moves' meridian pieces. A rigid holder never flips mid-path, so the side is the one the path reaches farthest on. The other side may hold only a past-centre overrun of at most `PAST_CENTRE` = 2.5 mm, as in a face pass cleaning the centre pip, while the far side reaches beyond twice it. A path on both sides beyond that, or whose far side stays under 5 mm while the near side is off the axis, is refused by name: "the lathe holder body cannot be judged: the path stands on both sides of the spindle axis ...". A round XY arc about the axis (a thread's half-turn, whose ends alternate onto the antipode) tells no side: it is left out of the reading and read at |rho| on the holder's side.
- `turning_holder::judge` reads `Reach::radii(side * X)`. On the + side the call is `radii(x)` exactly as before, so it is byte-identical. `body_axes`, which draws the body (#1038), flips its radial by the same side, so the drawn holder is still the judged one.
- `camcraft-tools::lathe_holder`: the docs now state that X is signed along the holder's own +x, which is away from the axis on the holder's side, front or rear post alike.

**Which signed X the generators produce.** Every turning generator places its straight moves' tips at `Frame::point(rho >= 0, ..)`, and a face pass runs to `rho = 0` at most. Threading is the exception: its half-turn arcs end on `Frame::antipode`, at -rho, by construction - so the side is read with those round arcs left out, and they are read at |rho| (as `kerf_of` already does). Every other generated tip is at X >= 0 of its own frame and reads as before. No turning op today carries a straight-move tip at X < 0, so the defect was latent and the issue stays P2, not re-rated P0. This is stated in the pinning tests and in `docs/decisions/1102-lathe-body-signed-reach.md`.

**UI/MCP wording.** Main has no "+x points away from the spindle axis" text. That text is in #1043, and under this law it is now true as written. No wording change was needed here.

**Expected merge with #1043 / #1061.** This PR touches only the reach reading in `turning_holder.rs` (a `side` field on `Scene`, one `sided_pieces` call in `judge` and one in `body_axes`, and the `radii` argument), plus a new module. Merging either way should be additive.

## How tested

- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::the_side_is_where_the_path_reaches_and_a_past_centre_overrun_keeps_it`: front paths are +1, a face run 0.4 past centre keeps +1, and a rear path starting 0.5 past centre is -1. Both-sides paths are refused by name, and so are a near side off the axis with a far side under 5 mm (`[2, -3]`) and a non-finite radius.

title: feat(edm): sinker orbit patterns (circular, vector, planetary) as explicit moves
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (M5's #541, sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`). Retarget to `main` before #1131 merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed

A Sinker Burn can now **orbit at the burn floor** after the plunge. The orbit is circular, vector or planetary, and it is expanded into explicit Feed chords (#290 D3), so the 3-axis stock sim's box atom (#541) verifies every move that would post. Corner joins are included, under the same laws as #541's burns.

- `motion::sinker_orbit` (new) holds the pattern geometry.
  - circular: out along +X to the radius, then one full circle;
  - vector: out to the radius and back along N evenly spaced directions from +X;
  - planetary: an Archimedean spiral from 0 to the radius over N turns, closed by a full circle.
  - Every vertex is on or inside the stated radius (an ulp-past rounding is pulled back in), so no chord overshoots it. Chords keep a sagitta of 0.001 mm or less. Their count is a multiple of 4, so the ±X/±Y directions are vertices and a rectangular electrode's walls move out by exactly the radius. The counts are bounded (vectors 1..=72, turns 1..=20), so an orbit cannot balloon into a hang.
- `motion::sinker::burn_to_depth` runs the orbit at the tip Z at the servo feed and returns to the centre before the rapid retract. With `orbit: None` the plain plunge's CL and params digest are unchanged.
- `SinkerBurnOp.orbit: Option<SinkerOrbit>` is an additive field and file key (`orbit: { kind, radius, vectors, turns }`), so old files load. It is edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`. MCP reaches it through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`, `"orbit": null` drops it). There is no new command, so there is no new MCP tool. The minimal sinker page gets Orbit / radius / vectors / turns rows on Passes.
- **Machine law** (`sinker_op::orbit_law`, #290 D6), refused by name at generation:
  - `machine X lists no vector orbit under edm.orbits ...`
  - `machine X states no maximum orbit radius (edm.max_orbit_radius) ...` (absent is not unlimited)
  - `the circular orbit radius 0.600 exceeds machine X's maximum orbit radius 0.500`
  - The job and the staleness stamp read it through `burn_gap`, so a re-stated orbit list or maximum marks the op stale. A garbled orbit is refused at the door (`is_sane`).
- **No schema change.** `edm.orbits[]` and `edm.max_orbit_radius` already exist in the `.mch` edm section from #530 (on this base), and #1141's post reads the same fields. They are read as they are. This PR emits no `EdmOrbit` PARAM: the orbit posts as its explicit moves, and a canned word on top would be a double orbit (D3's later item).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/544-sinker-orbits.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/sinker_orbit.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `sinker_orbit_circular_matches_golden`: golden `tests/golden/sinker_orbit_circular.cl`, which I read. It has the plunge to Z 14.050, out to +0.200 X, 32 CCW chords on the r = 0.2 circle back to +X, a return to the centre, and the retract. Max excursion is 0.200.
  - `a_circular_orbit_widens_the_simulated_cavity_by_its_radius`: on the simulated stock (0.05 cell), the cavity floor reaches electrode + gap + radius on ±X and ±Y, and the next column out stands untouched. The same burn without the orbit stops one radius short. The furthest move is the radius exactly.
  - `every_orbit_pattern_stays_in_its_radius_and_verifies_clean`: all three patterns stay inside the radius with chords only, and `simulate_document` finds 0 gouge cells in the orbit-sized cavity.
  - `an_orbit_wider_than_the_parts_cavity_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`
  - `an_unlisted_pattern_and_an_over_radius_orbit_are_refused_by_name`: also covers the unstated maximum (refused), radius == max (admitted), and the garbled-orbit door.
  - `the_orbit_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: file round trip, MCP add, an over-max edit refused at generate, undo, an unlisted pattern refused, `orbit: null` back to a plunge.
- `motion::sinker_orbit` unit tests: every pattern for radii 0.0005..12 is inside its radius and closes on the centre; the chord tolerance holds and the axis directions are vertices; garbled numbers are refused by name.
- `sinker_burn.rs` (#541) is unchanged apart from `orbit: None` in its literals, and its golden is byte-identical.
- Gate: the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `49904407` ran tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui: 3437 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model` ("SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left"). It is **pre-existing on the #1131 base**: I reproduced it on the base tree without this commit. `fidelity_law.rs` refuses `Section::Sinker`, but the test's `refused` list has no `SinkerBurn`. This PR touches neither file. It belongs to #1131.
- The sinker suites (`sinker_burn`, `sinker_orbit`), `edm_machine`, `edm_conditions`, `golden_cl` and `project_roundtrip` are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The fixtures are synthetic: an invented condition, invented orbit words and an invented 0.5 mm maximum.
- Posting waits on #542 (#1141). That post refuses arcs, and how it treats the lateral orbit chords has not been checked here. The post script is untouched.
- The stock view / playback (field eye) still refuses an electrode by name (#541), so the orbit is judged by the program verdict's column engine only.
- The minimal sinker page gains orbit rows; #548's full pages (PR #1165) will need them carried over.
- Interaction with #543's undersize (PR #1136) and #546's wear compensation was not exercised. Both touch the same op, and whichever merges second may need a small merge.

Changelog: Sinker Burn orbits (circular, vector, planetary) at the burn floor, expanded into explicit moves the stock sim verifies; a pattern the machine does not list, or a radius past its stated maximum, is refused by name (#544, PR #1166)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #544
