title: feat(threadmill)!: thread-mill tool kinds and a reworked helical thread-milling operation
body:
## What changed

First slice of #894: thread mills can be stored, and an internal thread-milling operation verifies clean and posts helical G2/G3 with Z.

**Tool model**
- Two new tool kinds: `thread_mill` (multi-form: rows of teeth at one pitch) and `thread_mill_single` (single-form: one row, a pitch range). They read diameter (across the crests), form angle (`tip_angle`), `pitch`, cutting length (`flute_len`), flutes and shank; a single-form mill also reads the new `pitch_min` key. Sanity law, pitch door and form door live in `crates/tools/src/thread_mill.rs`.
- Library and project file round-trip (`pitch_min` is written only when set; additive, no project-version step), the tool editor (kind list, pitch / pitch range / form angle rows, a sane draft when the kind is picked), the tree's kind name, the operation digest, and two starter-catalog tools (`TM-0600-P125`, `TMS-0600-P050-150`).
- The program simulation sweeps a thread mill at its tooth roots, the reading a tap already has (#266).

**Thread operation** (the existing `Thread` kind, reworked)
- The kernel is rewritten (`machining2d/thread_mill.rs`, `thread_ride.rs`): radial passes are full helices (equal steps, the last on the thread depth), a single-form mill winds one turn per thread, a multi-form mill makes one revolution per level; tangential lead-in / lead-out arcs that keep the helix's axial rate; climb / conventional and right / left hand by the handbook rule; the tip never below the floor, no rapid below the feature's top; the feed stated at the cutting edge and programmed at the tool centre.
- New operation fields `pitch` (optional: unstated reads a multi-form mill's own) and `hand`; both in the file, the page (Passes tab) and the MCP `add_operation` / `edit_operation` params.
- Refusals by name when the operation is created, edited, retyped or re-tooled, and again at generate: a pitch outside a single-form mill's range, a pitch other than a multi-form mill's, a form angle other than 60 degrees, an infeed past the thread depth, a mill no smaller than a hole's minor diameter, a zero / negative / non-finite pitch. A single-form mill with the pitch not stated yet is an unfinished operation (a new Thread operation starts that way): it may be made and edited, and generate refuses it by name.
- Gouge laws (main's #1071 readings since the refresh, behind this PR's round-wall gate): the tooth crests are judged against the major circle of the model's own wall (`thread_rims::major_rims`, tangency law); the solid law keeps the full cutter and excuses only the thread's own wall and mouth inside that major cylinder (`verify::thread_bore`), at the thread's own pitch (`thread_op::bores`). Both apply only where every threaded hole is a round wall (`thread_op::walls_round`, #1205); otherwise the teeth are judged at full radius. The crossing law stands down for Thread only (successive passes' lead arcs cross in plan by design).

**Why the kernel was rewritten rather than extended** - on `main` no Thread operation can post: the old ride retraces itself (the crossing law convicts every pair) and stands past the hole rim (the tangency law convicts every move). It also deepened the radius turn by turn while descending, so the top threads were shallower than the bottom ones, and its "climb" wound counter-clockwise while descending, which is a left-hand helix. Details and sources: `docs/decisions/894-thread-mill.md`.

## Breaking

- A `Thread` operation no longer accepts a Tap-kind tool (`tool_law::THREAD_MILL` was `[Tap]`). An existing one shows the tool law's after-state and refuses to generate or post until its tool is re-kinded as a thread mill.
- Every existing `Thread` operation reads Stale once (its digest now carries pitch and hand) and regenerates to the new ride.
- `Tool` gains the field `pitch_min`: a branch that builds a full `Tool { .. }` literal needs `pitch_min: 0.0` after it merges main.

## How tested

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a; refreshed against upstream/main 0ad525d8 in merge `f3dd45c4`).

Gate on the final head `f3dd45c4`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (the diff falls back to the batch plan) - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app suites and clippy `-D warnings` over all eight crates: ok. The ui step failed one test on the first run (`tool_thread_mill_row` still named the thread mills' kind numbers 13 and 14; they are 14 and 15 after main's Electrode took 13); fixed in the test, and the ui step re-run as the gate runs it: 643 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, the other ui binaries ok. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Thread suites on the head: `thread_mill` 8, `thread_mill_rim` 11 (main's #1071 pins, on the new kernel), `hole_wall_flats` 5, `solid_law_goldens` 7 (incl. `the_thread_golden_passes_its_gate` and `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`), `coarse_rims` 5, `mill2d_c` 9 - all passed.

Main moved once more after the merge (#1319, b0e29114, the verify's mid-turn sweep). It is not in this head; the PR merges with it cleanly, and a local trial merge passed the thread suites above plus `golden_cl` (29).

## Refresh against main (merge `f3dd45c4`, 27 conflicting files)

Most conflicts were both-sides-added lists (tool kinds, catalog, icons, UI rows, tests, `Tool` fields) and keep both. The judgements, recorded in `docs/decisions/894-thread-mill.md` ("The refresh against main"):

1. Region law: main's `major_rims` (#1071) replaces this PR's `crest_region` (main's circle grows from the model's own rim and is never wider), kept behind this PR's `walls_round` gate.
2. Solid law: main's thread grant with the full cutter replaces this PR's `root_cutter`, which credited the thread depth against every facet. The two are not stacked. `crest_region`, `root_cutter` and their unit tests are removed.
3. The grant reads the thread's own pitch (`thread_op::bores`): main passed `tool.pitch`, which on a single-form mill is only the coarsest of its range and would over-grant. Empty over a wall that is not round.
4. The crossing stand-down stays: tried off on the merged tree, 2 `thread_mill` and 5 `thread_mill_rim` tests convict.
5. Tool kind numbers: main's Electrode keeps 13, the thread mills take 14 and 15 (stamp digest in `stamp_tool.rs`, tool page list, `state.rs`).
6. Main's `thread_mill_rim.rs` and `coarse_rims.rs` mounted a Tap on a Thread op, which this PR refuses; they now mount a thread mill and state pitch and hand. No assertion changed.

No golden moved, no snapshot PNG, no process file.

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-tools` (lib): `thread_mill::tests::*` (4) - the two kinds' sanity, the pitch door, the form door.
- `camcraft-motion` (lib): `machining2d::thread_tests::*` (8) - hand and orbit sense for all 16 hand / climb / internal-external / form combinations, equal passes landing on the ISO depth, one shared helix across passes and levels, floor and no-rapid-below-top laws, the lead arcs' form law (a 60-degree tooth never leaves the groove), the centre-feed scaling, a boss never cut past its depth, the refusals.
- `camcraft-app` `--test thread_mill` (8): M8 x 1.25 with the multi-form mill and M8 x 1 with the single-form mill through the command path - no blocking warning, the post gate passes, the program simulation finds no gouge, Fanuc output carries `G03 ... Z ... I ...` blocks; left-hand and conventional variants; a mill whose roots meet the wall is a gouge; a bottom below the blind floor is a gouge; the creation-time refusals; a gated, undoable pitch edit; tool JSON and project-file round trip.
- `camcraft-app` (lib): `operation::thread_op::tests::*` (2) - the thread grant reads the thread's own pitch and only over a round wall, the crossing stand-down is Thread-only.
- `camcraft-app` `--test thread_mill_rim` (11, main's #1071 pins) and `--test hole_wall_flats` (5): a wider or off-centre declaration, a D-bore, an octagon, a 16-gon, a floor and a nearby wall convict; matched threads stay clean.
- `camcraft-app` `--test solid_law_goldens`: `the_thread_golden_passes_its_gate` (`posted_gates/thread.rs`).
- `camcraft-app` `--test mill2d_c`: the M2.4 C thread tests, updated to the new ride and tool kind.
- `camcraft-app` `--test mcp`: `thread_milling_over_the_tools`.
- `camcraft-ui` (lib): `egui_app::tool_thread_mill_row::tests::picking_a_thread_mill_kind_seeds_a_sane_tool_and_round_trips`, `egui_app::thread_mill_page_tests::the_thread_page_states_the_pitch_and_the_hand_and_apply_undoes`.
- `camcraft-app` `--test tool_gate` / `--test tool_law`: updated for the new kinds (the Thread row's catalog hint is now `TM-0600-P125`).

Goldens added (none moved):
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_multi_form_left_hand.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_external_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_fine_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc`

## Known gap (read before merging)

- **An undrilled hole is not refused.** A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the ride feeds it down the hole's axis. Nothing yet checks that an earlier operation opened the hole: on a part whose hole is modelled, a Thread operation with no drilling before it generates and verifies clean. Before this PR no Thread operation could post at all, so this path is newly reachable. The check needs the stock the earlier operations leave standing (the grid `operation::drill_prior` reads) and is filed as #992 (`bug`, P1). The tests here thread a modelled hole in a solid stock box with no drill before it - they pin the ride and the part laws, not that entry.

## What was not exercised

- External threads at the operation level: the kernel cuts a boss and is pinned by tests and a golden, but the operation always passes `external: false` (no boss recognition or pick, and the static region cannot judge a tool beside a boss). Filed as #985.
- The thread form in the simulation and the tool preview: the stock sim removes the root cylinder only, and the tool draws as the cylinder its crests sweep. Filed as #986.
- Forms other than 60 degrees (Whitworth, NPT taper, trapezoidal) are refused, not cut. Filed as #987.
- Spring passes, unequal pass depths, a stated thread-depth override and M4 (left-hand cutter) climb sense. Filed as #988.
- Posts other than Fanuc were not run on a thread program; the inverted-machine post path already refuses a helical arc by name (`post/invert.rs`) and was not changed.
- The UI rows were compiled and unit-tested through the draft; no pixel snapshot was touched and the release-lane snapshot suite was not run.
- The heavy `--ignored` release lanes and the batch tier's clippy over untouched crates.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill text does not yet mention the new kinds and fields (a process file; it would need a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump). Filed as #989 (`MCP:`).

title: docs(process): add test-placement, crate-edge and app-scope rules
body:
## What changed

Process-only (docs). Three placement rules are added to AGENTS.md, named in the PR-reviewer checklist and the work-issue skill. PROCESS_VERSION 18.

Quoted as added:

**AGENTS.md "Code shape"** (two bullets, after "One concern per subcrate"):

- **`app` holds the document, nothing else** (maintainer, 2026-11-11: "high cohesion, low coupling, because every gate is costly"). New code goes in `crates/app/src` only if it reads or writes the ECS world, the project file, a command, MCP or the CLI. Code that works only on domain values (cl, geometry, tools, post, sim, motion types) goes in the crate that owns them, and `app` re-exports it. A reviewer checks this from the new file's `use` lines: if none names one of those six things, the file is in the wrong crate.
- **No new dependency between our crates without a decision.** A `camcraft-*` entry added to `[dependencies]` or `[dev-dependencies]` in any `crates/*/Cargo.toml` needs a `docs/decisions/` entry in the same PR. The entry lists the imported items, says why the caller cannot pass the value in instead (a parameter, a closure, a recorded file), and names what now rebuilds when the dependency changes. An edge that would carry fewer than five items is not added: the caller passes the value in. (The wording of the five-item clause is the maintainer's to confirm.)

**AGENTS.md "Testing"** (the `crates/app/tests/` line is corrected, then one rule added):

- **A test lives with the code it tests.** A new test file goes in the lowest crate that provides everything it imports, and its Gate map names that crate (`camcraft_post::engine`, not `app::post`). A file in `crates/app/tests/` must import something `crates/app/src` defines; a test that uses only another crate's re-exports (`app::post`, `app::verify`, `app::machining2d`) belongs in that crate's `tests/`. A test that needs another crate's output reads a recorded file (`.cl`, `.cnc`) rather than importing that crate's generator.

Also: `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md` law check gets a "Placement" item naming (a), (b), (c); `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md` section 2 names the same three rules. `docs/decisions/920-placement-rules.md` records the decision.

## Decision on the fourth rule

The research proposed a fourth rule (a new test joins an existing suite). It is not in this PR: it waits for directory suites in xtask and for timings (#919 research, Q5).

## Maintainer to confirm

The "fewer than five items" wording of the crate-edge clause is as proposed in the #919 research. Its exact wording is the maintainer's to confirm on this PR.

## How tested

Docs and process only. No code changed, so no test was run for the change. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans "nothing in crates/ changed: no tests to run". `git diff --stat`: 5 files (AGENTS.md, PR-reviewer.md, work-issue SKILL.md, PROCESS_VERSION, the decision file).

## Not exercised

No review by a second agent yet; the rules' effect on future PR reviews is untested.

## Process

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16 at the fork point). PR #963 also bumps PROCESS_VERSION to 17; whichever PR merges second takes 18 when it merges main.

On merge, announce on #681: `PROCESS_VERSION 18` · PR #<this PR> · AGENTS.md test-placement / crate-dependency / app-scope rules · forks: normal process sync.

Changelog: none

Fixes #920

title: feat(post)!: the document's unit is the unit every post writes the program in
body:
#961 (its former parent) is merged; this branch has taken upstream/main.

**PathPilot Hub run (done 2026-11-12, 770MX sim):** `contour_plate_with_hole` inch (byte-identical to this branch's `golden/nc/inch/tormach/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`) ran to M30, 1:19, dimensions matching the mm reference. `drill_peck` inch alarmed `G73 Cannot feed with zero feed rate`: the fixture carries no feed/tool/spindle, the same in main's mm golden - filed as #1357, not caused here; #1357's own kit (T4 M6, F2.36) then passed. No inch program with rotary words was Hub-run.
Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed

The document's Units choice (`SetUnits`, already undoable and saved as `units`) is now also the unit every post writes the program in. One setting: the machine file's `units.length` no longer chooses anything; it only says what unit the file's own numbers are in.

- **Seam.** The app adds `Units: "mm" | "inch"` to `postOptions` on every post path (whole program, per-operation files, per-mount files) via `posting::program_options`. The stream stays mm. `post.exe` takes `--units mm|inch`.
- **Manifest law (`post::units`).** A script that can write inch declares `programUnits = "mm inch"`. An inch document on a script that doesn't is refused by name before any hook runs. This includes a user's own pre-#902 script. An unknown unit word is refused too.
- **Posts that write inch:** Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Doosan DNM (G20), and Siemens 840D (G700, the G710 twin). Lengths are written / 25.4 at four decimals and feeds in in/min at two. Angles, seconds and rpm are unchanged. The macro probe checks' band is one output step. The three Tormach posts now take the unit from the document instead of `machine.units`.
- **Posts that refuse inch by name:** Makera Carvera (its firmware is mm only), Heidenhain (#976) and Fanuc Lathe (#977). For Heidenhain and Fanuc Lathe, inch output needs verified dialect work, not a guess.
- **Old projects post byte-identical.** `PROJECT_VERSION` is now 60 (main took 59 meanwhile). A file at v59 or older opens on the unit its programs used to post in, taken from its machine files. If that differs from its saved display unit, a load note explains the change. A file whose setups posted in mixed units keeps its display unit, and a note names each setup whose unit changes.
- **UI.** The Post section (document/setup Post page) gets a "Program units" mm / inch row. It is the same `SetUnits` as the Stock page's Units row, now shared code. The post status line names the unit.
- **MCP.** New `set_units` tool (one undo step). `get_job` reports `units`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (the `Units` word, the `programUnits` manifest). Decisions: `docs/decisions/902-document-units.md`.

**Behaviour change / breaking:** a new document on an inch machine file now posts mm until the document is set to inch. This covers every shipped Tormach machine. Older builds refuse v60 project files.

## How tested

Pinning tests (new):
- `crates/app/tests/program_units.rs`
  - `every_inch_post_writes_the_mm_program_in_inches`: 6 posts × 8 mill goldens. Each inch program is checked word by word against the same post's mm program: the unit word swaps, lengths are / 25.4, feeds are / 25.4, and every other word is equal. The unit word comes before the first motion. `Units: "mm"` is byte-identical to no unit at all. Inch goldens are committed under `golden/nc/inch/<post>/` (contour_plate_with_hole, drill_peck).
  - `a_post_that_cannot_write_inch_refuses_the_document_by_name` (Carvera, Heidenhain, Fanuc Lathe)
  - `a_script_that_declares_no_units_refuses_inch_and_posts_mm`
  - `no_shipped_post_takes_the_program_unit_from_the_machine_file`
  - `an_inch_machine_file_no_longer_makes_an_inch_program`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_units.rs::the_document_unit_is_the_posted_unit_through_undo_and_save` covers the end-to-end path over MCP: a Fanuc face job posts G21; `set_units` inch posts G20 with X / 25.4; Carvera refuses by name; save and reopen keep inch; undo gives back the identical mm program. Also `set_units_refuses_nonsense_and_no_ops`.
- `crates/app/tests/units_migrate.rs` (5 tests): the v59 → v60 rung in four cases (inch machine, inch display on a metric machine, matching display, mixed-unit setups), plus a v60 file that keeps its unit whatever the machine.
- `crates/post/src/post/units.rs` unit tests (unit word, manifest law).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/program_units.rs::the_post_page_sets_the_program_unit_through_set_units`

Updated: the Tormach, plasma, microARC, probe and Carvera suites. Before this change, several of them used "an inch machine file" to mean "an inch program". Each now states an inch document instead: `SetUnits` in world tests, `Units` in engine tests. Their goldens are unchanged. `carvera_post::an_inch_machine_is_refused_by_name` became `an_inch_document_is_refused_by_name`. It now also pins that an inch machine file alone still posts G21.

**Goldens:** no existing golden moved; the mm output is byte-identical (conformance and every post suite green). New: 12 inch goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/`.

Gate (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/869-coolant-air` green: post, app (every app suite, since a shared test helper changed) and ui suites, 10.2 min, 0 failed. `.cps` changes are not gate-mapped (#923), but the whole app set ran, which covers every post suite (conformance, the per-post suites, post_unit_word). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- PathPilot Hub: see the top - the Tormach inch contour passed; no rotary inch program was Hub-run.

- No hand test on a real control in inch.
- Sinumerik G700 rests on the published G710/G700 pairing. It has not been run on an 840D.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table (`.claude/skills/`, a process file) is not updated with `set_units`. That needs a PROCESS_VERSION bump, so it is left for the maintainer.
- Overlap: #258 (Post dialog, in review) touches the same post section UI.
- Found while testing, not caused here: #978 (MCP `open_project` over a non-empty document duplicates its operations).

Review fixes (#981 M3 review, after merging main): main's `angleWord` (Fanuc, Doosan DNM) writes degrees through `wa`, never the unit-aware length formatter - pinned by `program_units::rotary_angle_words_are_degrees_in_an_inch_program` (mutation: `w` in `angleWord` fails it with A1.4764 for A37.5); grblHAL and TinyG (new on main) take the unit from `postOptions.Units` and declare `programUnits = "mm inch"` - pinned by `program_units::grbl_family_posts_write_the_mm_program_in_inches`; the six inch `drill_peck` goldens re-recorded for #994 (G99 + return move).

Changelog: Program units are a document setting: every post writes the program in the document's mm/inch (G21/G20, 840D G710/G700), never the machine file's; grblHAL and TinyG follow it too; Carvera, Heidenhain and Fanuc Lathe refuse an inch document by name; older projects open on the unit they posted in; MCP `set_units`.

Commit type: `feat(post)!` (BREAKING CHANGE footer; under 0.x it bumps MINOR).

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(sim): judge an upright tool within a stated tilt tolerance
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/upright.rs`: one predicate, `is_upright`, with one named tolerance `UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD = 1e-9` rad (~5.7e-8 deg). A pose within it is judged exactly as a vertical move (the prismatic branch, bit for bit); above it, downward, sideways, zero or non-finite reads tilted (the enclosing reading).
- Every verify law that branched on the exact `camcraft_cl::is_vertical` now reads `is_upright`: reach (c) and its mid-turn sweep (c3), fixture bands/rapids (c2)/(d2), posed steel, mesh steel, solid law, posed contact, posed-rapid second reading, all-air verdict.
- `camcraft_cl::is_vertical` itself stays exact, so CL dumps, posted G-code and goldens do not move.
- Law (c) no longer reports the same `ShankHit` twice for one move when both band groups (shank and holder) convict with the same verdict.
- Why 1e-9 rad is safe: at that tilt a 1 m stack moves 1e-6 mm sideways and a 100 mm holder disc dips 1e-7 mm, four orders below a 0.01 mm gouge tolerance. #938's 1e-10 deg (1.7e-12 rad) is three orders inside; a commanded 0.001 deg is four orders outside. The reasoning and the options I dropped are in `docs/decisions/938-tilt-tolerance.md`.

## How tested
- New `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` (5 tests; 4 fail on upstream/main without the fix):
  - `a_wide_holder_reads_the_same_upright_and_at_a_rounding_error_of_tilt`: no pose, [0,0,1] and 1e-10 deg give the same clean verdict (before the fix, 1e-10 deg gave two false ShankHits).
  - `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_is_still_judged_tilted`: 1.01e-9 rad and 0.001 deg still convict.
  - `a_noise_tilt_keeps_the_upright_conviction_exactly`
  - `a_leaning_shank_and_holder_report_one_shank_hit_per_move`
  - `the_fixture_band_law_reads_noise_as_upright_and_a_real_tilt_as_tilted` (law c2)
- Unit test `verify::upright::tests::rounding_noise_is_upright_and_a_real_tilt_is_not`, covering both sides plus down, sideways, zero, NaN and inf.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (sim, motion and app suites from the gate map). Also `posed_fixture` and `stock_posed` pass, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
- One existing expectation changed: `tool_body_bands::a_raised_foot_over_a_fat_shank_is_judged_stricter_than_the_cylinder` had pinned the duplicate `[ShankHit{1,true}, ShankHit{1,true}]`. It now expects a single report. The conviction is the same. No goldens or snapshots moved.

## Not exercised
- Batch and release tiers were not run, so the heavy `--ignored` lanes did not run.
- `stock_sim` and the motion generators keep their exact upright tests (they shape geometry, not verdicts). I left them alone on purpose; see the decision file.

Changelog: The verifier treats a tool tilted by rounding noise (up to 1e-9 rad) as upright, so a holder wider than the cutter no longer raises a false collision on float noise, and a move reports a shank/holder hit once (#938)

Effort: high (no escalation)

`#[test]` count per file (before = after):

| file | from | to | tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| heidenhain_arc_centre | app | post | 2 |

`origin_approach` scans the motion generators' source for the seed pattern; its walk root is now `../motion/src` (a file-system path, no crate dependency). Caveat: a change that touches only `crates/motion/src` no longer selects it in quick (cl owns it now); batch and release still run it.

## xtask
Batch picks the moved suites up in their new crates (`--dry-run` shows post/sim/motion/cl step lists). Three quick-selection pins asserted the heidenhain suites under the app step; they now assert them under the post step. New pin `moved_suites_live_in_their_owner_crate_and_not_in_app`. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bumped to 19 (#967 has 18).

## Tested
- post: 8 moved suites pass (2/5/11/2/2/3/6/7); sim: boundary_walls 2, real_tip 3; motion: arcs 7; cl: origin_approach 5.

title: feat(post)!: Air coolant mode, machine default coolant, editor keeps coolant codes
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

From the Makera Z1 user report: an Air M7 added in the machine editor was "ignored on save", the Carvera post emitted M8 from the seeded Flood, and an operation could not ask for air.

- **Air coolant mode.** `CoolantMode::Air` ("Air" in the op page's Coolant picker, `PARAM Coolant air` in the stream, `"air"` in project files). `COOLANT_KINDS` (the mounted-machine editor's pick list) gains `Air`.
- **Every post that reads the ask handles Air.** Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Doosan DNM and Tormach Lathe resolve `air` from the machine's `Air` / `Air blast` entry, or refuse it by name ("operation X: the machine states no air coolant code ..."). Tormach Plasma already refuses every ask but Off. The Tormach mill post does not read the ask, so the engine's existing `coolantModes` refusal covers it.
- **`carvera.cps` posts the coolant the op asked for.** It used to take "first Flood, else first coded entry", which posted M8 when the seeded Flood was kept. It now declares `coolantModes`. Air takes the `Air` entry. Flood takes the `Flood` entry, failing one a shop's own coded name. A missing match is a named refusal, never a wrong M-code.
- **The machine's default coolant.** `CoolantMode::machine_default(coolants)` is Flood when the machine can post a flood ask, otherwise the first coded entry's mode. `CreateOperation` starts each new op on its setup's machine's default. On the shipped Carvera (Air M7 only), a new op is Air and posts M7 / M9.
- **The machine file editor keeps the coolant.** "Add coolant" takes the name and the M code together and refuses an empty code by name. Each coolant row has a "Remove <coolant>" button, the seeded Flood included. A codeless coolant is a draft refusal that blocks Save and Save As. `save()` now checks the refusals itself, as `save_as()` already did.
- **`tormach.cps` flood law aligned** with the generic posts. On an Air-only (or Mist-only) list it refuses a flood op by name instead of posting the first coded entry (M7).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/869-coolant-air.md`.

**Behaviour change (heads-up for the release notes):** an op saved before this change on an Air-only Carvera is still Flood (the old default). It now gets a named refusal telling the user to pick Air, where it used to post M7. New ops on that machine start on Air. A generic post on a machine whose only coolant is named "Air" refuses a Flood op the same way; before, it treated "Air" as the shop's own flood.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/coolant_air.rs` (new)
  - `an_air_only_carvera_starts_a_default_op_on_air_and_posts_m7_m9`: the shipped Carvera, a default op is Air, posts one M7 and one M9, no M8, no warnings.
  - `an_air_op_posts_the_air_code_not_the_seeded_flood`: Flood M8 + Air M7 on every generic post and the Carvera. The default op is Flood. An Air op posts M7 and never M8. `air_blast` reads as Air.
  - `an_ask_the_machine_lacks_is_refused_by_name`: Air on a flood/mist machine is refused by name on every post. Flood on the Air-only Carvera is refused by name. The Tormach mill post refuses an Air op, and a Flood op on an Air-only list never posts M7.
  - `the_machine_default_coolant_reads_the_coded_list`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_edit.rs::a_blank_mill_swaps_its_flood_for_air_m7_and_keeps_it_through_save_and_reload`: through the real shell, a name-only add is refused by name; Air M7 is added; the seeded Flood is removed; Save As writes the file, which reads back as `[Air M7]` with an Air default.
- Updated: `machine_edit::a_coolant_code_must_be_a_well_formed_m_word` (an empty code is now refused by name), `coolant_followups::machine_coolant_names_read_through_spelling_variants` (`COOLANT_KINDS` pin), and `carvera_post` (the two-tool pocket stream asks `PARAM Coolant air`).

Gate (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (post, app and ui suites; the ui lib holds the new editor test). The gate map does not pick the post-script suites for a `.cps` change, so these also ran green: 44 app suites touching coolant / posts / machines (`coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `coolant_air`, `carvera_post`, `carvera_machines`, `fanuc_post`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `lathe_post*`, `posting`, `conformance`, `smoothing`, `project_roundtrip`, `machine`, `machine_library`, the drilling / probe / mill2d suites, and others). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. First quick run failed on the new UI test: the old one-line "New coolant ... Add coolant" row was clipped in a narrow pane, so the click never landed. The add controls now sit on their own grid rows, and the removes are in a wrapped row.

**Goldens:** none moved. `nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc` is byte-identical: its stream now asks for air, and still posts M7 / M9.

## Not exercised

- The mounted-machine editor window (Setup pane) beyond `COOLANT_KINDS` now listing Air; its "add coolant" still adds a codeless Flood row there (it only applies to the mounted machine, never writes a file).
- Hand test on a real Carvera / Z1.
- No MCP tool sets an op's coolant today (not added by this PR: it adds no command; `EditOperationParams::with_coolant` predates it). Follow-up filed: #954 ("MCP: set an operation's coolant", P1, effort:medium).

Changelog: Coolant: an operation can ask for Air (M7 air blast), resolved from the machine's list or refused by name; a new op starts on its machine's default coolant (Air on the Carvera); the Carvera post posts the op's coolant instead of the first Flood; the machine file editor adds a coolant with its code, can remove the seeded Flood, and never saves a codeless coolant.

Commit type: `feat(post)!` (the BREAKING CHANGE footer covers the Air-only Carvera Flood refusal; under 0.x it bumps MINOR like any feat).

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(mcp): set_wcs_from_features places the WCS from role-tagged feature picks
body:
#706 has merged into upstream main; this PR is no longer stacked and targets `main` with only its own files. Main's `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs` already carries the `(Role::Z, Role::Y)` arm fix below (identical hunk, taken from main in the merge). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **New MCP tool `set_wcs_from_features`** (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_tools.rs`): picks are `[{model, id, role}]`, `role` one of `origin | x | y | z`, ids from `list_features`. It runs the GUI's own law `pick::align_roles` (#701) unchanged, turns the fit into a WCS placement exactly as the GUI's `CommandKind::SetWcs` does (`quat_from_euler` of the law's roll/pitch/yaw), and executes the existing undoable `SetWcsOrigin` - no new command kind, no frame maths of its own, one undo step. Picks go through the same id parse, model check and one-pick rule (#692) as every other MCP pick. Optional `setup` must name the active setup (`SetWcsOrigin` places the active setup's WCS; the GUI greys Apply on an inactive row the same way) - otherwise refused by name. The reply carries the placed origin/rotation/word plus the fitted `axes` and `angles_deg`.
- **Fix to the law, `(Z, Y)` role pair** (`crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs`): with a Z pick and a Y pick (no X), `align_roles` put the Z pick's axis in the Y slot and the Y pick in X - the arm was a copy of `(Y, X)`. A box with Z = its +X side face and Y = that side's top edge came out x = [0,1,0], y = [1,0,0], z = [0,0,-1]: a WCS lying on its back, posting turned moves. Now Z stays Z, Y is squared to it, X = Y x Z. Now on main via #706 (identical hunk); this PR no longer changes `roles.rs`.
- camcraft-mcp skill: tool row, shipped-gaps line, and a caveat that a `list_features` face row's `normal` is the canonical plane normal (#956). `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 33 -> 36 (#681 entry to be posted at merge: `PROCESS_VERSION 36` · PR #960 · camcraft-mcp skill gains the `set_wcs_from_features` row · forks: sync process files).
- `docs/decisions/937-mcp-wcs-from-features.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/mcp_wcs_features.rs` (gate map: app::mcp::wcs_tools, app::pick::roles):
- `set_wcs_from_features_lands_on_the_guis_frame_as_one_undo_step` - three pick sets (plain 3-2-1; Z face + Y edge + corner; Z face + X edge + a cylinder wall patch as origin) on a box and a 48-segment bore imported over MCP. For each, the placed origin and rotation equal **bit for bit** what `align_roles` plus the GUI's `quat_from_euler` conversion give on an identical in-process world; the frames are then spelled out (identity at the corner; Z on the side's normal, Y along the edge, X = Y x Z; the bore's fitted centre projected onto the top face). Undo/redo walk one step each. **Red on `d2663a3f` without the roles fix, green with it.**
- `bad_feature_picks_are_refused_by_name_and_place_nothing` - missing `picks`, empty and single pick, a role given twice, fewer than two axes, a vertex as an axis, an edge as the origin, parallel axes (top face Z + vertical edge X), a stale id, a bad role word, an unknown model, an extra pick key, an inactive `setup`, an unknown argument; the WCS stays unplaced.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green at `be055d7d` - app suites (31 binaries incl. `mcp_wcs_features`, `wcs_roles`, `mcp_setup`, `mcp_pick`) ok in 33 s, ui suites (lib + 10 binaries) ok in 124 s; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The live-GUI path (`--mcp-port`) - the tool runs on the same `Env`/History as every other tool, nothing GUI-specific.
- A UI test for the GUI row with a Z+Y pair - the fix is in the shared law; the GUI row calls the same function.
- No script verb: `set_wcs` has none either.

## Follow-ups

- #956 - `list_features` reports a face's canonical plane normal, not its outward side (an agent steered by `normal`/`facing` picks the wrong face).

Changelog: MCP `set_wcs_from_features` places the active setup's WCS from feature picks with origin/x/y/z roles, through the GUI's "Set WCS from features" law and the same undoable command; a Z pick with a Y pick now keeps Z on Z (it landed on Y) (#937)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #937

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
**None.** No committed golden states a rotary rate on a tilted feed. The lathe's C-axis goldens (`c_axis_unwind.nc`, `c_axis_helix.nc`) are byte-identical through the shared rule.

## Test fixture changed
`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

## Not exercised
- No Hub run or machine cut yet.
- G93 inverse time is not implemented (see the decision file).
- Under G43.4 the machine's linear axes also make a compensating move that depends on the pivot length. No machine file states that length, so the control's own per-axis clamp covers it. The post caps the tip at `feedRateMax`.

Found while working this: #950 (P0). doosan-dnm without TCP assumes A0 at program start and after a tool change, so an A0 section after an A30 section posts no A word. This PR does not fix that output. With a rated A, it now refuses such a feed by name.

Changelog: Posts cap the feed of a block that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rotary rate and linear feed (fanuc, doosan-dnm, fanuc-lathe through one shared rule), refusing by name when the starting angle is unknown (#885)

Fixes #885

title: feat(machine): refuse rigid tapping by name at the program gate; validate spindle.rigid_tapping
body:
## What changed

- **Program gate, every post.** The machine check (`machine::check_ops`, which every post path runs through `verification_report`) now refuses a path carrying tap cycles on a machine whose `.mch` states `spindle.rigid_tapping: false`. The message names the op, the cycle count and the machine: `Tap1: 1 tap cycle(s) need rigid tapping, which Tormach 770M cannot do - use a tapping head or thread milling`. Before this, only `tormach.cps` read `machine.rigidTapping`, so a 770M posted through Fanuc or Haas wrote a G84 with no warning. The cycle is never converted to another cycle. `tormach.cps` is unchanged and keeps its own refusal for the standalone script path. The gate is `judge::tap_gate` (`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs`).
- **Schema validated.** A `rigid_tapping` value that isn't `true`, `false` or `null` now refuses the file by name, at the reader (`parse_mch`: `spindle.rigid_tapping must be true or false, not "no"`) and in the Machines pane's validator (key `spindle.rigid_tapping`). Before, `"no"` read as unstated, which means "not limited".
- **Machines pane.** The Spindle group's "Rigid tapping" row now reads `yes`, `no - tap cycles are refused`, or `not stated - not limited`, instead of the raw `true`/`false`. The structural UI test was updated; no snapshot PNG changed.
- **Machine files.** No `.mch` changed. Every Tormach mill and router already stated the value (#170, #618, #620): `true` on the four MX mills, `false` on the R8 M/M+ mills, the PCNC series and the routers. A new test pins the whole set. The lathes are unstated, so behaviour there is unchanged, and #795 tracks them.
- **Docs.** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` and `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md` describe the key. The decision is in `docs/decisions/786-rigid-tapping.md`: explicit on the Tormach files, absent means "not limited". Default-false was considered and dropped because it would change every non-Tormach machine.

## How tested

Pinning tests (new `crates/app/tests/rigid_tapping.rs`):
- `a_tap_on_a_machine_that_cannot_rigid_tap_is_refused_by_name_whatever_the_post`: a tap job on the 770M through Tormach PathPilot, Fanuc and Haas, run through `posting::post_setup`. It is refused by name, no file is written, and the machine check names it. Fails with the gate line commented out (checked).
- `a_tap_posts_where_rigid_tapping_is_stated_or_unstated`: the 1100MX on PathPilot and the generic VMC on Fanuc still post G84, and the check stays silent.
- `rigid_tapping_must_be_a_boolean_or_the_file_is_refused_by_name`: both doors.
- `the_machines_sheet_states_rigid_tapping_in_words`
- `every_tormach_mill_and_router_file_states_rigid_tapping`
- UI: `egui_app::tests::machines_pane::the_sheet_states_rigid_tapping_in_words` (AccessKit labels).

Suites run on the final head (merged with v0.17.0), all green:
- camcraft-app: rigid_tapping 5, machine 33, machine_library 11, machine_edit 12, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 24, tormach_machines 6, tormach_post 10, tormach_routers 5, plasma_machine 6, carvera_machines 1. Earlier head, also green: fanuc_post 11, solid_law_goldens 1, heidenhain_block_form 4.
- camcraft-post: all suites.
- camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` + `structural`: 11.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The 770MX G84 golden and every other golden are byte-identical; no golden file is in the diff.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate (the coordinator runs it) and the batch and release tiers.
- A hand check of the Machines pane: the Rigid tapping row wording on a real window.
- The Tormach lathes, which are left unstated (#795).

title: feat(ui): two orientation dropdowns, one section everywhere
body:
## What changed

The setup orientation UI is two dropdowns, one section everywhere
(#771, stacked on #770):

- **Plane orientation** - Axes (#769, the default), Points (#555),
  Face (#330), Manual (the preset/angles picker), and the new
  **Cylinder angle**: one pick on a bore's or cylinder's curved wall
  names its axis from the wall's own facet normals (any two
  non-parallel wall normals cross exactly along it; every other
  normal is verified - a mixed patch is refused by name, never
  misread). The axis lands on a chosen world axis (+X/+Y/+Z), turned
  by an angle about it, the part turning about its bounds centre.
- **Orientation point** - the parts' bounds or the setup's stock
  (corner or centre), or a picked vertex. The WCS's rotation is kept:
  the frame comes from the plane side; each setup places its own WCS
  (`SetWcsOrigin::for_setup`), never the active one's.
- The section is ONE component (`setup_orient_pick::section`) mounted
  on the Setups overview AND each setup's Settings page - same
  dropdowns, same options, same look (the user's law). The old rows
  keep their own entry points and draw verbatim as the expanded
  content.

## How tested

title: feat(ops): one machining-frame seam - OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame
body:
## What changed

Phase 1 of #763: **`OpFrame`** — the one machining-frame seam in
`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` — composes the two existing frame
mechanisms (the setup's `part_alignment` from #326 and the op's 3+2
`Tilt` from M5.1 B) behind one door, and `collect_job` reads through it:

- `OpFrame::of(op)` built once per generation; material and heights
  resolve through it; the tilt frame comes from
  `OpFrame::checked_frame` — one construction site, the refusal keeping
  its exact words and its exact precedence (after the heights resolve,
  the job's error-order law).
- The contract is stated once in the module header: D / S / L frames,
  right-to-left composition `p_L = T(A(p_D))`, the CL wrapping back via
  `TiltedFrame::world_path` (identity clone without a tilt), and the
  furniture law (stock / WCS / fixtures live in S: never aligned, but
  read local by the tilt).
- Heights and bounds in L ship correct from day one
  (`aabb_local_of`, `height_z_local`): they resolve against FULLY
  TRANSFORMED geometry, never a `z − origin.z` shift of the S box —
  the shift is only correct while the tool axis is the world Z.

**No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.** The four
verified kinds, picks, area controls and tilt-in-aligned-setups keep
their refusals; the later phases lift them one by one, each with its
numeric pin.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` (8 tests) + the seam's inline
  unit tests (6): identity passthrough; zero-tilt index reproduces the
  prismatic path EXACTLY move-for-move (the identity-bits law); a
  tilted face runs in its own plane (every endpoint maps back into the
  L1-folded height band over the local silhouette, tool axis =
  hand-computed Rx(45)); 90-degree alignment turns the solid and its
  TopOfModel height (15, not 10); 180-degree alignment mirrors the
  facets by hand math; alignment × tilt composition pinned against
  hand-composed transforms; local heights/boxes read fully transformed
  geometry (and provably NOT the z-shift); picks stay refused by name
  while the door Phase 2 will read through is already aligned.
- Capability gates: unchanged by design; the tilted-move refusal keeps
  its existing verbatim pin in `tests/inverted_post.rs`.
- The four kinds' aligned generation keeps its pins in the #326 suites
  (`plane_align`, `axis_align`, `rest_across_setups`, …), run by the
  same gate.

## What was not exercised

- The L-frame height/AABB resolve methods are pinned by tests only —
  no production call site switches onto them until Phase 2+ lifts the
  matching refusals (deliberate: the seam lands behavior-identical).
- The boundary/region builders (`boundary_ctx`, `material_region`,
  `boundary_picks`) still build their own frames from `op.params.tilt()`
  — they move onto the seam in the later phases.

Changelog: feat: one machining-frame seam (OpFrame) composing part_alignment and TiltedFrame behind a single door; generation reads through it byte-identically (#763, PR)

title: feat(wcs): anchor the WCS on a picked circle's centre; tidy the WCS page
body:
## What changed

**Shared pick primitive** - `crates/app/src/pick/circle.rs` (next to the #692 pick graph): `circle_centre(world, &GeoSel)`, `circle_of_edge(graph, edge)`, `circle_of_run(features, run)` return a `Circle { centre, axis, radius, closed }` or a named `CircleRefusal` (`Straight`, `TooShort`, `NotCircular`, `NotAnEdge`, `Gone`). The edge pick resolves to its **run** (one straight stretch or one arc), so an arc of a filleted rim works too. The fit reuses `feature_arc::fit_arc` and its tolerances, and checks every vertex. A non-circular edge is refused, never guessed. The axis sign is canonical, so a hole in a top face reads +Z. The centre is in the active setup's view frame (#326), the frame the WCS is set in.

**Command + MCP** - `SetWcsAtCircleCentre` (`crates/app/src/commands/wcs_circle.rs`) resolves the circle when the command is created and wraps `SetWcsOrigin` at the centre: one undo step, and undo restores the previous origin. The MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre { edge: {model, id}, rotation? }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_circle.rs`) runs the same command and returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. The camcraft-mcp skill doc lists the tool. No MCP follow-up is needed.

**WCS page** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, split out of the 1894-line `pages.rs`):
- Three collapsible sections: *Origin and orientation*, *Quarter turns* and *Anchor on*.
- The six value fields sit in a two-column grid, label and field on one row, with the fields in one column.
- The quarter turns are two rows of three equal buttons ([X+ Y+ Z+] / [X- Y- Z-]), plus *Level* and *Set Origin* as two equal halves. Every row spans the pane's width.
- The anchor grid is a 3x3 compass of equal cells (up to 72 x 30), placed exactly and centred.
- *Anchor on* has a third choice, **Circle centre**. It shows a "Pick a circular edge" toggle and then the result, e.g. "Circle Ø 20.00 mm, centre (0.00, 0.00, 10.00)", or "Not anchored: <reason>". While the toggle is armed, a viewport click takes feature edges only, one run per click, and hover highlights what a click would take. A landed pick disarms the toggle. Choosing Circle centre disarms the box markers, and the other way round.
- The Bottom/Middle/Top radios are now a plain "Z level" row. Beside the 120 px label column they widened the section past a narrow pane.

**Plumbing** - `CommandKind::SetWcsCircle`, and a new `state_wcs.rs` that also takes over the existing `SetWcs` arm (`state.rs` shrinks). The viewport routes clicks through `wcs_pick.rs` (anchor markers + circle pick), which shortens `interact.rs`. `feature_click::ask` returns the circle ask while armed.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/circle_centre.rs` (new, 5 tests) uses a plate with a drilled 8 mm hole (32 chords), off-centre at (5, -3):
  - `a_drilled_hole_rim_gives_its_true_centre_axis_and_radius`: centre within 1e-6, Ø 8, axis +Z, through a real ray pick, and again with the part moved.
  - `a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name`.
  - `an_elliptical_rim_and_a_face_are_refused_never_guessed`: ellipse gives `NotCircular`, face gives `NotAnEdge`, stale id gives `Gone`.
  - `the_anchor_command_places_the_origin_and_undo_restores_the_previous_one`: undo, redo, and a refusal never builds a command.
  - `mcp_set_wcs_circle_centre_anchors_on_a_rim_and_refuses_a_straight_edge`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs` (structural, no pixels):
  - `the_page_has_three_sections_and_one_row_fields_in_one_column`
  - `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`
  - `the_anchor_points_are_a_centred_compass_of_equal_cells`
  - It also holds the three `turn_wcs` tests, moved verbatim from `pages.rs`. The test count is unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_circle_tests.rs`:
  - `a_rim_click_anchors_the_origin_on_its_centre_and_undo_restores_it`: combo, then the pick button, then a viewport click on a boss rim, then G54 at the centre. The page states the circle, and Undo restores (1, 2, 3).
  - `a_face_is_refused_by_name_and_lands_nothing`
- Gate (macOS, worktree target):
  - Ran green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `camcraft-app --lib`, the full `camcraft-ui` lib and integration suites (459 lib tests), and these app suites: circle_centre, feature_pick, feature_pick_wire, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, mcp_live, one_wcs, setup_wcs, commands_undo, wcs_align, wcs_view_pose, face_origin, vertex_pick, pick.
  - Not run: `cargo xtask gate quick` itself. Its dry run fell back to every crate, which is batch-sized.

## Not exercised

- Nobody has looked at the page in the real app (hand check below). No snapshot PNG changed. The release-lane `egui_shell_snapshot` was not run; the WCS page is not in that frame.
- A circle on a rotated or aligned setup is covered by the view-pose transform, and the app test covers a translated part. No rotated-setup test was added.

## Hand check

1. Open the WCS node and check the three sections. Each field should sit on one row with its label. Narrow the properties pane: the turn buttons should stretch evenly, and the compass should stay centred with equal cells.
2. Set *Anchor on: Circle centre*, then press *Pick a circular edge*. Hovering a hole rim or boss edge should highlight it. A click should move the WCS origin to the circle centre at the rim's height and show "Circle Ø … , centre (…)". Ctrl+Z should restore the previous origin.
3. With the pick armed, click a straight edge: the status line and the page should say it is straight, and the origin should stay put.
4. Switch back to Stock box: the compass and "Pick markers in viewport" should work as before.

Changelog: WCS page: anchor the origin on the centre of a picked circular edge (hole rim or boss), undoable and with MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre`; page laid out in sections with one-row fields, even quarter-turn buttons and a 3x3 anchor compass

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. Re-applying the same pick is a zero step and is refused as "already holds the part that way".
2. **One flow.** The top row now reads "Part alignment - each move starts from where the part sits now", and its tooltip describes the flow.
   - "Start from a preset" presets turn the part from where it sits, and so does the typed "Turn by", through the new `CommandKind::TurnPart` → `AlignPartToSetup::turn_by`.
   - "As modelled" is the one reset.
   - The pickers' Apply tooltips say a move starts from the current pose and is one undo step.
3. **Readable status.** It now reads "1 face selected", "2 points selected" or "1 edge selected" (`pick_words`).
   - Points show where they are: "Point 2: on 'part' (x, y, z) mm".
   - Internal ids ("Face 0xccc7c…") never show; app refusals on the page are stripped of " 0x…".
4. **Picks you can see.** `align_pick_viz::paint`:
   - picked faces are filled with the pick violet (alpha 96);
   - picked points are 6 px filled discs;
   - picked edges are 4 px strokes.

**Splits, so no large file grows:**
- `commands/align_stock.rs` comes out of `setup_align.rs` (422 → 298 lines).
- `state_align.rs` comes out of `state.rs` (4116 → 4062 lines).
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/738-align-flow.md`.

## Pinned by
- `align_compose` (new, 3 tests):
  - axes then face;
  - face then three points;
  - turn-by after a lay, for both pivots, plus the zero and NaN refusals.

  Each checks that the second move composes on the first, and that undo, undo and redo step back exactly.
- `setup_align_tests::a_preset_after_a_face_lay_composes_and_as_modelled_is_the_one_reset` (real clicks, Ctrl+Z).
- `setup_plane_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_face_and_never_shows_an_id` and `setup_points_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_points_and_never_shows_an_id`.
- `plane_face_pick::picked_faces_fill_points_are_discs_and_edges_are_bold` (paint assertions on the rendered shell).
- `pick_words` unit tests.

## Tested
- **app suites:** all green. lib 107, `align_compose` 3, `plane_align` 9, `plane_align_edges` 5, `points_align` 8, `axis_align` 10, `setup_align` 9, `turn_pivot` 5, `commands_undo` 32, `project_roundtrip` 71, `wcs_align` 5, `mcp_setup` 6, `fixture_locate` 11, `winding_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_relative` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `fixture_locate_stock` 3, `wcs_view_pose` 3.
- **ui suites:** all green, lib 447.
- **clippy `-D warnings`:** ui lib+tests and the app lib are clean.

## Not exercised / for the hand check
- The look of the fill, discs and bold edges on a real part, including a tilted face.
- How the new wording reads in the narrow properties pane.
- Pressing "Turn by" Apply twice turns the part twice; this is intended.
- **Behaviour change:** MCP `lay_part_on_points` / `lay_part_on_plane` now also compose, since they share the command.

**Stays a draft until the maintainer or user hand-checks it** (binary: `~/camcraft-builds/camcraft-ui-738`).

title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body: Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0. ## What changed - **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before. - **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name: - a number outside 1-9999; - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`. Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time. - **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves. - **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool. - **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md. - **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead. - **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set. **Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals. - **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `()`. - **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set. - **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment. - **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `% G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name. - **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N__MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment. Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`. ## How tested - **New `program_info` tests (9):** - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set; - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone; - post-time refusals; - command validation, undo and redo; - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`); - per-op numbering; - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001; - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused. - **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal). - **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.** ## Not exercised A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set. Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258) Refs #258 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAgjpiZbXSvmXLvdmL --- ## Update: merged upstream/main (head 1676ad9e) - **Project file is now v61, not v59/v60.** #981 (#902, the unit law) took v60 first. So #258's `program` key gets its own step: `PROJECT_VERSION` 61, and a v60 -> v61 migration where v60 and older files load with nothing set. The reason for the step is unchanged: an older build would drop the key and post O0001. - **Inch programs:** #564's header logic and #981/#1126's unit handling are both kept. A new test, `program_info::a_stated_identity_posts_the_same_header_in_an_inch_program`, checks that Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas, Tormach and SINUMERIK write the same O-word / name / header comment in an inch program, followed by G20 (G700), never G21. - **Goldens:** none changed. Changelog (supersedes the line above): The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v61 (#258)

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
**Replaces #432** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except tests that already fail on main:
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415);
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests; red on main, fixed by PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft)
- GUI check of the new Passes-tab rows.
- **Posted G-code for non-default plans** (flank, constant area, allowance, spring passes) is new. It needs a lathe simulator or machine run before ready. Default plans post exactly as before.

Changelog: Threading op: infeed method (radial / modified flank / alternating), decreasing-depth schedule, minimum depth, finish allowance and spring passes (#416)

Fixes #416

Rendered headless (egui_kittest `Harness::render()` on lavapipe) through the real `pages::properties` code: a lathe, bar stock, the TD-1732-60 threading insert and one Threading op, Passes tab open. After: infeed method Flank (29.5°), Constant area schedule, minimum depth 0.05 mm, finish allowance 0.03 mm, 1 spring pass.
